# Fix log

Root cause, fix, and verification for non-trivial defects — the record version control cannot carry:
a diff shows what changed and never why the old behaviour was wrong. Newest first. The knowledge
service indexes this file per entry, so a sibling can ask "has anyone hit this" without opening the
repository.

## 2026-10-24 - A session's own git read a committed file past 260 characters in its tree as deleted (TREELONG1)

- **Symptom:** seen on the install's work workspace. A file at 242 characters in a repository's checkout is at 265 in a session's
  tree, which sits deeper under the trees home. The session's `git status` showed it changed and its `diff` showed it deleted,
  though the file on disk was the committed one; an agent's `git add -A` could have committed the deletion.
- **Root cause:** Daoris's own git says `-c core.longpaths=true` on every call (`WorkingTree.GitStart`, D109), but that is a
  command-line word of Daoris's own git alone. The environment a session's start is handed (`Spawning.Shell`) scoped only the author
  (`GitAuthor.Hand`) and the remote helper (`GitWiring.Hand`), so a session's git ran without long paths. Without it Git for Windows
  cannot open a path past 260 characters: under its own system default `core.fscache` the file reads as deleted, and without that it
  says "Filename too long" and lists nothing.
- **Fix:** `Spawning.Shell` scopes `core.longpaths=true` into every session's git environment beside the author's, through
  `GitRouting.Scope` (`GitLongPaths.Hand`). `GitLongPaths.NeededAsync` reads `git config --show-scope --get-all core.longpaths` in the
  start's root and leaves the setting out where a scope of the person's names it, either way; the command scope there is Daoris's own
  `-c`, and is not the person's. The setting is also left out where the inherited command scope already names it.
- **Verification:** `GitLongPathsProcessTests.A_sessions_git_reads_a_tree_past_260_characters_clean` commits a file at about 240
  characters, adds a session's tree where it passes 260, and runs `git status` there through the stub adapter's prepared start and
  through a git handed nothing, with the person's system and global configuration kept out and `core.fscache` on. With the hand
  disabled it failed: the handed status read ` D` for the committed file. With it, the handed status is clean, and the bare git still
  reads the file as deleted. `A_person_whose_configuration_says_it_is_handed_nothing` holds the person's `core.longpaths=false`.
  `GitLongPathsProcessTests` passed with `process.runsettings` (2 of 2); `GitLongPathsTests` and the fast classes that build a
  session's start passed (387 of 387).

## 2026-10-24 - The router's union merge left a changed row twice, the older copy coming back (ROUTERMERGE1)

- **Symptom:** on 2026-10-24 six landings left a design's or a reads file's row in `docs/README.md` twice, an older copy
  coming back each time, with no conflict reported; only `doc-duplicates` caught them.
- **Root cause:** `.gitattributes` merged the router by union, the driver suited to the append-only records. The router's rows
  change in place, and union keeps both versions of a line two branches changed: a branch that changed a row `main` also
  changed, or that still carried a row `main` had since replaced next to a change of its own, left both rows. Replayed over the
  router's last 138 two-parent merges, 41 left a key more times than `main`'s side had it.
- **Fix:** `tools/merge-rows.mjs`, a merge driver declared for `docs/README.md` (`merge=rows`), merges each table's rows by their
  first cell three ways and the prose around them as text; a row both sides changed differently is a marked conflict. The root
  `npm ci` configures it in the clone's own git config (`prepare` runs `--install`). The append-only records keep union.
- **Verification:** `tools/merge-rows.test.mjs` (16 cases, a base and two sides for each rule; the first 15 written before the
  driver, 12 of them seen failing against a stub that kept ours), including a scratch repository under `_fixtures/` whose two branches each edited one of two neighbouring rows,
  merged by git through the driver, each row once. The same replay through the driver: no clean merge added a duplicate a side
  did not already carry; 25 stop as marked conflicts instead.
## 2026-10-24 - A word kept while a limit's move was under way reached neither part (LIMITWORD1)

- **Symptom:** seen on the install. A chat met its account's limit at 09:19:27 UTC; a word was kept on that record at 09:20:02; at
  09:20:11 Daoris went on in a new part on another account, and the brief it handed carried the history but not that word, which no
  part ever read.
- **Root cause:** the ended-record move (`LimitMove.MoveEndedAsync`) read the old record's waiting words once, before it wrote its box,
  and named only those in the box's `said`; `ComposeAsync` handed only the box's words, filtered from that early read. Opening the new
  part takes seconds, and until its record exists a word for the conversation is kept on the old record (`WordsNever.ContinuedIn`
  sends it to the new part only once that record continues the old). A word kept in that gap was in neither the box nor the new
  part's record, so the move never carried it and the delivery never took it off.
- **Fix:** at the go-on, once the new part's record exists, the move reads the old record again and adds every person's word the box
  does not yet name to it, after its own in the record's order (`LimitMove.Carried`), writes the box, and composes the message from
  that read. The come-up's replay of a box (`TakeUpBoxesAsync`) does the same, for a shell that ended between the new part's open and
  that box write. A word kept after the go-on goes to the new part by the say door, as before; one already in the box is not added
  again, so none is sent twice.
- **Verification:** `LimitWaitsProcessTests.A_word_kept_between_the_moves_box_and_its_go_on_reaches_the_new_part_once` keeps a word
  on the old record as the new part's record opens, the box already written. Before the fix it failed: the new part's prompt held the
  refused turn and the boxed word but not the new one, and the word stayed on the old record. After the fix it passes: the word is
  handed once, after the boxed word; the old part never hears it; it leaves the old record as taken by the new part; the box is gone.
  `LimitWaitsProcessTests` passed with `process.runsettings` (12 of 12), and the driver's fast half passed 14,411 of 14,412. Its one failure,
  `MachineFactsTests.A_judge_that_never_answers_holds_no_other_subject_and_is_never_judged_twice_at_once`, is outside this change, and
  its class passed alone (13 of 13).

## 2026-10-24 - A conversation continuing a quest's worker read its line's origin, not its quest's run (CHATFLOW1a, Codex's finding 6)

- **Symptom:** found by Codex's read of the accepted chat-flow design, not seen on the install. A quest an ask sent, its worker gone on
  as a conversation, read every run of the ask in its *Workflow* view; a quest whose entry inherited its publisher's session origin from
  another tree, its worker gone on, read `chat-own-tree`; and a conversation that did read its quest's run was none of that run's work
  records, so its tree, landings and acceptances were left out (the worker's were shown).
- **Root cause:** row a classified a record by its stored origin, which groups work by line and does not name the work: the service
  gives an ask-sent quest's worker the ask's origin and a published quest its publisher's (`Sessions/SessionEntries.cs:97`, `:108-112`).
  The run's records were then selected by `session.Quest` alone, which a conversation keeps null.
- **Fix:** `WorkflowRunReader.WorkOf` resolves the quest whose workflow governs a record (its own; else the nearest record its `From`
  links reach that names or took one; else a quest its line took in its tree; else a stored quest origin), `ChainsOf` reads it before an
  origin, and `RunAsync` selects its work records by it (`Workflows/WorkflowRun.Read.cs`). The doors' use of it is CHATFLOW1i's.
- **Verification:** two `WorkflowRunTests` cases, seen failing first (the ask's two chains where one was expected; the worker's id
  where the conversation's was), then green with the `WorkflowRunTests`, `WorkflowPortsTests`, `WorkflowRunCommandTests`,
  `WorkflowRunSaidTwinTests` and `TraceTests` classes (288), the driver's fast half (14,411) and `DriverModuleWorkflowRunTests` (17).

## 2026-10-24 - A test's stand-in listened on a port Node's fetch refuses (FLAKE1)

- **Symptom:** in `npm run verify`, `tools/rehearsal-kit.test.mjs`'s *a set-up step's stub says what it showed through its
  connector and closes done* failed with *the quest door at http://127.0.0.1:2049 did not answer take: fetch failed: bad port*;
  it passed twice alone.
- **Root cause:** the stand-in listened on port 0, and the system hands out any free port. The WHATWG Fetch standard refuses a
  list of ports as bad (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#port-blocking), 2049 among them, and Node's fetch follows it: the request
  never left the process. Six test files listened this way for a fetch or a browser to reach.
- **Fix:** `tools/listen-port.mjs`'s `listenFetchable` listens on port 0 and again while the port is on the standard's list
  (`BAD_PORTS`, undici's own list, which Node's fetch runs), and answers the server's url; a listen that fails is the caller's
  error. `tools/listen-port.d.mts` types it for the CLI's tests. The stand-ins of `tools/rehearsal-kit.test.mjs`,
  `tools/ux-count.test.mjs`, `src/Daoris.Cli/tool-test/setup-kit.test.ts` and `src/Daoris.Cli/test/service/`'s
  `brainstorm`, `exit` and `running` tests listen through it. The two .NET tests whose stand-in login listens on port 0
  (`CodexAccountProcessTests`, `SignInPhasesTests`) reach it with .NET's `HttpClient`, which refuses no port, and are left.
- **Verification:** `tools/listen-port.test.mjs` (4, in `verify`): every listed port is one Node's fetch refuses as a bad port,
  and a server whose first listen is handed a blocked port (injected, so every run sees it) is listened again on one fetch
  reaches, seen failing first against a helper that listened once (10080 kept). Then green: the rehearsal kit's, ux-count's and
  the helper's tests (61), `setup-kit.test.ts` (33), the three service tests with `doc-duplicates` and `dogfood` (70), the CLI's
  typecheck, `tools/test-map.mjs check` and `LoopbackListensTests` (2).

## 2026-10-24 - A terminal's attachments were bound by their paths, not their bytes (CONFIRMWAIT1a-i, Codex's finding 5)

- **Symptom:** none seen; Codex's read of the confirm-wait design found it in 1a-i on main, which no installed build carries.
  `SESSION_INPUT` sent by the verb with files (`said`, `paths`) could be confirmed hours later after a file was replaced at the
  same path. The session was then handed the new bytes, not what the asker attached.
- **Root cause:** the route's grounds were the session and its question alone (`PipeTargetRows.cs`). The handler reads `paths`
  only once the press runs (`ConversationRoutes.cs`, `SessionsCommand`), so the payload the record keeps held the reference and
  not the content.
- **Fix:** an `attachments` ground for that form: each path as given, and a rooted file's SHA-256 (`LoopGrounds`), kept in the record
  like any other ground (the design §15.1 item 5).
- **Verification:** `PipeGroundsBindingTests.A_terminal_s_attachment_replaced_at_its_path_moves_its_press` and
  `LoopGroundsTests.A_terminal_s_attachments_are_read_by_their_bytes`, each failing before the change.

## 2026-10-24 - A repository ground was the name's presence, not what it resolved to (CONFIRMWAIT1a-i, Codex's finding 4)

- **Symptom:** none seen (1a-i is in no installed build). A repository unregistered and registered again at another checkout under
  the same name kept its `repository` ground, and a waiting press such as a hand-off then ran against the other checkout.
- **Root cause:** `IPipeGroundWorld.RegisteredAsync` answered a boolean, so the ground compared `registered` with `registered`.
- **Fix:** `RegistrationAsync` answers the rows a name resolves to, each repository, workspace, adoption and full root, and the
  ground compares that. The reason now reads *no longer registered on this machine as it was*, en and zh (the design §15.1 item 4).
- **Verification:** `PipeGroundsBindingTests.A_name_registered_again_elsewhere_moves_its_repository_ground`, failing before the
  change; `PipeConfirmTests`' stale-ground cases still green.

## 2026-10-24 - An old Resume could release a newer pause (CONFIRMWAIT1a-i, Codex's finding 3)

- **Symptom:** none seen (1a-i is in no installed build). A `WORK_RESUME` asked while a pause stood, then the pause removed and made
  again, confirmed later, released the newer pause and its stops.
- **Root cause:** `WORK_PAUSE` and `WORK_RESUME` were grounded on the ask's or the quest's state alone. A pause is a file, never a
  state (`WorkPausing`), and the ask stays open throughout.
- **Fix:** both read `WORK_PLAN`. Resume binds the pause's `at` and each stop. Pause binds each quest's status and pause act, each
  session's state, and whether a pause stands (the design §15.1 item 3).
- **Verification:** `PipeGroundsBindingTests.An_old_Resume_does_not_release_a_newer_pause` and `A_Pause_binds_the_work_it_stops`,
  each failing before the change.

## 2026-10-24 - A discarded tree named by its path bound no commits (CONFIRMWAIT1a-i, Codex's finding 2)

- **Symptom:** none seen (1a-i is in no installed build). `DISCARD_SESSION_TREE` by `path` with `force`, asked on a clean tree,
  passed its Confirm after new commits landed in the tree, and removed them. Staged bytes could also change under an unchanged
  working file.
- **Root cause:** the head was read by `id` alone (`BranchGround.HeadOf("id")`), and the forced ground fingerprinted the uncommitted
  paths' working bytes, which were empty for a clean tree before and after.
- **Fix:** a `tree` ground for both forms, resolved as the handler resolves the tree: its head, its index's staged entries
  (`WorkingTree.StagedAsync`, `git diff --cached --raw --no-abbrev`), and with `force` each uncommitted path's bytes (the design
  §15.1 item 2).
- **Verification:** `LoopGroundsGitTests.A_tree_named_by_its_path_is_bound_by_its_head_and_its_index` over a real repository, and
  `PipeGroundsBindingTests.A_discard_binds_the_tree_it_removes_by_id_or_path`, each failing before the change.

## 2026-10-24 - Plan grounds bound counts and short ids, not commits (CONFIRMWAIT1a-i, Codex's finding 1)

- **Symptom:** none seen (1a-i is in no installed build). A branch rewritten to different commits of the same count, its short id
  unchanged, passed a sweep's, a sync's, a hand-off's or a landing's Confirm. An id-only hand-off named no branch for its `branch`
  ground at all.
- **Root cause:** the plan reads answer eight-character ids (`TreesRoutes.cs`, `EntriesRoutes.cs`, `LinesRoutes.cs`) and counts with
  no tip. The projections took what the answers carried, which D156's 1a-i note said but did not bind.
- **Fix:** a plan ground whose rows name branches also binds each branch's full tip, read by one `git for-each-ref` per checkout or
  tree (`ReadGround.Tips`, `WorkingTree.TipsAsync`): the landing's tree head and target, each entry's parts and target, the hand-off's
  resolved branch, the sweep's rows, and the sync's lines here and at origin, rebases and deletes (the design §15.1 item 1).
- **Verification:** `PipeGroundsBindingTests.A_branch_rewritten_to_as_many_commits_moves_its_plan`, seven cases, each failing before
  the change; `LoopGroundsGitTests.Every_branch_s_full_tip_is_read_at_once`.

## 2026-10-24 - The queue's runner formed a candidate from the queue as it stood before its hold (FLAKE1)

- **Symptom:** the tool-test `merge-queue.test.ts`, *a red candidate of two*, now and then found its first red run's members
  `['bad']` where `['good', 'bad']` was expected: in the CI on `ffcf42926`, and alone on this machine once in seven runs.
- **Root cause:** the records were true; the candidate was wrong. The failing run's `local/scope-runs.jsonl` held a green run of
  `good` alone, promoted, then a red run of `bad` alone on it. `queueStep` reads the queue once at its top, and its `none` action
  formed the next candidate from that read's `queued`. The test's hold (`MERGE_BRANCH_QUEUE_HOLD`) is looked at after the read and
  a git call: a step that read `[good]` before `bad` was queued, then found the hold lifted, formed `good` alone from the stale
  read, and `bad` went next on its own. Beyond the test the same read formed a request dropped (`--drop-batch`) in that moment all the
  same, and one dropped and queued again at a new tip at its old tip, the new one left queued beside it.
- **Fix:** the members are taken from the queue under its lock, in the same write that removes them from `queued`
  (`tools/merge-branch.mjs`, `queueStep`'s `none` action); a queue emptied meanwhile forms nothing. The test's pick of the first
  red run stays: it is the candidate's own run once the candidate is right, and the case still proves that `bad` never reaches
  main, is handed back pinned at member 2, and that `good` is promoted on its own green.
- **Verification:** the case run alone 30 times in a row, 30 green (it failed on the seventh run before the fix); the whole
  `merge-queue.test.ts` file 57 of 57; `npm run tooltests` in `src/Daoris.Cli` 375 of 375; `test/doc-duplicates.test.ts` and
  `test/dogfood.test.ts` 48 of 48.
## 2026-10-24 - A provider's 529 struck and carried on a driven session, or parked it on the person (AGENTERRORS1a)

- **Symptom:** two driven sessions on `claude-code-acp` met `API Error: 529 Overloaded` on the morning of 2026-10-24 (the
  agent-errors design §0). In the first, the prompt's JSON-RPC error ended the record `failed`, `ended.turn-failed-taken`, a strike,
  and the next look carried it on briefed in a new session, leaving its 219,284-token conversation behind. In the second, a word the
  person added mid-turn was refused with the error, the turn read as clean, and the run parked on the person, who went on by hand 33
  minutes later in the same conversation.
- **Root cause:** nothing in the driver read a failure's kind. The wire carried `data.errorKind: "overloaded"`, which
  `AcpRefusal.ErrorKind` kept and the conclusion dropped (`Loop/Driver.cs`, the capture's catch took `error.Message` alone); no
  table named a 529, an overload or a 5xx, so the only end a provider's outage could reach was a failed run's, a strike and a
  briefed carry-on, or, refused on a mid-turn word, no end at all.
- **Fix:** D210's row 1a. One reader at the agent interface (`AgentErrors.Read`, `Agents/Errors/AgentErrors.cs`) reads a door's
  failure as limit, access, transient or fatal from the adapter's `ErrorWords` and its owner's; a driven session's protocol door is
  handed a `TransientRetry` (`Agents/Acp/TransientRetry.cs`, `Loop/TransientRetries.cs`), and a transient failure is tried again
  inside `AcpSession.RunAsync` on the same session after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 minutes, never a word on the wire twice; past the bound
  the record ends `ended.transient`, no strike and no cool-off, and the planner holds its quest for the person's word. The second
  shape, a mid-turn word's refusal, is row 1a2's, and until it lands that end is unchanged.
- **Verification:** `TransientRetryTickTests` on real ticks with the driver's retry clock held: shape 1's stand-in failing twice then
  working goes on in one record and one conversation, seen red with the retry un-handed (the tick ended at once, today's end); one
  that keeps failing ends `ended.transient` after five tries and 31 minutes, its quest held across looks until the person's word
  resumes the same conversation. `AcpTransientTests` (the episode on a moved clock), `AgentErrorsTests` (the tables both ways),
  `SessionWatchTests` (the wait never quiet, seen red without its hook) and the page's rendered conversation.

## 2026-10-25 - STEWARDROLE1a-i reached main with two zh sentences the glossary refuses

- **Symptom:** the next landing's `npm run verify` failed `src/locales/names.test.ts`, *say in sentences only what the audit found to be
  another thing's word*, on `projects.supervisor.refused.holder-harness:zh` and `projects.supervisor.refused.scope:zh`, both added by
  STEWARDROLE1a-i, which was already on main.
- **Root cause:** the two sentences used words the glossary lists to avoid: 渠道 (the *channel*'s, whose word is 频道) for the maker's
  release channel, and 这台机器 where *this machine* is 本机. STEWARDROLE1a-i's own `verify` had failed twice at its landing, on this test
  and on a rehearsal-kit stub handed a port `fetch` refuses; the steward read the first failure, re-ran it green as a flake, and
  committed without reading the second.
- **Fix:** 用其厂商自己的方式安装 (the agents page's own wording for a maker's install) and 本机; the Web README's i18n row says what the
  test refuses. The steward reads every failing line of a `verify` before calling any of it a flake.
- **Verification:** the locale tests 104 of 104, `i18n:check` agreeing on 6,943 keys, `npm run verify` passed, in CONFIRMWAIT1a-ii's
  landing (`888d3bdcb`).

## 2026-10-24 - The wiring census read the CLI tests' scratch as a source, and two test classes were split by hand

- **Symptom:** the CI on `ffcf42926` failed `driver` on `SystemWiringTests.Every_variable_the_sources_name_is_on_the_list_shown_or_set_aside_with_its_reason`,
  naming `DAORIS_STUB_QUEUEING`, which no source under `src/` spells; it passed in the checkout, alone and in the fast half. The same
  CI failed `cli` on PART1's partials check: `PipeStandingTests` and `StandingConfirmationTests` were each declared `partial` in two
  hand-written files (SUPERVISOR1a-ii's `.Role.cs` and `.Appointments.cs`).
- **Root cause:** the census walks every file under `src/` and filters by path (`WiringVariables.Searched`), skipping `fixtures` but
  not `_fixtures`. The CLI's tests keep their scratch at `src/Daoris.Cli/_fixtures/` (`test/_fixture.ts:9`), and the deployment test
  writes the rehearsal kit's stub agent there (`deployment-rehearsal.test.ts:576`), whose text names the stub's switch. CI runs the
  `cli` and `driver` gates side by side in one gate tree, so the census read the stub while it stood. The merge tool's quick gates
  do not run the partials check, so the split classes reached main unseen.
- **Fix:** `Searched` skips `_fixtures` beside `fixtures`, held by `The_search_reads_code_and_never_a_tests_scratch`; each split class
  is one file again, the second file's body folded into the first, its summary kept as comments.
- **Verification:** `SystemWiringTests` 31 of 31, the two folded classes 59 of 59, `node tools/partials.mjs` clean; the next full CI.
  The same CI's `tool-tests` failure, the merge queue's red-candidate case, failed once more alone and then passed: FLAKE1's.
- **The next CI (`de3febc9e`) found two more.** The search's new case named `_fixtures` in `SystemWiringTests`, which deletes scratch of
  its own, so `GitSeedTests`' census read it as a test deleting its scratch by itself: the case is its own class, `WiringSearchTests`.
  And HOOKMERGE1's hook check ran `git diff` without `--no-optional-locks` (`TreeLands.cs:329`), which `verify`'s optional-locks check
  refuses and the merge tool's quick gates do not run. `npm run verify` passes, and the touched classes 60 of 60.

## 2026-10-24 - The trees read made more git starts when the line moved on than at its first read (MAINRED1)

- **Symptom:** the CI on `16769207d` failed `driver-process-git`: `HelpTreesReadTests`' 145-tree proof made 1616 git starts once the
  line moved on, where the first read made 1409. The test's rule is that the moved-on read makes fewer. It failed the same way alone.
- **Root cause:** REVIEWLANDED1's fourth form of the content proof (`ReplayHolds.ReadAsync`) asks the landing's own per-commit reading
  (`LineHolds.JudgeAsync`) of every tree with commits once the line has a commit since the branch left it. That reading walks the
  branch commit after commit by content (`BranchJudging.CutByContentAsync`, a content proof each), about fourteen starts a tree. The
  fixture's 49 trees with commits each paid that, though none of their commits is on the line.
- **Fix:** the form first reads, in one log, which commits the line holds by patch (`LineHolds.ReadBeyondAsync`), and the line's
  files since the branch left it (`LineHolds.MayHoldByContent`, the gate *Bring up to date*'s look already uses). Where no commit is
  held by patch and the walk could find none, the line holds none of the branch's commits: no replay, and nothing lacked that a
  landing counts otherwise. That costs two starts, and the walk is not asked.
- **Verify:** `HelpTreesReadTests` 4 of 4, the moved-on read 1273 starts where the first made 1409 (1616 before the fix, on the
  same machine). With `git.process.runsettings`, `HelpTreesReadTests` and `ReviewLandedTests` passed 8 of 8, and the covering classes
  69 of 69 (`SquashSeenTests`, `EndJudgementGitTests`, `ContentHeldTests`, `ContentLandingTests`, `ContentOfferTests`,
  `ContentProofLossTests`, `SessionTreeWorkTests`, `LandGitCountTests`, `BranchTidyingProcessTests`). The driver's fast half passed
  14316 of 14316, `ContentHoldWordsTests` among them. Detail: D102's MAINRED1 note.

## 2026-10-24 - Three tidy tests met a machine log file the calendar had aged (MAINRED1)

- **Symptom:** the CI on `16769207d` failed `driver-process-git`: in `BranchTidyingFolderTests`,
  `A_tree_whose_paths_pass_260_characters_is_moved_aside_and_purged` and
  `The_purge_deletes_a_folder_left_untouched_and_keeps_one_written_after_its_move` each got a second tidy line, `tidy  removed 1
  file(s) of the machine log older than 30 days`. KEEPSIZE1a's run saw the same two failures. The quest also named
  `A_tree_reached_through_a_link_under_the_trees_home_stays`; it passed here alone and in the class, both before and after the fix.
- **Root cause:** a date bomb. `BranchTidyingFixture.Log()` wrote the home's machine log on a fixed clock, 2026-10-09, while the
  looks read the real clock, the purge's fifteen days ahead. The look's daily log prune (KEEP1d, `BranchTidying.KeepLogs`) keeps
  thirty days, so from 2026-10-24 a look fifteen days ahead found the fixture's own file past its days, removed it and said so.
- **Fix:** the fixture's log writes on the real clock, so its file is today's and no look in these tests (at most fifteen days
  ahead) finds it past thirty days. Nothing the tests assert about the folders changed. `BranchTidyingTests` keeps its fixed
  clock: it never runs a look, only `Said`, so no prune reads its file.
- **Verify:** `BranchTidyingFolderTests` 13 of 13 with `git.process.runsettings`, where the two failed before the fix, and
  `BranchTidyingProcessTests`, which shares the fixture, in the covering run of the replay fix above. `BranchTidyingLandingTests`
  and `BranchTidyingWatchTests` were not run.
## 2026-10-24 - A merge its repository's commit-msg hook refused read as git refusing the merge (HOOKMERGE1)

- **Symptom:** a sibling repository reported (quest `#a2a221f5e2c3`) that accepting a session's branch always failed at the merge,
  with no conflict and a fast-forward possible. Its commit-msg hook scans each message for private names, one of which matches
  `daoris`, so the merge message `Merge branch 'daoris/s-…'` was blocked. The landing said only `git would not merge …` and git's
  first line, so the hook's own output was the only place the cause showed.
- **Root cause:** `TreeLands.MergeAsync` read every failed `git merge --no-ff` as git refusing the merge and quoted the first line of
  its stderr. A merge's commit runs the repository's `pre-merge-commit` and `commit-msg` hooks. When one refuses, git leaves the
  merge staged with `MERGE_HEAD` standing and nothing unmerged, and says *Not committing merge*. The landing aborted that state
  without reading it.
- **Fix:** before the abort, the merge reads git's state (`MERGE_HEAD` and no unmerged paths), not its words, which may be
  localised. A hook's refusal now says that the repository's own hook refused the merge commit and nothing conflicted, quotes the
  hook's output (up to 600 characters, without git's closing line), and says Daoris does not skip a repository's hooks. The person
  changes what the hook refuses, or merges by hand. The merge stays `--no-ff` with the branch in its message, and no `--no-verify`
  is passed: a fast-forward would also avoid the hook, but it would give up the one merge commit a person can read and
  revert as a unit, which the merge door makes on purpose.
- **Verify:** `TreeMergeTests` 9 of 9 by filter, with
  `A_merge_its_repositorys_hook_refuses_says_the_hook_and_its_words` new: a real repository whose `core.hooksPath` holds a
  commit-msg hook that refuses merge messages, the hook's words in the sentence, the checkout's head and status as found.

## 2026-10-24 - The set-aside folders at the trees entry's old place were never purged or counted (KEEPSIZE1a)

- **Symptom:** on the install, KEEPSIZE1's measurement found 164 set-aside folders (76.7 GB) under `data/trees/.tidied`, the oldest
  set aside on 10-15, past no purge. `trees list` named the 77 folders at the new place and none at the old; the *Disk space* card
  counted the old ones under *Everything else*, where 3.5 million files stopped its walk short. The steward removed them by hand.
- **Root cause:** D172's layout gave the trees entry two places, and TREEPLACE1 taught the trees' readers both
  (`TreeContext.TreesRoots`). The set-aside folders kept one root, `TreeSetAside.SetAsideRoot`, `.tidied` under `TreesRoot`, which
  `DaorisHome.Entry` answers with the new place once it holds anything. So the purge, the slim, the press, the floor, the look's
  pass, the trees' list and the card all read the new place's `.tidied` alone, and the folders set aside before the move were out of
  every rule's reach.
- **Fix:** `TreeSetAside.SetAsideRoots`, `.tidied` under each of `TreesRoots`, the new first, read by every one of those readers. A
  folder still moves into the new place alone. Each place keeps its own `purge-failed.json`. The card's `trees` kind reads both
  places too, passing over each `.tidied`.
- **Verify:** `SetAsidePlacesTests` 4 of 4, all four seen failing on the old readers; the covering fast classes by filter
  (`SetAsideSlimTests`, `SystemSpaceTests`, `SpaceFreeTests`, `SpaceFloorTests`, `KeepRulesTests`, `WorkInventoryTests`,
  `CleanupLeftoversTests`, `ReadShareTreeTests`, `PassLeftoversTests`, `BranchTidyingTests`: 239 of 239); the covering `Process`
  classes with `git.process.runsettings` (`KeepingSlimTests`, `BranchTidyingFolderTests`, `TreeLinkRemovalTests`,
  `PassLeftoversProcessTests`): 26 of 28. The two that failed are `BranchTidyingFolderTests`' purge cases. Each also met the
  machine log's daily prune line, and both fail the same way on the commit before this fix, so this fix did not cause them. Detail:
  D195's KEEPSIZE1a note.

## 2026-10-24 - A session its landing replayed stayed to review, and its tree needed --force (REVIEWLANDED1)

- **Symptom:** on the install a session whose landing replayed its commits onto a line that had moved, and merged them, kept its row
  in *To review* and *What needs you* for two days, and `trees remove` refused its tree without `--force`, while `trees land --plan`
  said its branch held nothing `main` lacked. Seen again with nine sessions each landed on a `quest/` branch the parent merged and
  pruned. Sessions told to rebase after their landing made new commits, which showed as the same stale row, every commit counted.
- **Root cause:** two readings of one question. The landing's plan reads each commit against the line (`LineHolds`: the walk by
  content, then patch identity), so a replay reads landed. The review row (`TreeWorkReads.WorkAsync`), the removals and the clean-up
  asked ancestry, then the content proof (squash tree, files, SQUASHSEEN1's merge). A replay's commits have ids of their own, so
  ancestry missed them, and once the `quest/` branch was pruned nothing held them by ancestry at all. And a tree the content proof did
  hold still counted to review (SQUASHTIDY1b kept the groups as they were).
- **Fix:** the content proof asks the landing's reading as a fourth form (`ReplayHolds`), held to the line as it stands: a differing
  file's newest change on the line, by the graph, must hold one of the branch's patches (D148). A tree held on the line by content
  whose discard would go leaves the review (`TreeWork.Holds`). Where the reading lacks some commits, they alone are counted, offered
  and named as work to land (`ContentProof.Lacks`).
- **Verify:** `ReviewLandedTests` 4 of 4 (`git.process.runsettings`, run twice), `ContentHoldWordsTests` 22 of 22; the covering
  `Process` classes by filter (`SquashSeenTests`, `EndJudgementGitTests`, `ContentHeldTests`, `ContentLandingTests`,
  `ContentOfferTests`, `ContentProofLossTests`, `SessionTreeWorkTests`, `LandGitCountTests`, whose ceilings held unchanged).
  `ContentHeldTests`' squash row now expects `OnLine`. The first run of the pruned-branch test read the line's newest change by date
  and picked the wrong one of two commits made in one second; the log reads `--topo-order` now. Detail: D102's REVIEWLANDED1 note.
## 2026-10-24 - The window could not be typed into while a read worked on its thread (NOBLOCK1)

- **Symptom:** the owner could not type while the window stalled. The install's machine log ranked `ui.stalled` by its slowest
  route: `DAORIS.DRIVER.SESSION_WHERE` 1,439 times, up to 65.9 s; `HEAVY_SLOT` 51, up to 2.9 s; `DAORIS.UPDATE.STATE` 50, up to
  1.9 s; `SESSION_OPENINGS` 46, up to 7.5 s; `HELP_PROPOSALS` 36, up to 1.3 s; `TOOLS_LIST` 8, up to 1.4 s.
- **Root cause:** UIFREEZE1 moved a route's awaits off the window's thread, but its part before the first wait still runs there,
  and these reads did their work in that part. `SESSION_WHERE` was synchronous whole: for each session the rail shows it parsed
  `landings.json` again (`LandedBranches.Landing`, under the record's lock) and listed the tree's folder, so a rail of hundreds of
  sessions was hundreds of parses on the thread. `SESSION_OPENINGS` read each session's record synchronously; `HELP_PROPOSALS`
  read the pending proposals' files and `TOOLS_LIST` the tools' files and the system's path before their first wait;
  `HEAVY_SLOT` waited on the service's registry. `DAORIS.UPDATE.STATE` reads a field under a lock held only for assignments
  (`InstallUpdater.State`): its time was the thread stopped by something else while it was the route on it (the stall's `events`
  and `gc2` count what), not work of its own, so it is unchanged.
- **Fix:** a read marked `[ByEvent]` is answered at once from what the driver's module holds (`HeldAnswers`), `{pending: true}`
  while nothing is; its work runs on a task of its own (`Task.Run`, so not a line of it on the asker's thread), joined by identical
  asks, forgotten by a press, and its answer, where it moved, told as `DAORIS.ANSWERED` naming the page's query by the payload's
  `held` (never the payload, whose trees are paths). The page's state hub writes it into that query (`bridge/state/held.ts`), read
  as the query's own ask reads it, and a pending answer keeps what the query held. The five driver routes are marked;
  `SESSION_WHERE` also reads the landings' record once per ask.
- **Verify:** `DriverModuleHeldTests` (each marked route's ask timed under `UiStallWatch.Bound` with its work held back by the
  `BeforeWork` seam, the event naming the query, the held answer after it, no event for an unmoved answer; SESSION_WHERE's landing
  told by event; a press overtaking a work; a failed work told and refused), `WindowCensusTests` (every route declaring no change
  held, told by event or owed, the owed only falling), the route suites through the test bridge (553 of 553 in the filtered run),
  `held.test.ts` and `SessionRail.test.tsx`'s event case.
## 2026-10-24 - A new Ask Daoris chat's first words went to the one New chat finished, and its open hung (HELPNEWCHAT1)

- **Symptom:** the owner's report on the install at `5e36d25`: words sent in a new Ask Daoris chat went back into the earlier
  conversation's box, and pressing *New chat* again stayed on *正在打开问道衍…*. The machine log beside it: the trees step of
  `help.room.look` asked about 245 trees at 7 to 15 s against its 500 ms bound.
- **Root cause:** three. (1) `START_HELP` carried on any Ask Daoris conversation whose process still ran in the workspace
  (`HelpRoutes.StartHelpAsync`), and *New chat* finishes the running one, which winds up before its process ends: the start was answered
  with it, `running`, and the page handed it the new chat's first words and showed it again. (2) First words handed to a conversation
  stayed in the panel's `firstWords` until its queue answered; *New chat* cleared the panel and left them, so the blank panel read as
  opening and, `firstWords` set, the next conversation never opened ahead. (3) The trees part asked every ended session's tree its records
  name, 238 of the install's 245 gone or moved aside, and its line counted them all. The open itself never waited on the look
  (HELPSTART1, PARALLEL1a); the seconds are the few live trees' git walks (TREELOOK2).
- **Fix:** `ChatRunner.Finish` marks the conversation until its run ends (`Finishing`); `START_HELP` passes a marked one over, waits up
  to 5 s for it (`WoundUpAsync`), then places the new one, and past that answers it `finishing`. The page waits out a start answered
  with one it finished or one said finishing, asking again once the list says it ended, and *New chat* sets the finished one's first
  words aside (`help/AskConversation.tsx`). The trees part walks and counts only a tree whose folder is here and not under `.tidied`
  (`TreeFolders.Walkable`), still listing the rest as asked so no door walks them.
- **Verify:** `AskDaoris.test.tsx`'s two HELPNEWCHAT1 cases (failed first, 77 of 77 now, `src/help` 366 of 366);
  `HelpFinishingTests` 3 of 3; `DriverModuleHelpStartTests` 10 of 10, with the open under a look never answering and failing;
  `HelpTreesReadTests.A_part_walks_only_the_trees_still_here_never_a_gone_or_set_aside_one` (failed first, counting 245).

## 2026-10-24 - A line carried on to another maker credited the earlier maker's uncommitted work to the new one alone (MAKERTRAIL2)

## 2026-10-24 - Sessions a squash landed together were told to rebase onto work already on the line (SQUASHSEEN1)

- **Symptom:** the parent landed two sessions' work on `main` as one squashed commit, beside `trees land`, to correct a
  commit's attribution (LIMITGOON1). Daoris told both sessions to rebase onto `main`; each ran again and found everything there.
- **Root cause:** SQUASHTIDY1's content proof (`ContentHolds.HeldByContentAsync`) knew two forms. One is a squash whose tree is the
  branch's, and the other is every changed file reading the same on the line. A squash of two sessions is neither. Its tree
  holds the other session's work too. The files both sessions changed read otherwise on the line: the backlog, the records and
  the generated index. So the landing found the work unlanded and replayed its commits. Where the two sessions had moved out
  neighbouring backlog rows, the squash removed both in one hunk, the replay conflicted in `TASKS.md`, and the look and the
  terminal told the session to rebase (`RebaseTelling`).
- **Fix:** a third form of the same proof, `SquashCarries`. It asks whether merging the branch into the line as it stands (`git
  merge-tree --write-tree`, the repository's merge attributes applied) adds nothing. Generated files
  are left aside, and the declared backlog is read by rows (`RowsHeld`). The landing refuses such a tree as `carried` before
  any replay, so no rebase is told. The head offers its discard, and the removals and the clean-up take it as landed, with
  the clause *a squash carried it: merging it there adds nothing*.
- **Verify:** `SquashSeenTests` with `git.process.runsettings`, 4 of 4. The landing test fails with the proof switched off, on
  the owner's case: a `TASKS.md` conflict and the rebase words. The content and landing classes the proof reaches ran by
  filter with the same file: `ContentHeldTests`, `ContentLandingTests`, `ContentOfferTests`, `ContentProofLossTests`,
  `TerminalLandRebaseTests`, `AutoLandingRebaseTests`, `LandRebaseLandingTests`, `LandBacklogLandingTests`,
  `LandingSquashTests` and `EndJudgementGitTests`, 70 of 70 with the new class. A first build that asked past commits of the
  line failed `EndJudgementGitTests`' patch-only case, so the proof asks the line's tip alone. `ContentHoldWordsTests`, 15 of 15, and the driver's fast half, 14,183. Detail:
  D102's SQUASHSEEN1 note.

## 2026-10-24 - Conversations an update closed never came back (LIMITRESUME1i)

- **Symptom:** on the install, an update closed conversations mid-turn or with words waiting, and none came back after the
  restart (design §3.9). A driven session that *Update now* stopped counted a strike and was carried on briefed. An update could
  also apply while a conversation was still opening. Four Ask Daoris records the person resumed by `help resume` were told no id
  was kept, though none had ever taken a turn (design §3.10).
- **Root cause:** the updater closed as the person does (`MainForm.CloseForGood`). Neither `StopAll` nor the driver's close could
  tell an update from a person's close. `TakeUpAsync` takes only ended chats with words waiting, and the close left none.
  `DriverLoop.Work` counted only tracked processes whose turn ran. `ReadStrikes` read every interrupted stop as a strike. The
  swallowed keep in `HarnessConversations` left no trace, and `chat.not-kept` was written only where no stop reason stood.
- **Fix:** `ShellClose.Update(build)` is handed to the shell before the close. The close holds the turns and stops the process,
  then keeps a restart word, unsent, on each ended record it cut. The come-up resumes that record by its kept id. An idle
  conversation ends `chat.restarted`. `ChatRunner.InFlight` holds the drain for opening and going-on conversations. A driven
  stop is coded `update.closed`, is passed by `ReadStrikes`, and is step 1's line. `conversation.unkept` is logged, and
  `chat.not-kept` is said beside a stop. `help resume` says `never-spoken`.
- **Verify:** `ChatGoesOnProcessTests` and `LimitResumeTickTests` with `process.runsettings`, 34 of 34. `ChatTurnsTests`,
  `HarnessConversationsTests`, `HelpCommandTests`, `StrikeTests`, `ChatGoOnTests`, `NoteCodesTests` and `HelpCoverageTests`,
  246 of 246. `SessionMessagesTickTests`, whose stand-in changed, 19 of 19. `DriverLoopChatTakenUpTests` and
  `InstallUpdaterTests`, 21 of 21. The driver's fast half, 14,173. `noteLines.test.ts`, 75, and `i18n:check`. The installed
  proof is 1g's. Detail: D206's LIMITRESUME1i note.

## 2026-10-24 - An intake, an opinion and a helper a limit cut off never ran again by themselves (LIMITRESUME1h)

- **Symptom:** none seen on the install yet; D206 design §3.8 read it from the code. An intake an account's limit ended used up its

  answer*, so a lead that ended its turn waiting on it (HELPERWAIT1) was brought back to the person.

  ask (`RecordIntakeAsync`), and the look picks only asks with no binding, so nothing unbound it. The host derived a failed pass's

  session, on a move to `failed` alone (D205 §3.5(f)'s door). The intake sends it with a limited end, which also raises no *Ended*.
  The host says a limited pass's why as `limited`, and the gate sets `Unavailable` / `Cooling` with the `Until` from the cool-off
  its session wrote (`AccountCooling.OfSession`), or the moment it was read where none names it any more. A limited helper's ask
  becomes `cooling` with its account's reset, which `HelperWaits.Open` counts as open. The look runs it again while its lead waits,
  and the walk passes the cooling account. Once the lead no longer waits, the look refuses it `limited` and never runs it again.
  The asker's line, `helper.limited`, says when that account is ready again. The page words the cooling row and the refusal in en
  and zh.

  (the ask still bound to `i1`), `OpinionLookTests.A_pass_a_limit_ended_is_asked_again_by_the_look_after_its_accounts_reset`
  (`limited`, no `Until`), and `HelperLookTests`' two limited-helper tests (`refused`, `no-answer`). Green by class: the service's
  `IntakeTests` (9), `OpinionStoreTests` (12), `HelperBoxShapeTests` and `McpHelperToolTests` (7), and the host's two state-door
  tests. The driver's Process classes `IntakeTests` (39), `OpinionLookTests` (8), `HelperProcessTests` and `HelperWaitTickTests`
  (6), each with `process.runsettings`. The fast `AttentionTests`, `AccountLimitHoldTests`, `AskSignatureTests` (65),

## 2026-10-23 - An approved hand-over that could not be taken read as refused (HANDOVERSAID1)

- **Symptom:** on the install at 13:13 UTC, session `cc63a27e` (quest `#289dcd93ebeb`) wrote `handover.asked`, *Its agent
  asked to hand this session over*, to `codex-acp`. The person pressed yes in the window. Seven seconds later the look wrote
  `handover.refused` with `cannot`, *Its agent's ask to hand this session over was refused: the hand-over could not be taken*.
  The person read that as their own refusal. The session then went on with its own agent, and nothing said so.
- **Root cause:** every path that lets a hand-over go and then fails to take it (`DriverHandOvers.GoAsync`,
  `TakeHandOverAsync` and the window's yes in `SessionsRoutes`) wrote the ask's state and note with one code, `cannot`. The take's
  own reason, a `HandOver` code such as `quest-closed`, went only to the look's line, which the record does not keep. The note's
  wording was the refusal's, so a yes that stood read as a no. Nothing judged the take before the ask waited, so a quest that was
  already closed still asked the person. The ask on the install was the agent's own: its `.hand-over-ask.json` says
  `askedBy: agent`, and its events show the `handover_propose` call at 13:12:43. The person's own hand-over of a quest's session,
  from a terminal or the window, wrote nothing on the record. The real reason on the install is not recoverable. The quest
  started again at 13:13:50, so it was probably not closed at 13:13:16.
- **Fix:** a hand-over let go that the take cannot go on with is said as not taken: `handover.not-taken` (*This session goes on
  with its own agent*), or `handover.not-taken-ends` where its quest closed, went elsewhere or its tree is gone (*Nothing goes on
  with this session*). Each names the take's own reason in words. `HandOverAskWhy` takes the take's codes (`Of` keeps any other as
  `cannot`), and the page's reason family follows them. Before an ask waits on the person, the look judges the take
  (`TakeRefusesAsync`, at each look while it waits). A quest that is closed, an agent that is unavailable or a tree that is gone

  person's words as *failed twice* (TURNFAIL1 read a limit's failure as any other).

  on the protocol door, Daoris's word is kept on the ended record just before it goes on. The same conversation resumes, and every
  conclusion takes the word off. A refusal goes on briefed in the same start, or is held for the person on `elsewhere`. A limited
  record's words go with the walk, an open quest is carried on, and a limited end's words always wait (`WordsAfter.LimitWait`). A
  reset that did not lift the limit is said once.

  cases failed with step 1 switched off. Green by class: `LimitResumeTickTests` (9), `AccountRotationTickTests` (9),

## 2026-10-23 - A turn its model's provider refused parked on the person (APIREFUSAL1)

- **Symptom:** LIMITGOON1's first session on the install (session `cc63a27e`, 08:16 UTC) ended parked: *It stopped with its
  quest still taken, to ask you:* followed by `API Error: Opus 5.5's safeguards flagged this message … Details:
  [reasoning_extraction] … Request ID: req_…`. It sat in *What needs you*, and there was nothing the person could answer.
- **Root cause:** the session's record shows the shape. The adapter said the provider's error as the agent's own message, then
  answered the prompt with `stopReason: refusal`, and exited 0 once stdin closed. The driver logged the stop reason only on the
  console (`— the turn ended: refusal`). The observation reads the exit, the quest's state and a failed call (ACPEND1), never
  the stop reason, because the wire flattens most endings to `end_turn`. So the run read as a clean end with its quest taken,
  the park (STANDDOWN2), and the error was quoted as the agent's question.
- **Fix:** `AcpOutcome.Refusal` names the stop reason, and the run's `HarnessEnding.ProviderRefused` carries it to the
  conclusion. `Observation.Conclude` reads it right after a failed call and before every park (a background cut, a helper wait,
  the park itself). The run is `failed` under its own code, `ended.provider-refused`, followed by the provider's words, request
  id included, as a program's words (`NoteBy.Program`). A failed run is a strike and is carried on as any failed run is.
  `Observation.Resumed` does the same for a resumed run, including one whose quest had closed. A done or a new question to
  another repository reached first still stands. The code is worded in en and zh (`note.json`, `noteLines.ts`).
- **Verify:** red first: `ProviderRefusalTickTests.A_turn_its_provider_refused_is_a_failed_run_by_its_code_and_never_a_park`
  (a real tick, a stand-in ACP agent that takes its quest, says the refusal and ends `refusal`) failed with `awaiting-person`.
  Green: that class's two tests (the question case still parks with `ended.parked-asked`) and `AcpTurnFailureTickTests`, by
  class with `process.runsettings`; `AnswerContinuesTickTests` (its stand-in now keeps `noteParts`); the fast
  `ObservationTests` (with `A_turn_its_provider_refused_is_a_failed_run_by_its_own_code_never_a_park`), `NoteCodesTests`,
  `NoteSitesTests`, `StructureTests`, `AttentionTests` and `AcpTests` (223); the web's `note.test.ts` and `noteLines.test.ts`
  (88). The driver's fast half (14119) and the modules' (2331) pass. Censuses: home and live-logins are clean.
- **Not covered:** Daoris has not measured a refusal on the native door, whose `result` frame it reads for no stop reason. A
  native run its provider refused is still concluded by its exit and its quest's state.

## 2026-10-23 - A parked driven session could be finished or declined, and not answered (PARKANSWER1)

  own wherever the box at the foot answers the park*: the frame passed `onAnswerSession` only where the box did **not** answer
  (`here && !answering`), and the card offered *Answer and carry on…* only where it was handed that. So the card's only way
  to answer was a faint sentence pointing at the box below, and a park whose box the person did not have before them could
  only be ended. The head also guarded the card's answer on `session.quest`, and a park nothing here can answer (a teammate's,
  a browser's) showed its words with no press and no word why. The exact install state was not reproduced from source: a probe
  of the frame with the install's record (`6639c1f2`, carried on after a hand-over, in the work workspace) under every
  reach the driver gives drew either the box or the card's press. The card's dependence on the box was the defect either way.
- **Fix:** the card answers every park the frame can answer (`AwaitingPerson`'s `onAnswer`, `onChoice`, `below`). Where the
  box answers the park too, the card's words go through the box's own say door (`SESSION_INPUT`, `WorkFrame`'s `sayFromCard`),
  with the same refusals (`unaccepted`: go-aheads first, too long), a question's answers as presses once the card's answer is
  opened (PARKVIEW1, the question's id named), and words on their way shown as the box shows them. Elsewhere the card keeps
  the park's answer door (STANDDOWN2). A refusal is said in the card with the words kept. Any driven park takes the card's
  answer, quest or none; a parked chat's stays its composer's. The hint names both places. A park nothing here can answer says
  where it is answered (`work.awaiting.cannot.teammate`, `.elsewhere`, en and zh).

  card, under the question in its closing words* (the install's shape: another workspace, carried on, no process, a yes-or-no
  in the note; sends `SESSION_INPUT`, not the answer door), *says in the card why its answer was not taken, keeping the words*,
  *says on a teammate's parked record why it is not answered here*, the foot-box test's hint, and `WorkFrame.test.tsx` *answers
  the question from the head's card…* (`question: 'q5t10n00'`). Green: the frame's eleven parts with `AttendedSession`,
  `AwaitingPerson`, `SessionHead`, `WaitStrip` and `waits` (305 and 219 tests); `tsc --noEmit`; the i18n and names checks.
- **The trap:** "one owner for the answer" was read as "one place to answer". The owner rule is about which surface owns the

## 2026-10-23 — A conversation whose account met its limit stayed on it, and Ask Daoris reopened with nothing carried (LIMITGOON1)

- **Symptom:** seen on the install at 07:28 UTC: an Ask Daoris conversation's account answered *You've hit your weekly limit* twice,
  both turns failing with the person's words in them. The record then ended, and a new Ask Daoris session opened on the next account
  with nothing carried (`account.rotated … carries=null why=cooling`). The person's lines stayed in the old chat, now under history.
- **Root cause:** a conversation's refused turn was read for a limit (`ChatRunner.Limited`): its account cooled and the turn ended
  `error`, but nothing moved the conversation. The usage curve's move (`CurveMove`) judges what an account said of its windows, never
  a refusal, and passes Ask Daoris by. The brief's go-on (`BriefedMove`) moves only a proven loss, on the same account. So every
  later word was refused the same way, and the next press opened a fresh conversation. The person's words were taken by the refused
  turns, so nothing waited to go on with. Ask Daoris's history listed each record as its own conversation, so even a continued line
  would have shown split.
- **Fix:** `Chat/LimitMove.cs`: at a turn's end whose refusal was read for a limit, the conversation moves to a new part on the
  account the walk offers next, the cooling one passed. That part is handed Daoris's brief of the line before the refused turns and
  then the words those turns held (`Domain/LimitHeld.cs`), its record `from` the old by `limit`, by `daoris`. Ask Daoris's opens in
  its room, its history naming the old. `account.rotated` names what it carries. Ask Daoris's history folds a part continued by the
  brief into its line (`HelpConversations.List`, `Parts`), and the page shows the parts as one conversation and follows the newest
  (`AskConversation.tsx`). Why the brief and not the agent's own resume: the limit-goes-on design, and D189's note of this date.
- **Verification:** red first, `LimitGoesOnProcessTests` (Process, with `src/Daoris.Desktop/process.runsettings`): a stand-in ACP
  agent that answers one exchange on `account-1`, then refuses with Claude Code's limit sentence. For a repository's chat and Ask
  Daoris, the conversation goes on on `account-2` with the brief (carrying the answered exchange) and then the held words, each
  part saying the move once. `LimitHeldTests`, `HelpConversationsTests` (a continued line listed once before search and paging,
  its name, pin and opening kept), the modules' `DriverModuleHelpHistoryTests`, and `AskDaoris.test.tsx` (both parts' answers on
  one page, one message box, the next words to the newest part). No real agent or sign-in ran. The window has not been seen.
- **Commit:** `5a2cd2a1f`, `5abcb801f`.

- **Symptom:** trees whose sessions the person finished stayed locked as `daoris session <id>`. Even `trees remove --force`
  failed with Git's "cannot remove a locked working tree", including trees at the home's old place.
- **Root cause:** TREELOCK1 (`3f98e479a`) released locks in the run's `finally` only when that run did not retain its tree.
  A parked run retained it, but a later terminal move had no release. Its fallback sweep accepted only `TreesRoot`, missing
  the old place TREEPLACE1 accepts, and forced removal never checked whether a session lock's owner had ended.
- **Fix:** successful terminal state responses release only that local record's own lock; helper waits and setup continuations
  retain theirs. `SessionLocks` sweeps both places through `TreeContext.Holds`. The removal's local ledger check keeps running
  and parked trees under the repository's start lock, and force releases a matching ended owner's lock before asking Git.
- **Verify:** red first, `SessionLocksTests` with `src/Daoris.Desktop/git.process.runsettings`: 13 tests, 8 failures (five terminal
  moves retained their lock; the old-place sweep missed its tree; forced removal failed at both places). The final expanded class
  passes all 23 tests, including removal beside an unrelated live record naming no tree. Desktop discard's four protection cases
  failed before its forwarding was fixed. Filtered driver fast classes pass 207 tests; the reached modules classes pass 54.
  Individually with the git settings: `TreePlacesGitTests` 4, `SessionTreesTests` 20, `LandingTidyTests` 11 and
  `BranchTidyingProcessTests` 14 pass. `SessionTreeLockTickTests` passes its real-run lifecycle test with `process.runsettings`.
  Home, read-sharing, optional-lock, live-login, partial-type and workspace-word censuses pass.
- **Test observation:** one intermediate lock run failed the old-place parked-holder case once; the quiet runner emitted no
  diagnostic. All four holder cases and then the full 23-test class passed unchanged on reruns. The cause is undetermined.
- **Commit:** `d874f9d84`, `445a4118f`, `f12c716b0`, `3ad4e1454`.
- **A regression the family rehearsal found, fixed the same day:** `trees remove` began requiring a service
  (`ServiceClient.FromEnvironment()` in `TreesConsole.cs`), so a terminal with none, as the rehearsal runs it, was refused with
  *no DAORIS_SERVICE_URL* where it had judged from the files. The verb now asks the service's ledger where it finds one, and goes
  on from the files where it finds none (`TreesConsole.ServiceOrNone`).

## 2026-10-23 — Leaving Review left its git running, and a runner returned before its git had ended (GITAPP1a-iii)

- **Symptom:** a person who left Review mid-read (another session, another tab, the window closed) left the host's git running to
  its end: the page's wait was cancelled and nothing reached the host (`bridge/sessions/trees.ts`'s reader said so). Two windows on
  one review each started their own read.
- **Root cause:** three gaps (D202's round-4 point 3 and round-5 points 4-5, Codex R3-8, R4-4, R4-5). The bridge's call carries no
  cancellation, and `SESSION_DIFF` had no id the page could name, so no door led from the page's leave to the route's token. The
  route was not shared, so a second window was a second chain. And the three runners (`ChildProcess.RunAsync` beneath
  `RunGitAsync`, `ReadGitAsync`, `GitBytesAsync`) killed git's tree on cancellation and returned without awaiting its exit, the
  process disposed in `finally`; `KillTree` swallows a refused kill, so one that failed read as one that worked.
- **Fix:** `SESSION_DIFF` carries a `read` id the page makes per call. The router opens it in `ReadLeaves`, a source linked to
  the route's own token (the asking window's bridge lifetime), and joins the read through `RouteFlights` by the session alone
  (`[OneFlight("SESSION_DIFF", By = "id")]`, the id kept out of the flight's key). `READ_LEAVE { read }` cancels that source and
  answers `left`; the last waiter stops the flight. The page's `readDiff` counts its waiters and sends it once the last has been
  gone `READ_LEAVE_GRACE` (10 s); a return within the grace joins the read. A window destroyed cancels its bridge's lifetime and so
  its reads, with no script. In the driver, `ChildProcess.EndAsync` kills the tree and awaits the exit within `ExitBound` (5 s); the
  three runners end through it and dispose the process only after. An exit not seen there is thrown as `ProcessUnendedException`
  (the cancellation, with the pid and the reason) and said by the seam as `git.unended` (node, runner, kind, pid, reason, no
  path) to the log the route opens (`GitUnended.SaidTo`). The streamed runners' pipe reads now hear their token (`Heard`), since a git
  that outlived its kill would otherwise hold its runner in the read and never be said.
- **Verification:** driver `GitRunnersEndTests` (Process, 9): each runner cancelled during creation and while running returns with
  the stand-in's pid exited, watched through a handle of the test's own; with the kill refused by a stub, each throws
  `ProcessUnendedException` after its bound and the log says `git.unended`. Beside it `ChildProcessTests`, `ChildProcessKillTests`,
  `GitStreamEndsTests`, `GitLaunchTests` and `GitBoundsTests` (86 with it), and `HelpCoverageTests`, `ProcessStartsCensusTests` (108
  with `GitLaunchTests`). Modules `DriverModuleReviewLeaveTests` (Process, 4) through the real route boundary with a stand-in git
  that waits and then runs the real git: the page's leave kills it and the call is answered `OPERATION_CANCELLED`; a second window
  waiting keeps the read until it leaves too; two of the kit's own `IpcHostBridge`s over the kit's `MessageDispatcher`, one disposed
  mid-read (its git ended, no `READ_LEAVE` sent), and a read both wait on surviving the first's disposal and answering the second
  its review. `DriverModuleReadLeaveTests` (2) holds a leave for an unknown or answered id as `left: false`. With them
  `DriverModuleOneFlightTests`, `StatePublisherTests`, `PipeCensusTests`, `DriverModuleRoutesTests`, `DriverModuleTreesTests` and
  `DriverModuleReviewTests` (335). Web: `trees.leave.test.ts` (4: the grace, the last waiter, a return within the grace, an
  answer within it) and the review's 22 files (319); the web typecheck. The censuses: home, optional locks, one word, read shares.
  The runner cases were written beside the fix and not first run red against the old runners.
## 2026-10-23 — Review asked every git after the one before, whatever it needed (GITAPP1a-ii)

  before: its depth was its starts (13 for the review, then 21 for the offer, on the before-bench).

  choices moved into `ReviewChoices` and `UntrackedFold`, which the chain calls too. The census found one defect of the graph
  before landing: the selection (I) began only after the uncommitted Π chain, so it waited on W, S and the untracked reads. Σ now
  runs outside Π, and only M waits its Π turn.

  chain's on every P1.7 branch: the answer as JSON (patches byte for byte), refusals and faults by their words, the Π commands in

  `LandedReviewTests`, `TreeDiffTests`, `TreeDiffSplitTests`, `WorkingTreeProvenanceTests`, `GitReviewCommandTests`,

- **The after-bench** (design §10.3, reported, never failing): `git review 3372bd58 --time`, this row's own session tree (15 files

## 2026-10-23 — Review's git was counted for one runner of three, and never timed (GITAPP1a-i)

  its flow's budget, and the gate's wait and the creation (`ProcessStarts.Timing`) apart from the run. It adds no flag. `SESSION_DIFF`'s
  chain moved unchanged into `SessionReviews`, which the route and `daoris-driver git review <session> [--json] [--time]` read
  through; each read writes `review.read`.

  today's chain per path, as D202's GITAPP1a-i note lists. `GitReviewCommandTests`, `DriverCommandTests`, `HelpCoverageTests`,

  modules' `DriverModuleTreesTests` and `PipeCensusTests`. The git classes counting `Started` or covering the runners pass too (82,

  `PullRequestStateTests`, `SessionTreesTests`, `TreeSyncStartsTests`, `GitStreamEndsTests` and `ReviewBaseTests`; and with `process.runsettings` `ChildProcessTests`, `GitHoldsProcessTests` and `GitSshHoldsProcessTests` (18).
- **The before-bench** (design §10.3, reported, never failing), at `958a0e0b8`: `git review 65ea247e --time`, this row's own
  session tree, ten runs each. Nothing else of this session ran beside it; the machine's other sessions did.

  | Case | Starts (review + offer + untracked) | Median | p90 | Creation, summed (median run) | Gate wait |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 29 files committed, nothing untracked | 34 (13 + 21 + 0) | 6.2 s | 7.4 s | 0.49 s | ≤ 2 ms |
