## 2026-10-23 — A refused move back to the person was said to no one (HELPERWAIT1c)

- **Symptom:** found by Codex's round-2 read of COWORKUX1 (#5, its second half), never seen on a machine. A lead waiting on its own
  helper, whose helper ended with no answer and whose move back to the person the service refused, stayed `completed`. Its refusal
  was said only as a `Wait` look line (`DriverHelpers.BackToPersonAsync`). That class promises a row of *What needs you*
  (`LookSaid.cs`, `LookClass.Wait`), and no record carried one: the person was never shown the session, which kept its tree while it
  waited. Beside it, the go-ahead read the service does not answer parked the turn, with no case proving it (design §5 point 1).
- **Root cause:** HELPERWAIT1 kept the move's failure in the driver's memory alone (`_backFailed`), to say it once. *What needs you* is
  judged from records (`NeedsAPerson`), and its park row reads `awaiting-person`, which the refused record never reached. Nothing
  else on file said the record waited on the person.
- **Fix:** the driver keeps a refused move as `<session>.back.json` beside the helper's asks (`HelperBack`, `HelperFiles.WriteBack`).
  It holds the service's words and dates from the first refusal. An unreachable service writes none, and leaves a kept refusal as
  it was. It goes once the move lands, or at the first look that no longer brings the session back. The attention slice reads it
  (`AttentionStateSlice.BackWaits`), and the judge makes a `helper-ended` row in *Holding work*, unless the record in hand has
  moved on. The page words it in en and zh, the refusal passed through as a value, and its door opens the session
  (`attention.ts`, `AttentionRow.tsx`, `App.tsx`; the terminal's `NoticesRead.KindGroups`).
- **Verification:** red first. `HelperLookTests`: the refused move is kept, an unreachable service keeps none and leaves a refusal
  standing, and the move landing or the quest closing lets it go (failed before the fix: no record). The go-ahead read, unreachable
  or refused, parks the turn. It passed against the built code, so it was checked against a mutant that read the failure as "none
  asked", and both cases went red. `AttentionStateSliceTests`: the row by its session, with the refusal, none for a record that
  moved on, and the file's read. `attention.test.ts`, `AttentionRow.test.tsx`: the wording in en and zh, its group, place, order
  and door. Green: the driver's helper classes (78), the modules' attention and notices classes (114), the driver's fast half
  (13,881) and the modules' (2,320), the web's attention and locale files (282, 104), the Process classes `HelperWaitTickTests` (2) and `HelperProcessTests` (4) with `process.runsettings`,
  and `HelperCaptureProcessTests` (4) with `git.process.runsettings`.

## 2026-10-23 — A hand read back after its answer was lost told nothing on this machine (HELPERWAIT1b2)

- **Symptom:** found by Codex's read of COWORKUX1's round 4 (its one blocking finding), not seen on a machine. A helper's answer whose
  hand kept the word and then lost its answer (a 500, an unreadable success, a timeout) was marked handed at the next look and never
  reached the asker's run. A conversation's runner was never told, so the word waited on its record until another word or a restart;
  an urgent ask's running asker never had it held for its next step.
- **Root cause:** HELPERWAIT1b's read-back (`DriverHelpers.HandedBefore`) found the word waiting and wrote `Handed`, but the hand's
  local dispatch ran only on a hand that answered: the inbox's `HoldKept`, the asker's note and, for a conversation, the
  `reaches: resume` event the shell's chat runner hears (`ChatGoOn.Heard`). The uncertain return skipped all three, and the read-back
  did not make them up. The runner's come-up sweep (`TakeUpAsync`) runs once at the shell's start, so nothing else recovered it.
- **Fix:** the read-back now returns the record holding the word and the word itself, and dispatches it before it marks the ask
  handed: to that record, under the word's id, with no second hand. One `Dispatch` serves the hand and the read-back. It holds an
  urgent word in a running asker's inbox where its door takes words at the next step, then keeps the note, then the conversation's
  event. It is idempotent by the id: the inbox holds an id once, and a conversation already told of the word is not told again. The
  hand now dispatches before the state's mark, so a mark that fails to write leaves a word the read-back completes. A word consumed
  with no event still settles `hand-uncertain`.
- **Verification:** red first, each timing out on the dispatch it lacked, then green. `HelperLookTests`: a lost hand to an ended
  conversation, with the real `ChatRunner` over the driver's events, goes on once (`working`, `failed`, one end announced, one
  `resume` event under the word's id) and a later look tells it nothing more. A lost urgent hand to a running asker reaches its inbox's
  next step once, under the record's id at the urgent level. Green: `HelperLookTests` (65), the driver's fast half (13,859), and
  the Process classes `HelperProcessTests` (4) and `HelperWaitTickTests` (2) with `process.runsettings`, and
  `HelperCaptureProcessTests` (4) with `git.process.runsettings`.

## 2026-10-23 — The helper wait did not keep four guarantees its design claimed (HELPERWAIT1b)

- **Symptom:** found by Codex's read of COWORKUX1's round 3, not seen on a machine. Round 3 claimed four guarantees of the built
  helper wait that the code did not keep. The guarantees: a park keeps the question it parked for, a hand is made once, the waiting
  lead keeps its tree until it reaches the person, and the answer goes to the line's live part.
- **Root cause:** four separate gaps. (1) `QuestionFiles.Settle` kept only a question that read and was fresh, and deleted the rest.
  A question file that did not read made the turn park (`AskedSince` null), then the same conclusion deleted it. (2)
  `HelperDoors.HandAsync` answered `Handed: false` for any unsuccessful or unreadable answer, and the driver cleared the attempt mark
  on it. But the desk keeps the word before its answer is made, and the host can still answer 500 after. A word consumed with its
  event unwritten then left no evidence and no mark, and the next look handed it again. (3) `BranchTidying.WaitingOnHelpersAsync`
  held a waiting lead's tree only while one of its asks was open. After its last ask was refused and its move back to the person
  failed, the lead was still waiting but held nothing, so the tidy could let go of its lock and take its tree while the ledger held
  it. (4) The hand door and the driver's line read stopped at sixteen links and took the record there, which the line may have left.
- **Fix:** (1) a parked conclusion keeps a question file that does not read; a read of it is still none. (2) `HelperHanded` tells
  `Kept`, `Refused` and `Uncertain`. Only the desk's own refusal is `Refused`: its sentence on a 400, 404 or 409, or an older host's
  bare 404. The mark is cleared on that alone. An uncertain hand keeps its mark and is said as a retry. The next look reads the line
  back: the word found marks it handed, and nothing found settles `hand-uncertain`. (3) the tidy, the lock's let-go and Ask
  Daoris's housekeeping read the service's predicate: waiting on its own helper while its quest is taken. (4) both sides follow one
  link past the bound, and a line that goes on is refused `CannotTake`, nothing kept. Beside them, `HelperWaitTickTests` runs at a cap
  of one (Codex's finding 5), and three of HELPERWAIT1's look lines are classed where they are made, which `LookSaidTests` refused
  once HELPERWAIT1 met main's census. The partner's door has the same bound (PARTNERLINE1, open).
- **Verification:** red first, each for its own reason, then green. `QuestionFilesTests` (the unread file kept by a first run's and a
  resumed run's park). `HelperLookTests` (a word kept and its answer lost as a 500, an unreadable success and a timeout; found, or
  consumed with no event; one hand each; a line of seventeen links refused, sixteen handed). `BranchTidyingTests` (held after the
  refusal with the return failed, and with no ask on file; let go once the quest is done). `HelperHostTests` (seventeen links refused
  with nothing kept, sixteen reach the newest; red without the fix). Green: the driver's fast half (13,792), `HelperHostTests` (10),
  and the Process classes `HelperWaitTickTests` (2, with its cap-one assertion) and `HelperProcessTests` (4) by class with
  `process.runsettings`, and `HelperCaptureProcessTests` (4) with `git.process.runsettings`.
## 2026-10-23 — A tree opened before the home's layout moved was refused as not a session tree (TREEPLACE1)

- **Symptom:** after the install's layout move (`home.moved`, the start of 2026-10-23), 11 trees of this repository still sat
  under the install's `data/trees/` while new ones opened under `work/trees/`. `trees land` refused such a tree as not a
  session tree, so SESSWATCH1a and COAGENT1b part 7 were merged by hand. `trees remove` refused it too. The tidy kept it as
  "checked out at …, which is not a session tree", so seven trees whose work was already on main stayed, and every look
  walked them (TREELOOK1).
- **Root cause:** D172 point 6 never moves a tree: git's worktree links and the agent's conversation name it by path. So the
  move left the trees at the old place of `HomeEntry.Trees` (`trees/*/*/*` under the old home) and moved other entries. Once the new
  place held anything, `DaorisHome.Entry(home, HomeEntry.Trees)` answered the new place. `TreeContext.Holds`, and the
  hand-written prefix tests in `TreeLands.MergeAsync` and `TreeRemovals.RemoveAsync`, accepted only that one root. D172's
  HOMELAYOUT3 note ("one root each, as found") assumed the old root would answer while it held any tree. It did not, once
  anything was written at the new place.
- **Fix:** one predicate, `TreeContext.RootOf`: the place of `HomeEntry.Trees` (`DaorisHome.Places`, new then old) holding the
  path below it. `Holds` asks it, and so do the merge's and the removal's guards, which no longer test a prefix of their
  own. `OwnerOf` and `LinkBelowTreesRoot` read the layout under the root that holds the tree. A layout lookup by branch
  (`TreeContext.TreeAt`: the folder at either place where it is, else the new place) serves the gate's and landing's unit,
  the set-aside's last look, `MovedOnTo`, the replays' trace and `SessionBranches.Lives`. The look's list and
  `LearnTreesAsync` read both places. The other fix offered, moving each tree with `git worktree move`, was not taken.
  D172 point 6 and its *Rejected* line keep a tree where it is, since a running or resumable conversation names its folder.
  New trees still open at the new place, and the set-aside folder stays under it.
- **Verification:** `TreePlacesGitTests` (real git, a scratch home whose two places differ). Each tree is opened, then moved
  with `git worktree move` to the old place. A chain's later tree there lands on a branch rule, and the landing's tidy takes
  the earlier one there with its branch. A tree there merges. One is removed by its path and one by its branch's door. A
  tree moved outside both places is refused by land, merge, remove and the branch's door, even forced, and keeps its work.
  With the driver change reverted, the three old-place cases fail and the outside one passes. `TreePlacesTests` holds the
  predicate on paths: both places held, the workspace and repository read under each, and a lookalike `trees-old` refused.
  Also green: the driver's fast half, and 18 tree Process classes by class with `git.process.runsettings`.
## 2026-10-23 — A session started through the launcher had no job the driver could read or end (CONTAINCPU1)

- **Symptom:** found in review of TERMTRUST1a part (i), not seen on a machine. Since every agent starts through `daoris-piece-start`,
  `SessionProcesses.JobOf` answered null for every agent. The watcher (SESSWATCH1a, D200 §1.2) read every session's busy as
  unknown, so a silent session whose child computed was marked quiet as if it did nothing. State E's end of a run whose capture a
  stray descendant held (`Driver.CaptureWithinAsync`, `JobOf(id)?.Terminate()`) ended nothing.
- **Root cause:** `SessionProcesses.Track` holds a job of its own over a start (ORPHAN1's `ProcessJob.Hold`), and part (i) skipped it
  for a launcher (`ThroughLauncher ? null : ProcessJob.Hold`). A launcher already in a fresh job cannot join the agents' job that
  other agents hold. The launcher's own kill-on-close job, which contains the harness's tree, was unnamed, so the driver had no way
  to it, and the entry's job stayed null.
- **Fix:** the launcher names its own job by its process id, `Local\daoris-launched-<pid>` (`PieceLauncher.OwnJobOf`), unnamed only
  where the name will not take. `JobOf` opens that job by name the first time it is asked (`ProcessJob.OpenHolding`, query and
  terminate). It keeps the job only where `IsProcessInJob` says it holds the tracked launcher. It holds it until the tracking lets
  go, as the job of a direct start is held. By then the launcher's joins are long over, so the open races nothing. Until the
  launcher has made it, the answer is null and busy is unknown for that look. The person's stop now also ends the session's job
  after its tree kill. That reaches a process whose parent had exited, and a launcher's job that the driver's handle keeps open.
  The launcher reporting its handle back was not taken: its stdout is the harness's protocol, so a report would need a second
  channel and a handle duplicated into the driver. A name derived from the session was not taken either: a run tried again on the
  same session could meet the name still held.
- **Verification:** `LaunchedSessionJobProcessTests` (Process, `Alone`) starts a stand-in through the built launcher laid out beside its
  home. The stand-in is `cmd` leaving a computing child whose parent has exited, then waiting silently. `JobOf` opens the launcher's
  job, which holds three processes. The watcher, reading through the driver's own `JobRead`, brings it as *busy, nothing heard* and
  never marks it. `Stop` empties that job and the agents' job. With the open by name removed, the test fails at `JobOf`. Also green:
  `PieceLauncherTests` (the name), `PieceLauncherProcessTests`, `AgentStartsProcessTests`, `ProcessJobTests`,
  `SessionWatchProcessTests`, `CaptureBoundProcessTests`, the fast `SessionProcessesTests`, `SessionWatchTests`, `AgentStartsTests`
  and `CategoryTests`, and the Process classes that stop a real session.

## 2026-10-23 — Opening Review could take the index lock in a tree its session was writing in (REVIEWLOCK1)

- **Symptom:** found by Fable's GITAPP1 proposal, not seen on a machine. Review reads a session's tree while its agent may be
  writing there. A read that took the tree's `index.lock` at the moment the agent's `git add` or `git commit` wanted it failed
  the agent's write with git's "index.lock: File exists".
- **Root cause:** a `git status`, and a `git diff` against the working tree, refresh the index's stat data. They take
  `index.lock` to write it back. Review's status (`WorkingTree.UncommittedDiffAsync`), the offer's (`TreeWorkReads.UncommittedOfAsync`)
  and `WorkingTree.CleanAsync` asked without `--no-optional-locks`, as did 19 other statuses and diffs in the driver. Only the
  helper capture and the help door passed it. A second cause showed up in a probe with git 2.53: a `git diff` against the
  working tree refreshes and writes the index whatever `--no-optional-locks` says. `diff --cached` and a diff of two commits do not.
- **Fix:** all 24 statuses and diffs in the driver pass `--no-optional-locks` before the command. Review's range read
  (`WorkingTree.RangeAsync`, whose uncommitted range is `HEAD`) also passes `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false`. Unrefreshed,
  git lists a file whose stat data alone moved as `M` in `--raw`, with no `--numstat` count and no patch. `RangeSplit` drops
  that file: a file that changed always has a count, a binary one `-`. `tools/optional-locks.mjs`, run by `npm run verify`,
  refuses a status or diff in the driver's sources asked without the flag before its command. A read meant to write marks
  its line; none does. One worktree diff still refreshes the index: `BranchReplays`' conflict listing (`diff --diff-filter=U`).
  It runs inside a replay the driver makes in the tree itself, not in a read of a running session's tree.
- **Verification:** `ReviewLockTests` (real git, a session tree in scratch) makes Review's reads in `SESSION_DIFF`'s order.
  In one case a stand-in holds the tree's `index.lock`: each read answers, the lock is still the stand-in's, and the
  stand-in's own commit succeeds once it lets the lock go. In the other the index's stat data is stale: the index's bytes and
  time are unchanged and no lock is left. With the offer's status flag removed again, that case and the census both fail.
  `TreeDiffSplitTests` holds the stat-only drop and the read's arguments. The census's test refuses planted cases and passes on
  the tree. Also green: `TreeDiffTests`, `ReviewBaseTests`, `LandGitCountTests`, and the fast classes whose git stand-ins
  match on the command (190).

## 2026-10-23 — A session waiting on its own helper was shown waiting on the person (HELPERWAIT1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, twice in GITAPP1's design session. A driven session asked a Codex helper (`helper_ask`) and ended
  its turn so the helper could read its work. It was recorded `awaiting-person`, its note saying it stopped "to ask you", and *What
  needs you* counted it as the person's while the helper worked. When the helper answered, the answer sat unread until the person
  answered a question nobody had asked, and every look read the records whole to hold the hand again.
- **Root cause:** `Observation.Conclude` read every clean end that held its quest as a park, with no input for an open ask of the
  session's own. `DriverHelpers.DeliverHelperAsync` (then `:411`) held any parked asker's answer until the person answered, and
  retried that hold at every look.
- **Fix:** such an end concludes `completed` by `ended.awaits-helper` when its agent's own ask is still open (an unjudged one
  included) and its turn asked the person nothing (a question file that does not read counts as asked). The helper's answer reopens
  it once, as the next turn, with `HelperWords.Compose`, handed to the newest record of its line. It keeps its tree while it waits:
  the ledger's exclusion, the run's lock, the planner's further part and the tidy all read it as the holder. A park keeps its park;
  its helper's answer is handed beside the person's once they answer, so both reach it in one prompt. A helper that ends with no
  answer brings it back to the person with the reason, through a new guarded ledger move (D46's note); a failed move is retried at
  each look and said once. An attempt mark written before the hand door makes the hand once-only across a restart: an attempt with no
  evidence on the line settles `hand-uncertain` and is never made again. A held or refused hand is said once and not read again
  until its asker moves. D188's HELPERWAIT1 note has the rule; Codex's round-2 findings 1-5, 7 and 8 on COWORKUX1 are each built.
- **Verification:** red first, then green. The covering driver classes outside the Process half (573: `HelperLookTests`,
  `HelperWaitsTests`, `ObservationTests`, `EntryPartsPlanTests`, `PlannerTests`, `BranchTidyingTests`, `SessionGroupsTests`,
  `ContinuationTests`, `NoteCodesTests` among them), the service's `SessionLedgerTests` and store classes (148), `HelperHostTests` (8),
  and the Process classes `HelperWaitTickTests` and `SessionMessagesTickTests` (21): a stand-in asks, ends its turn, and goes on with
  the answer with no press of the person's; a park made before the rule is kept parked, then goes on with both answers in one prompt.
  The web's `note.test.ts` and locale tests hold the new reason in en and zh. The censuses (home paths, one word, partials, read
  shares, live logins) are clean. No real agent asked a real helper here; the installed window is the parent's to see.

## 2026-10-23 — The account fold read a stray folder under the agent homes as an agent (POOLSTRAY1)

- **Symptom:** POOL1d found this on the install. The fold at the 13:42 UTC update wrote
  `rotation["claude-code$a"] = ["backups", "sessions"]` into `harnesses.json`, with a `pooled` receipt under it.
  `claude-code$a` is a folder that a start with an unexpanded `$a` in its config path left on 2026-10-12.
- **Root cause:** `HarnessSettings.AccountsOf` enumerated every folder under the account homes as an agent. It read each
  folder's subfolders as that agent's accounts (`Profiles`). `AccountSet.Fold` then folded every agent the accounts or the
  wiring named. Nothing asked whether any adapter or plugin named the folder.
- **Fix:** the agents Daoris knows are `AdapterSet.Agents`: the build's names, each door's owner, and every installed plugin's
  harnesses, disabled ones included. They are handed to `AccountsOf` and every path-level read and write of the wiring. The
  fold folds only an agent the accounts name. A stray folder is said once to the machine log (`accounts.stray`). A stray
  agent's `rotation` and `pooled` entries are dropped at the next change, with an `accounts.strayDropped` line. D197's
  POOLSTRAY1 note has the detail.
- **Verification:** three new `AccountSetTests` cases run on a scratch home. A stray folder folds to the known agent alone and
  is said once. A wiring naming the stray loses its order and receipt, with its line. A disabled plugin's agent stays known.
  Also green: the class's other 16, and the covering driver (815) and modules (73) classes, outside the Process half.
## 2026-10-23 — The driver's other readers of a record moved into place read it plainly (READSHARE1)

- **Symptom:** found by BINDRACE1, not seen on a machine: every driver reader of a file `AtomicFile` writes, but the run binding's,
  read it through `File.ReadAllText` (or `ReadAllBytes`, `OpenRead`), which a file Windows' move still holds refuses with error 32.
  Each failed its own way in that moment: a record read as missing or unreadable, an edit refused as unreadable, a process marker
  counted alive, a lease read as busy, a stamp read as moved so every tree was walked again.
- **Root cause:** BINDRACE1's (its entry of 2026-10-22): a reader's share mode. Nothing held the readers to `AtomicFile.ReadText`; the
  shared read was a convention of four call sites.
- **Fix:** 85 reads in 63 driver files go through `AtomicFile.ReadText`, `ReadBytes` or `OpenRead` (the latter two new). That takes
  in the home's lease and identity and the git grants, which the driver moves into place itself, and the launcher and the git door
  compile `AtomicFile.cs` for the readers they share. `tools/read-shares.mjs`, run by `npm run verify`, refuses a plain read in a
  driver source that writes through `AtomicFile` (or `JsonFile.Write`, `JsonKeeping.Save`, `RecordList`), or that names where one
  lands (a writer type's path member, a home entry a writer names). A read of a file nothing moves is marked on its line; ten are. The eleventh mark keeps one
  read plain on purpose: `SessionRequests.TakeAt` (REQTAKE1) reads what it renamed aside, and its refusal is what tells it another
  loop's rename still holds the file and will move it on. Shared, both loops read it and one request was honoured twice
  (`SessionRequestsTests.Two_loops_taking_twenty_at_once_honour_each_exactly_once`, seen failing with the read shared).
- **Verification:** 90 tests hold each moved reader's file with `MoveHold`, assert a plain read is refused, and read it through
  the product's reader (five `ReadShare…Tests` classes, and `HelpTreesReadTests`' stamp case, which is real git). With the fix commit
  reversed, its reads plain again, 83 of those tests failed; the other seven cover readers a separate commit moved. A 91st
  holds the exception: a take whose moved-aside file is held is put back, not taken. All pass with the fix, with `AtomicFileTests` and `WorkflowRunBindingTests`. The census's own test plants each shape it refuses
  and passes on the tree. Writers that read and then write over a held file see the hold released mid-call, as a real move's is.

## 2026-10-23 — The git half's fixtures built repositories, cloned origins and let git start its maintenance, a start each (PROCSPEED1b)

- **Symptom:** `driver-process-git` on the full set at `c557800`: 693 tests, 16,326 s of test time in 4,135 s of wall (69 min) at
  four classes at once, about 24 s a test, with builders loading the machine.
- **Where the seconds go (measured):**
  - *The wall is the summed time over four.* At `c557800` four tests ran for 4,036 of the 4,135 s, and the longest class
    (`PullRequestStateTests`) took 914 s: no class was the wall, so splitting one shortens nothing. Slowed 2.2 times (the traced
    run below), its 2,729 s did pass its share (2,443 s), and 1,060 s of that run's end had fewer than four running.
  - *A test is its git starts.* The slowest test of each of fifteen slow classes, traced one at a time (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, a
    file a process; the machine at a mean 45% with other sessions' work): 3,023 starts in 1,274 s. git itself ran 0.1 to 0.2 s a
    start, and for about half of each test no git ran at all: the start's own cost. A `git rev-parse` from node took 439 ms at the
    median with the CPU at 6% (a bare `cmd /c exit` 74 ms, and 1.3 s at its 90th percentile): the security products hook every
    start (DEVDRIVE1). No fixed wait was found: no gap between two starts reached 5 s, and the longest, 2 to 4.4 s, were starts.
  - *Who starts them.* The whole half on its base (`7794ad49`), traced, four at once: 37,353 starts, the product's 27,370 (73%),
    the fixtures' 5,503 (15%: `commit` 1,286, `add` 1,203, `rev-parse` 662, `config` 558, `init` 314, `push` 146) and git's own
    4,480 (12%): `maintenance run --auto` after every commit, merge and fetch 1,692, `worktree add`'s `reset` 738 and `branch` 658
    (the product's), and each push's receive side (`receive-pack`, `pack-objects`, `unpack-objects`, `rev-list`).
  - *The product's own.* In the slowest test (`PullRequestStateTests`' clean-up case, 691 product starts) 459 repeat an earlier
    start's arguments in the same checkout: each flow, a landing, a plan, a look, asks afresh by design (D88, LANDGIT1). Of the
    fifteen tests' 284 `merge-base --is-ancestor`, 76 ask a commit against itself, and 19 `rev-list --count` count a commit
    `--not` itself. Left to PROC1d-v, the owner's call on D88.
- **Fix (the fixtures only; no product line changed):** every remaining step-by-step build copies a seed: `GitSeed.PlainAsync`
  (on `main`, its identity, `README.md` committed as `first`) for `AutoLandingFixture` and `AutoLandingWakesTests`, `SweepTests`,
  `SessionTreeOnlyHereTests`, `SessionTreeWorkTests`, `CanonicalLineTests`, `CloseFenceGitTests`, `LandGitCountTests` and
  PROCSPEED1's five; shapes of their own for `BranchTidyingFixture` (its ignores and build output), `LandingPluginFixture` (an
  origin nothing was pushed to) and `GitReadsTests` (the whole dated history, whose ids every build shares). Each seed's
  repositories, bare origins too, set `maintenance.auto` and `receive.autogc` off (`GitSeed.NoMaintenanceAsync`), so a commit,
  a merge, a fetch or a push in a copy or a tree opened from it is one git. `LandedFixture.SquashOnPlatformAsync` and the
  platform's commits (`CommitOnOriginAsync`, which `TreeSyncFixture`, `TreeUpdateTests`, `TreeSyncHeldTests`,
  `TreeStartSyncTests` and `ReviewBaseTests` now call) are git's plumbing in the bare origin (`merge-tree --write-tree`,
  `commit-tree`, `mktree`, one `update-ref --stdin`): three starts for a squash, where a clone that merged, committed and pushed
  twice made about twenty. A test that reads the first commit reads the seed's, the same in every copy, and none reads its time
  (the strays' quiet reads only what is under the home's trees, and no copy is). Not copied: `SessionTreesTests`, `TreeMergeTests`, `SessionLocksTests`, `TreeDiffTests` and
  `TreeFilesTests` init on git's own default branch on purpose, and `GitStreamEndsTests`' two 5 s waits (10 s of the half) are
  negative waits a shell's kill cannot signal.
- **Verification:** red first: `FixtureGitTests` did not compile without `GitSeed.PlainAsync`, then failed two cases on the old
  fixtures (a landed copy's commit started `maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`; the squash left a `platform-*` clone),
  then all six passed. After, on main's merge (2026-10-23, the machine otherwise quiet): the 18 changed classes' git cases, 242
  of them, in 14 min 6 s of wall at four classes at once, about 3.5 s a test against 24 s; the whole half's time comes with CI1's

## 2026-10-22 — A folder held on the own sign-in's file would have reached *What needs you* without its `own` (POOL1c)

- **Symptom:** found in POOL1c's build, before any window showed it: the attention row of a trust hold on the person's own
  sign-in's file would have offered *Trust this folder*, which `TRUST_FOLDER` refuses as `TRUST_OWN_HOME`.

  pushes each row picked to `AttentionStateSlice.Fields`, whose `trust` named `folder` and `trustFile` alone, so the pick
  dropped `own` and no test read a row as pushed.

  `runs` leave the allow-list with the page's types, which the twin test holds equal both ways.

## 2026-10-22 — One slow service answer froze the window's sessions list for the rest of its life (SLICESTALL1)

- **Symptom:** the owner reported work in a workspace looking stuck. On the install, the window's `sessions` slice still held a
  driven session as *working* 90 minutes after the service ended it (timed out, then carried on and completed). It held no record
  created after about 05:02 UTC, while the `quests` slice beside it was current to the minute. The service's own answer of the
  same records was right, and the machine log said nothing about the slice.
- **Root cause:** `StateSlice.JudgeAsync` (`Platform/StateSlices.cs`) took every `OperationCanceledException` from its read for the
  worker's own stop, and `RunAsync` caught one only when its token was cancelled.
  - The sessions slice reads the service through `DriverHttp`, whose `HttpClient` times out at 30 s by throwing
    `TaskCanceledException`.
  - The machine was under heavy load at the time, with four builders and the gates beside the install. One answer past 30 s
    therefore left `RunAsync` as a faulted task that `StateSlices.RunAsync`'s `Task.WhenAll` never observes alone.
  - So the slice stopped judging, its wakes went unread, and every window kept what it last held. A throw past the read
    (`Moved`, `Tell`) would have ended it the same way.
- **Fix:**
  - A judgement's failure now includes any cancellation that is not the worker's stop: said once until one succeeds, with what
    was judged kept.
  - Each turn of the worker (a judgement, the manifest) runs through `SurvivingAsync`. That says anything thrown past the
    judgement, once until a turn succeeds, and goes on to the next wake.
- **Verification:**
  - `StateSlicesTests.A_read_that_times_out_is_a_failed_judgement_and_the_worker_judges_again_at_the_next_wake` and
    `A_judgement_that_throws_past_its_read_is_said_once_and_the_worker_goes_on` failed on the old code: the first at once, the
    second hung to its bound because the worker had ended. Both pass with the fix.
  - The modules' fast half passed, 2242 of 2242.
  - An installed window held by this fault is freed by a restart, and the next release carries the fix.

## 2026-10-22 — Ask Daoris's *Go there* answered that its plan changed once its quest was taken (ASKQUESTS1)

- **Symptom:** reported to the steward from ASKDISMISS1's build: a go card about a quest Ask Daoris had published, pressed after a
  session took the quest, answered that the plan had changed and applied nothing; pressed again on the card drawn anew, it went.
- **Root cause:** a go card's sentence says where its quest, ask or session stands (ASKDISMISS1 adds *taken*), and the card's
  revision is a digest of that sentence (HELPAPPLY1), so a take moves the plan the Apply judges. The cards were asked only when an
  Apply or a Not now published `help`, or every 4 s in a window with no bus, so the card on the window stood for the plan before
  the take, and `HELP_APPLY` answered `changed`, as it must for a plan the person did not see. Reasoned from the code; the window
  was not looked at.
- **Fix:** while a go card is shown, the proposals are asked again at each push that moves a quest's status, an ask's state or its
  quests, or a session's state (`useStandingsMark` in `data/queries.ts`, read only while the quests, asks and sessions are pushed,
  never a pull and never on a clock). The conversation's list of what it published (ASKQUESTS1) opens a quest with no judge at all.
- **Verification:** `AskDaoris.test.tsx`'s *draws a go card again when a push moves where a quest stands*, seen failing with the
  redraw taken out, then green; it holds that no quest or ask list was pulled.

## 2026-10-22 — The start that lost the race for its run's binding read the winner's as unread and held (BINDRACE1)

- **Symptom:** `WorkflowRunBindingTests.Two_starts_of_one_run_at_once_both_take_under_one_binding` (FABRIC-CUTOVER1g) failed in
  every full driver fast half run beside other builders on 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22, the install's own build among them, with
  `[Bound, Unread]` where both starts should take under one binding. It passed alone every time. On a machine, two starts of one run
  at once could hold the second as if its binding did not read.
- **Root cause:** a reader's share mode, not a missing or partial file. Windows' move (`File.Move`, MoveFileEx) opens the file it
  moves for deletion and closes it only after the file is in place, so for a moment the binding is there and whole and still held.
  The losing start reads it in exactly that moment: its own bind finds the file there (`WorkflowRunFiles.Bind`), and its read
  (`WorkflowRunFiles.Read`) opened it through `File.ReadAllText`, which shares reading only. Windows refused it with a sharing
  violation, the read answered null, and the start said `Unread` and held. Under load the loser lands in that moment far more often.
  - A probe of `File.Move` without overwriting beside a reader waiting for the file and reading it as it appeared, under one spinning
    thread per core in the probe's own process, refused 478 reads of 700 through `File.ReadAllText`, every one error 32 (sharing
    violation), none missing. Sharing deletion, none of 700 was refused.
  - The product's two starts in a loop, each pair's reads of the chain released together as the test releases them, came to
    `[Bound, Unread]` in 45 rounds of 300 under that load, and in none of 300 without it.
  - `KeptVersions` and arming's `GraphRuns` read the same files the same way. A refused read named no version, so a workflow saved
    past its newest 20 in that moment could drop the version a run had just bound, and the run was missing from that look's graph runs.
- **Fix:** `AtomicFile.ReadText` reads a file sharing its writing and deletion with a writer, as `KeepLock`, `HeavySlot` and
  `QuestionFiles` already read theirs. Every read of a binding goes through it: `WorkflowRunFiles`' `Read`, `AnyNamed` and
  `KeptVersions`, and `GraphRuns`. The writer is unchanged. A retry would only wait out the same refusal, which sharing deletion never
  meets. `File.Replace` needs a file already there, so it cannot create a first binding without overwriting, and its own handle is
  held the same way. The binding is created without a lock and its writer takes none, so a lock on the read would make every gate's
  read wait on writes for nothing.
- **Verification:** the tests hold a file as the move does (`MoveHold`, a handle open for deletion that shares everything). Three
  new tests were seen failing before the change, two at runtime and one as a compile error.
  - `WorkflowRunBindingTests.A_start_reads_the_binding_its_move_into_place_still_holds` reads it as unread before the fix. The
    kept versions of the held run are empty.
  - `A_graph_run_is_found_while_the_move_into_place_still_holds_its_binding` finds no graph run.
  - `AtomicFileTests.A_file_is_read_whole_while_its_move_into_place_still_holds_it` fails to compile, and each test also holds that
    `File.ReadAllText` is refused in that moment.
  - After the change, the product's loop came to `[Bound, Already]` in 1300 of 1300 rounds under the same load.
  - `WorkflowRunBindingTests` passed 20 runs of 20 in a loop, 16 of 16 each, and the driver's fast half passed 13288 of 13288.

## 2026-10-22 — Dismissing Ask Daoris's card about a quest it had published was told to the agent as the person's word (ASKDISMISS1)

- **Symptom:** the owner, using Daoris: after applying a proposal that published a quest, the conversation showed a card about
  that quest with a press to go to it; pressing its other button did something to the quest, which a session had already taken,
  where the person only wanted the card gone.
- **Root cause:** that card is a `go` proposal (`Open Quests → quest …`, *Go there*), and its other press was *Not now*, every
  kind's. The page sent `HELP_DISMISS` (`AskConversation.tsx`, `useSettleHelp`), which settled the card `dismissed` and said
  "Not now: the person did not apply `#<id>`." into the conversation in the person's words (`HelpRoutes.HelpDismissAsync`). That
  started a turn in which the agent could take the press for the person's word on the quest the card named, and act on it. A go
  changes nothing (HELP6), so there was nothing for the press to answer. The card also never said the quest was taken: a go's
  sentence named done, declined and closed only.
- **Fix:** `HelpProposals.Dismiss` settles the card and tells the conversation nothing for a `go`; a change's *Not now* is still the
  person's answer (D89). The route says nothing for a go. The page words a go's second press *Dismiss* (移除, a notice's word for
  taking something out of a list), never *Not now*. A go to a taken quest says `, taken`, and one to an ask names its taken quest.
  The room tells the helper that a go card's dismiss tells it nothing.
- **Verification:** seen failing first, then green: `HelpGoProposalsTests` (the dismiss, and the taken quest and ask rows),
  `HelpRoomMayProposeTests`, `DriverModuleHelpTests.Dismissing_a_go_card_settles_it_and_tells_the_conversation_nothing`,
  `ProposalCard.test.tsx` (three cases) and `AskDaoris.test.tsx`'s dismiss case. The last presses *Dismiss* and holds that the
  page sends one `HELP_DISMISS`, no Apply, no words and no quest's or ask's route, and that the card leaves. No window was looked at.

    The terminal's verb still acts on them until POOL1b.
  - The two Process cases pressed the refused `profile-default`. The order Ask Daoris's door writes is now whole, and a raw-laid
    workspace default is folded before its next edit.
  - `ACCOUNTS` came to answer `pooled` (§5.2), but the accounts slice did not class it, so the push dropped what the pull answered.
- **Fix:**
  - `AccountsStateSlice.AgentFields` pushes `pooled`.
  - The both-ways comparison spells a receipt's id and moment, and the ten one-set rows moved to a case that holds the route's
    refusal with nothing written; POOL1b returns them.
  - ROSTER1's case edits the set's order where it set a default.
  - The workspace-default case now holds the refusal, set or cleared, with nothing written.
  - Ask Daoris's order case expects the order whole and the raw default folded.
- **Verification:** the four classes green. The two Process cases ran filtered with `process.runsettings`. The modules' and the
  driver's fast halves are green.

## 2026-10-22 — The agents' text table on `main` still held the account files as written before the fold (POOL1a1)

## 2026-10-22 — A crashed swap was rolled back outside the home's lease (SWAPLEASE2)

- **Symptom:** none seen; found reading HOMELEASE1 against the RPC design's §5. A launcher putting back a swap a dead launcher left
  (`swapping`, or `started` with nothing running), at its start or after its own error, moved `app/` holding no lease, so a verb the
  install carries could start alone from a folder half put back.
- **Root cause:** HOMELEASE1 (`Daoris.Desktop.Launcher/Program.cs`) took the lease around `InstallSwap.Run` alone; `Recover`, and
  `AfterError` through it, ran before and after it.
- **Fix:** `InstallSwap.Recover` takes `LeaseHome`'s lease as a swap before it undoes a journal, reading the journal again under it;
  an act holding it past the wait leaves the journal and says who (`HeldBy`), and the launcher starts nothing on `app/` and says so.
  Finishing a confirmed swap moves nothing and takes none. D171's SWAPLEASE2 note.
- **Verification:** `StagedBuildTests.A_crashed_swaps_roll_back_holds_the_homes_lease_and_moves_nothing_under_a_verbs_hold` (every
  move back made while the swap holds the lease; nothing moved under a verb's) and `Only_a_roll_back_waits_for_the_homes_lease`;
  `InstallHomeTests.The_launchers_recovery_holds_the_installs_home_lease` reads both of the launcher's recoveries.

## 2026-10-22 — A verb and the loop took the home's lease in two homes when the driver's config was named elsewhere (LEASEHOME2)

- **Symptom:** none seen on an install, which names no override; found after HOMELEASE1. With `DAORIS_DRIVER_CONFIG` naming a file
  outside `DAORIS_HOME` (the family rehearsal's scratch does), a terminal's verb never met a headless loop's lease,
  nor the loop the verb's, and a verb writing the config's home held another home, so what only the lease's holder writes there
  (`HomeLease.HeldHere`, a recovery's drop) was refused it.
- **Root cause:** HOMELEASE1 (`5a5bee786`) took a verb's lease in `DaorisHome.Resolve()`, while the loop, the desktop and every door
  derive their home from the config's folder (`DriverConfig.HomeOf`, CONFIGSEAM1); the two agree only where the config is
  `DAORIS_HOME`'s own.
- **Fix:** `DriverConfig.FindHome` names the config's folder, found without reading or making anything, and the host takes a verb's
  lease there (`Driver.Host/Program.cs`). D171's LEASEHOME2 note says which families that write `DAORIS_HOME` itself it leaves.
- **Verification:** `DriverHostTests.With_the_config_elsewhere_a_verb_takes_the_lease_in_the_home_the_loop_drives`, seen failing
  before the host's change (the verb wrote the config's home and held `DAORIS_HOME`), green after; `ConfigSeamTests` holds the
  resolution to the loop's lease file in each environment.

## 2026-10-22 — Two starts of one run could each write its binding, the second over the first (FABRIC-CUTOVER1g)

- **Symptom:** none seen on an install; found by the cutover design's second reads (D190, design §13 row 29). Starts run beside one
  another, so two quests of one run starting together could each bind it, and the run kept whichever binding was written last, which
  a choice or a version saved between the two would make another workflow than the first start took under.
- **Root cause:** `WorkflowRunFiles.Bind` asked whether the run's file was there and then wrote it through `AtomicFile.WriteText`,
  which replaces a file: a check, then a write over whatever landed between the two. Both binds answered that they had written.
- **Fix:** the binding is written beside and moved into place without overwriting (`AtomicFile.TryCreateText`, the shape `HomeLease`,
  `KeepLock` and `HomeIdentity` already create theirs in): exactly one write lands, every other answers that the run was bound already,
  and the start's bind (`WorkflowRunStart.AtStartAsync`) then reads the binding that landed and takes under it.
- **Verification:** `WorkflowRunBindingTests`: eight binds of one run released together by a barrier, ten rounds, leave exactly one
  written and the file whole as that one wrote it, with no file left beside; two starts of one run whose reads of the chain meet take
  under one binding, one made and one read. Both were seen failing before the change (all eight wrote; both starts made one).

## 2026-10-22 — A full set's gates that died of the machine's memory were read as the change's failures (MEMGATE1)

- **Symptom:** a full set (`--full --beside`) ran on a 64 GB Windows machine whose commit limit was about 80 GB, beside the install
  with five or more driven sessions and two or three builder agents. The universal gate's sensitive scan threw
  `OutOfMemoryException`, `web-rules` died with "cannot allocate memory" and a `DataCloneError` "out of memory", and the family
  rehearsal's landing printed "Out of memory." twice. The deployment rehearsal's start after a restart timed out. Each was reported
  as the change's failure, and each passed when run later on a calmer machine.
- **Root cause:** the merge tool started each gate whatever the machine held, and read a gate's death of memory as any other failure:
  a FAIL, which stopped the run, or for a rehearsal that reported failed checks, a failure never run again. Nothing it printed said
  memory.
- **Fix:** `tools/merge-branch.mjs` reads the machine's free commit and free physical memory before a heavy gate (`readMemory`: on
  Windows `Win32_OperatingSystem`'s FreeVirtualMemory and FreePhysicalMemory). While either is below the gate's need (`MEMORY_NEEDS`
  by class, or `"memoryGb"` on the gate), it waits up to ten minutes and says so (`memoryGate`); a light gate is never read for. A gate
  whose log or exit shows a death of memory (`memoryDeath`) reads MEMORY and stops nothing. Once both lanes have ended it runs again
  once, alone, after waiting for its memory (`againOfMemory`): a pass is a FLAKE of memory, which the summary names as the machine's;
  a second death of memory fails, still named as memory. A Process half's named tests that died of memory run alone after the same wait.
- **Verification:** 11 new tests in `src/Daoris.Cli/tool-test/merge-branch.test.ts`, each seen failing before the change. A stand-in
  reader short of memory delays a heavy gate and says why. Every sign is classed as memory and run again once, after the gate beside it
  ended. A second death reads MEMORY, a light gate is never read for, and a run a failure stopped runs none again. The whole file and
  `tsc -p src/Daoris.Cli --noEmit` pass. The deployment rehearsal's timeout printed no sign of memory: it is waited for before it starts
  (10 GB), and is not read as memory when it times out.

## 2026-10-21 — The person's words to a quest's sessions around an ask-and-wait never reached a run (SAYHELD1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, a driven session ended waiting on another repository's answer (D79), and the person wrote to it. Once
  the answer came, the quest resumed in a new session whose opening and events never held their words: they stayed on the first
  record, unread. That session parked to ask a go-ahead, and the person answered the park. Nothing went on for hours, though the
  go-ahead was later refused (none waited) and no account was cooling. No plan action, start or reopen was logged for it.
- **Root cause:** the service names the question a taken quest waited on (`awaits`) until the quest closes (`QuestLog`), and the
  driver read that field alone as a wait. (B) `Planner.WordsOn` planned nothing for a quest naming one, so the park's answer was
  never taken up. The quest fell to D79's resume branch, whose `Consider` found the park itself among the active sessions and sat it
  `RepositoryBusy` (*session … is already working on …*). The go-ahead held nothing. The start read the same field too:
  `ResumesOwn`, the continuation's guard, `carryingOn` and the answer's read. Had the planner planned the park, the start would have
  opened a third session. (A) MSG1b left words to a waiting quest's session on that record until its resume, and the resume opened a
  new session without handing them. Only a fallback's carry-on hands words on (`HandedOnAsync`), and the asker, superseded by the new
  session, was never planned again.
- **Fix:** `Planner.ResumedOnAnswer`: a quest whose question has left the open list and whose last session here is a park was resumed
  on its answer, since a session that asks ends `completed`. It waits on nothing: the park's words go on in its own conversation, and
  its resume is not planned again. A record already left so goes on at the next look by itself. The start's reads of `awaits` yield to
  words going on. The D79 resume reads the asker's words as they stand (SAIDBACK1f) and hands the person's and Daoris's to the new
  session (`SessionTarget.Handed`): quoted beneath the answer in the `written-to` section, shown under their ids after the target, and
  taken off the asker naming it. The asker's conversation says where they went (`went`, reason `resumed`, worded in both catalogues).
  A resumed park is told which of its go-aheads still wait and that their acts are not yet its own (`GoAheadsText.Resumed`).
- **Verification:** red before, green after: `SessionMessagesPlanTests` (the answered park after a resume read `RepositoryBusy`),
  `AskAndWaitPromptTests` (the resume's instruction and opening), `GoAheadsHandedTests` (the waiting go-ahead said), and two real
  ticks in `SessionMessagesTickTests`. In A, the words reach the resume's prompt and events and are taken off the asker naming it. In
  B, the park's own conversation resumes with the answer and the quest closes. Both tick rows were seen failing on the same lines.

## 2026-10-21 — A window on one workspace counted another workspace's sessions to review (NEEDSSCOPE1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, two windows on one home, each scoped to its own workspace. One window's title bar and taskbar
  (`nav.waiting`) said three things waited on the person; they were another workspace's sessions placed *To review*, and that
  window's *What needs you* listed none of them.
- **Root cause:** `NeedsAPerson` gave a row a `workspace` only where it was judged from the service's sessions, quests or asks (an
  intake, a proposal, a go-ahead, a departure, a set-up, a park, an unanswerable quest). A row reached through the driver's own lists or
  the groups slice was built without one, though each is one session's, quest's or ask's: a review, an opinion, a parked quest, a
  helper's ask, a held call, a held answer, a unit's clean-up, a held attempt, an unreadable node record, a partial close; and the
  Sessions badge's parked quest. `useAttention` keeps a row with no workspace in every window, which is right for the machine's rows
  alone, so every window counted those rows whatever its scope. Why that window's list showed none of the three was not found in the
  code: the bell, the taskbar's count, *Notifications*' band and Overview's summary all read the same scoped rows. The taskbar's count
  is the first main window's alone until NOTIFY2c, whichever window is in front.
- **Fix:** each of those rows carries its record's workspace, from the record in hand (a unit's by its quest, its ask or its session);
  a rule carries the workspace its change reaches, a folder's trust and an account's wait the one their holds share. A terminal's
  press, a machine rule, an account, a unit no record owns, and a row whose record is not in hand carry none, each with its reason, so
  every window shows them. The page's counts and lists read one `needsListed`.
- **Verification:** `AttentionStateSliceTests`: the review, parked-quest, helper, permission, answer and folder shapes, the badge's parked
  quest and the new scope case red before (7 failed), green after with the machine case (90 and `AccountAttentionSliceTests`' 36). Web:
  `needsListed`'s case red before; `sessionsBadge.test.tsx`'s window on one workspace counts and lists its own and the machine's rows on
  the bell, the taskbar and Sessions' badge and never another's, and a window on every workspace counts them all.
## 2026-10-21 — Three censuses on `main` broken by merges that passed their own gates (GENREGEN1, FABRIC-CLOSE1d3, LANDBACKLOG1)

- **Symptom:** the full set on `main` failed `NoConsoleWindowTests` and `EveryChildIsHandedTheToolsTests` (driver),

- **Root cause:** GENREGEN1's `GeneratedWriters.Shell` set `CreateNoWindow` after its initializers and never handed the tools'
  environment, so a writer ran whatever `node` the PATH it inherited found; its merge was committed under another change's message,
  so the merge's own gates never ran. FABRIC-CLOSE1d3 made the page's quest list read `reopened`, which the quests slice still named
  the pull's alone, so the list never received it. LANDBACKLOG1's test called `tool.backlogOf` without declaring it in the test's
  typed import. Each passed the gates its merge ran; the full set caught all three.
- **Fix:** the writer's shell says `CreateNoWindow` in each initializer and is handed the tools (TOOLS5); `reopened` is pushed with
  the quest; the import declares `backlogOf`.

## 2026-10-21 — A landing whose replay conflicted only in the backlog was refused, and its session sent to rebase (LANDBACKLOG1)

- **Symptom:** replaying a branch's work onto `main` conflicted in `TASKS.md` alone, and the landing was refused with the rebase words.
  In this repository each session archives its own row, so nearly every landing touches the backlog, and under LANDREBASE1 most would
  cost the session a turn over rows the merge tool settles by itself.
- **Root cause:** LANDREBASE1's replay (`BranchReplays.RebaseTakingGeneratedAsync`) went on past a stop only where every conflicted file
  was marked generated; anything else was the session's conflict. The merge tool had learned the backlog's rule (MERGETASKS1), the
  landing had not, and the two shared no code to learn it from.
- **Fix:** D87's LANDBACKLOG1 note. A stop whose conflict is the backlog the line declares, alone or beside generated files, is merged
  by its base (`BacklogMerge`) and staged by its blob; the plan's trial does the same over objects. The rule is a twin of the merge
  tool's, both held to `backlog-merges.json`.
- **Verification:** `LandBacklogLandingTests.A_conflict_only_in_the_declared_backlog_is_settled_by_its_base_and_lands_replayed`, red
  before (refused with *Merge conflict in docs/backlog.md*, and the plan named it), green after; the edited-twice, beside-code and
  session-declared cases refused; `BacklogMergeTests` and `merge-branch.test.ts` on the table.
## 2026-10-21 — A terminal's press confirmed past its time still ran when its timer fired late (NOTIFY2a)

- **Symptom:** found by Codex's read of the notification design (D196, its finding 2.5) and the steward's check (S1), never seen on
  the install. A Confirm pressed after a press's two minutes ran the press if the timer that ends it had not fired yet, and a window's
  word that the card was shown, past the press's ten minutes to be found, gave it two more. The bound the card states was not the bound
  kept.
- **Root cause:** `PipeConfirmations` read the clock only in the timer's firing (`End(…, due: true)`); `Answer` and `Show` took the
  press as waiting while it was in the list, and `Show` returned early for a card shown before without reading the clock. A pool
  under load runs a timer late, so the list held a press past its time.
- **Fix:** D196's NOTIFY2a note. `End` reads the clock for every answer: one at or past `Expires` ends the press `Expired` and is
  answered `gone`. `Show` reads it first, before its early return, and ends a press past its time alike. The card toasts the refusal,
  since the press's end takes the card away before its answer returns.
- **Verification:** `PipeConfirmationsTests` (seven cases) and `PipeConfirmTests`' late Confirm over the pipe, on a `HeldClock` whose
  `Pass` moves time and holds every timer late, failed before the fix (each `Answer` or `Show` past the time answered true) and pass
  after; `DriverModulePersonTests` and `SessionBalloonTests` stay green; `Confirmations.test.tsx`'s toast cases failed and pass in en
  and zh.

## 2026-10-21 — A running session's *Who it worked with* stood eleven times over on its page (RELSPAM1)

- **Symptom:** on an installed window for another workspace, a driven session on an ask, working, showed its folded relations line
  (*Who it worked with · asked by ask #… · Show who it worked with*) eleven times, one copy under another. The count grew while the
  session ran, and moving to another session left the copies in place.
- **Root cause:** a parent's keys are one namespace across all its slots, not only within a list. `AttendedSession` keyed both
  `SessionRelations` (HEADFIT1) and `WorkMilestone` (MILESTONEUX1) by `session.id` alone, both added 2026-10-20. Any falsy slot
  before them (no parts, no entry Accept, a one-stop chain) sends React's reconcile to its key map, where the milestone's old fiber
  overwrote the fold's under the shared key. The new fold was matched to the milestone's fiber, a type mismatch, so a fresh fold
  was mounted; the old fold was in no map and never deleted, so its DOM stayed. One copy per draw of the record, folded each time.
  The Work frame's foot had the same collision since WAITFOOT1b: `WaitStrip` and the chat `Composer` were keyed `attended.id`,
  and `SentSettler` by the same id held as `sending.lateTo`. A settler leaving, or a move between two conversations, left a fiber
  behind: the settler's events reader, or the old session's strip.
- **Fix:** each keyed child says what it is beside the id (`relations:`, `milestone:`, `parts:` in the record; `strip:`,
  `settler:`, `composer:` at the foot). `design/siblingKeys.test.ts` reads every shipped `.tsx` with the TypeScript parser and fails
  on two slots of one parent keyed alike, the branches of one condition being one slot. Its sabotaged cases show it catching what
  it should.
- **Verification:** `AttendedSession.test.tsx`'s new case (ten redraws of a running session with relations and a milestone, then a
  move) and `WorkFrame.landed.test.tsx`'s (a driven session on a quest an intake published, its record changed ten times) each saw
  11 regions before the fix and 1 after. `siblingKeys.test.ts` named the record's and the foot's collisions before, and passes
  after. `WorkFrame.test.tsx`, `WorkFrame.words.test.tsx`, `DetachedSession.test.tsx`, `SessionRelations.test.tsx` and
  `work/waits` are green.

## 2026-10-21 — A resource location another writer added while one wrote `tools.json` was lost (PUSH1f2c)

- **Symptom:** found building PUSH1f2c, the alone-path design §1.4's audit of `tools.json`'s writers. Two writers of the resource
  locations at once (a terminal's `daoris tool locations add` beside the window's Tools place) could each succeed and one location
  be gone: the second wrote the list as it had read it.
- **Root cause:** KEEPALL1c's keeping write takes the file's keep lock over its re-read and its rename, but `Tools.SetWay`,
  `AddLocation` and `RemoveLocation` read the file and decided their edit before it. `locations` is an array, which the keeping write
  writes whole, so the edit carried the stale list over the other writer's.
- **Fix:** D173's PUSH1f2c note. Each writer takes `KeepLock.Take` before its read and writes through `JsonKeeping.SaveHolding`, the
  keeping write for a holder, so another writer waits its turn and finds the file as this one left it.
- **Verification:** `ToolsTests.A_change_another_writer_makes_while_this_one_writes_is_kept`, red before for an added and a removed
  location (the other's lost), green after; `ToolsTests`, `HomeFilesKeepTests`, `KeepLockTests`, `ToolInstallTests` and
  `ToolActionsTests` green.

## 2026-10-21 — Wiring a workspace deleted what `remotes.json`'s writers did not know, and the page wrote over a torn map (KEEPALL1e)

- **Symptom:** named by KEEPALL1's audit (D173's KEEPALL1 note). Wiring or unwiring a workspace, at Settings or with
  `daoris remote add|remove`, rewrote `remotes.json` as `{ workspace: { url, key } }` sorted by name: every other top-level key, an
  entry's own unknown keys, an entry missing half its pair and CRLF went. At Settings, over a map that did not read, the page's
  entry was written alone and every other workspace's key was lost; the CLI already refused that.
- **Root cause:** `RemotesModule` rebuilt the dictionary `RemoteTarget.LoadFile` parsed and wrote it with `RemoteTarget.Save`; the
  CLI's `writeRemotes` wrote the `Map` its reader parsed. Both readers keep only whole pairs, and the driver's reads a torn file as
  no remotes.
- **Fix:** D173's KEEPALL1e note. Both edit the file as it stands (`RemoteFile`, `readRemoteFile`) and write through the keeping
  write (`JsonKeeping.Save`, `writeKeeping`); the page says a refusal as `DRIVER_REFUSED`. The service's `RemoteConfig` writes
  nothing, and reads what they write.
- **Verification:** ten `remotes:` rows in `home-files-keep.json`, each with the map the readers read, through `HomeFilesKeepTests`,
  `homefileskeep.test.ts` and the service's `RemoteConfigKeepTests`; `RemotesModuleTests`' new case (unknown keys kept, a torn map
  refused and untouched) holds what the old writer broke. `RemoteTargetTests`, `SyncStateSliceTests`, `RemoteConfigTests`, `homefiles.test.ts`,
  `remotes.test.ts` (its order row re-decided) and `dogfood.test.ts` green.

## 2026-10-21 — A session that committed its work and failed before its take was built again from nothing (RETRYWORK1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, MERGEWEBRULES1 and FABRIC-PIPELINE1b2 were each built twice: the first session built and committed
  the row, failed, and the next session built it again in a new tree, about twice the tokens.
- **Root cause:** each first session failed only because its connector could not start (QUESTOPENLOCK1), so it never took its
  quest. D80 carries on a cut-off of a take alone; an open quest's failed session was read as having done nothing, and the quest's
  next start was a first start, which grows a new tree from the line. Nothing asked whether the failed tree held commits.
- **Fix:** the look counts the commits beyond `baseCommit` in such a session's tree (`CommittedWork`), and the planner carries an
  open quest with any on in that tree (`Planner.RetriedFrom`, `Consideration.CarriesWork`), told to take the quest and finish the
  work with Daoris's brief of the line; the strikes still park it on the third failure. D80's RETRYWORK1 note.
- **Verification:** `RetryWorkTickTests` through real ticks (a session commits, fails on a closed quest door, and the next look
  carries it on in the same tree, its instruction naming the commit and the words, its record's note saying so); `PlannerTests`'
  RETRYWORK1 rows, `CommittedWorkTests`, `SessionGroupsTests`' row, `NoteSitesTests`' row and the `retried` golden.

## 2026-10-21 — An edit of `tools.json` or the browser's settings changed numbers, line endings or a key written twice (KEEPALL1c)

- **Symptom:** named by KEEPALL1's audit (D173's KEEPALL1 note). Choosing a tool's way or a resource location with `daoris tool`,
  or a browser setting with `daoris browser`, rewrote `1.50` as `1.5` and a number past 2^53 as its neighbour; the same edits at
  Settings wrote a CRLF file in LF; and both twins edited a file holding a key twice, the driver's reader failing on it first.
- **Root cause:** these writers already edited a node read at the write, so they kept unknown keys, but wrote it whole: the CLI
  from `JSON.parse`'s values, the driver from `JsonNode` with `JsonFile.Write`'s LF, neither through the keeping write the other
  home files took in KEEPALL1. `JsonNode` threw `ArgumentException` on a key written twice.
- **Fix:** D173's KEEPALL1c note. Both twins write both files through `JsonKeeping.Save` and `writeKeeping`; the driver's loads read
  a key written twice through `JsonKeeping.Once`, as `JSON.parse` does.
- **Verification:** eleven `tools.json` and `browser/settings.json` rows in `home-files-keep.json`: `homefileskeep.test.ts` all
  eleven, `HomeFilesKeepTests` the six tools rows (the twice row red on `ArgumentException` before the load's fix) and
  `BrowserSettingsTests` the five browser rows; `ToolsTests`, `ToolResourcesTests`, `ToolInstallTests`, `ToolsChildrenTests`,
  `BrowserModuleTests`, `tools.test.ts`, `resources.test.ts`, `toolinstall.test.ts` and `browser.test.ts` green.

## 2026-10-21 — A turn that ended just after its background command did parked on the person (BGWAIT3)

- **Symptom:** a driven session on the install backgrounded a test class, wrote that it would close its quest when the tests

- **Root cause:** the command ended about three seconds before the turn did, after the agent's last step, so the harness had not
  handed the agent the ending (its last words said the command still ran). The wire said the task ended, and BGWAIT1 waits only
  on work still running at the turn's end, so the session closed and parked five seconds later, before the harness's wake for
  that ending could come. The task frames had arrived: the record keeps none of them, so their absence there proved nothing.
- **Fix:** `AcpWake.Unseen` names an ending read after the agent's last step, after the last woken turn began and after Daoris's
  last go-on; a turn that ends on one waits for the woken turn, or sends the go-on after the quiet, where the quest would park.
  Every protocol-door session asks for `asyncTasks`, so the headless loop gets the frames too. D83's BGWAIT3 note.
- **Verification:** `AcpBackgroundTests`' install case (0.84.0's frames: the spawn at the call's result, the ending after the
  last step), the go-on told once and the quest that does not wait failed before the fix; the reshaped real-question case
  stays green. `AcpTests`' capabilities and task-frame cases failed before it.

## 2026-10-21 — A knowledge host exited at start with "database is locked" when sessions started together (QUESTOPENLOCK1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, eight driven sessions started within a minute, each with its own knowledge host over the one
  `knowledge.db`. Two hosts exited at start with `SqliteException: SQLite Error 5: 'database is locked'`, thrown from
  `SqliteDataRecord.Dispose` under `SqliteCommand.ExecuteScalar` at `QuestStore.EnsureSchemaAsync`'s version stamp. A session whose
  connector did not start had no quest tools: it committed its row but could neither take nor close its quest, and was recorded
  failed.
- **Root cause:** Microsoft.Data.Sqlite sets no SQLite busy handler; it waits out a busy lock (every 150 ms, up to the command
  timeout, 30 s here) only around a statement's first step. A write with a `RETURNING` clause, run on its own, writes at that first
  step and returns its first row; its autocommit commit runs when the reader ends (`sqlite3_reset` in the record's dispose), which
  is not retried. The file keeps a rollback journal (no `journal_mode` is set; `delete`), so that commit needs an exclusive lock,
  and any other host's read under way answers it busy at once; SQLite then rolls the write back. The stamp is such a write at every
  open, added by CLOSETAKE1/QUESTSTOREVER1 (660d4b545). Two other writes were the same: a channel post's `RETURNING urgent`
  (COWORK1d, ec0d27c60) and a registration's `RETURNING workspace, default_branch, lanes` (older).
- **Fix:** each runs in the connection gate's write transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), whose `BEGIN` and `COMMIT` are first steps the
  driver waits on: `QuestStore.EnsureSchemaAsync`'s stamp, `ChannelStore.KeepAsync` and `RegistrationStore.UpsertAsync`. The four
  quest-log and take-bind writes already ran in the caller's transaction. A source scan in `ConnectionGateTests` refuses a
  `RETURNING` write whose member neither takes nor opens a transaction. D173's QUESTOPENLOCK1 note.
- **Verification:** `ReturningLockTests`: another host holds a read for half a second while the quest store opens (once, and on four
  connections at once), a channel post and a registration are written; each waits and is kept. Red before the fix with the
  install's own stack (four of six; the driver pin and the publish guard green), green after. The scan named exactly the three
  sites on the old stores. `QuestStoreTests`, `ChannelTests`, `RegistrationStoreTests`, `QuestTakeBindTests`, `QuestLogTests` and the
  other classes over these stores green, with the HTTP host's channel and registry classes.

## 2026-10-21 — A terminal that was not elevated could not press into an elevated Daoris (PIPEOWNER1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, which runs elevated, `daoris-driver sessions say` from a terminal that was not elevated was
  refused at once, saying the running Daoris's pipe *did not answer within 5 seconds*. Its reads went alone without a word.
- **Root cause:** the pipe's descriptor named no owner, so it took the creating token's default owner, which for an elevated
  token is the Administrators group. The client opened with `PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly`, which compares the pipe's owner with the
  caller's token's default owner, the user's SID when not elevated, and refused it (`UnauthorizedAccessException`, about 50 ms);
  the ACL let the same process in, in 1 ms. `ConnectAsync` returned null for that refusal as for a timeout, so it was said as
  silence.
- **Fix:** `InstancePipe.Security` owns the pipe by the user's SID. The driver's client reads the owner itself, taking the user's
  SID or its token's default owner: with the server's change alone, `CurrentUserOnly` refused every elevated client instead (the
  modules' pipe tests did so under elevated PowerShell). A refused connect (an ACL that refuses the user, or an owner not taken)
  is `InstanceFound.Refused`, *… refused this terminal; nothing was done. Its pipe belongs to another Windows account or
  elevation.* The CLI's client reads no owner; its connect the ACL refuses (`EPERM`) is said in the same words.
- **Verification:** `InstancePipeTests`' owner row failed under elevated PowerShell (owner `S-1-5-32-544`), then passed;
  `InstanceDoorTests`' three refused rows failed (two said *did not answer*, one pressed), then passed; `instance.test.ts`'s two
  failed the same way, then passed. `InstancePipeTests` and `PipeCensusTests` (77) and `InstanceDoorTests` (39) under both
  elevated PowerShell and Git Bash, the instance-path classes (109), `instance.test.ts` (29).

- **Fix:** the driver's fix, written with the service's own code (the twins rule): each line seeks to the file's end under the
  mutex `Local\Daoris.MachineLog.<hash of its full path>`, waiting a second at most, a mutex left by a dead writer taken on. A

## 2026-10-21 — The change stream's and the help start's claims were timed on the machine's clock (TESTCLOCK3, TESTCLOCK1)

- **Symptom:** TESTCLOCK1 left ten elapsed bounds in the modules' and the service's tests as they were. Each compared a `Stopwatch`
  with a few seconds (500 ms to 10 s): "answered at once", "woken", "the stop answers a held wait", "the start does not wait for a
  line". A loaded machine could fail any of them, and widening one would let the defect it guards pass.
- **Root cause:** the claim was measured as the machine's time, not as what the code waited on. `ChangeStream` read a wait's bound
  off `Stopwatch`, so no test could hold it.
- **Fix:** `ChangeStream.OpenAsync` takes a `clock`, a `TimeProvider` used for a wait's bound only. The sampler's paces stay on the
  machine's clock, since they set how often it looks and bound no wait. The local host passes the clock its services hold, so it
  opens the stream after the build. `ChangeStreamTests` hands it the service tests' `MovedClock`, which stands still:
  - the bootstrap, the moves before the ask and the ninth wait are answers at all, within `Poll.Patience`;
  - the woken wait names its family without timing the wake;
  - the 400 ms wait is answered only once the clock passes it, and not 1 ms before;
  - the ninth wait that never queues is asked while the test holds the sampler (`HoldSamplerAsync`, standing in for a writer's lock).
  The HTTP tests' `MovableClock` (now its own file) moves its timestamp and holds its timers. A `HeldChangesHost` fixture hands it
  to `ChangeStreamHostTests`. The real host in `ChangeStreamProcessTests` runs on the machine's clock, so its wake and its stop are
  judged against the wait's own 30 s end, counted from the ask, where the test's own 5 s and 10 s bounds read the machine's load.
  `DriverModuleHelpStartTests`' line judge never answers and has no bound (`Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`). A start that waited for it
  would never end, where the rules' 30 s would have let it end late.
- **Verification:** `ChangeStreamTests` (48), the three HTTP classes with `ConfirmationTests` (24) and `DriverModuleHelpStartTests` (8)
  were green alone, then three runs of each at once (about 1 m 55 s). Not run: the whole projects.

## 2026-10-21 — Two machine logs on one day's file overwrote each other's lines (MACHINELOGAPPEND1, ONEINSTANCE2)

- **Symptom:** ONEINSTANCE2 measured that of two `MachineLog`s on one file, the second's line was gone after the first's next,
  so a later desktop launch's line (the guard's warning as it exits) could be overwritten by the running instance's next.
- **Root cause:** `FileMode.Append` on Windows seeks to the end once, at the open, and the handle then writes at its own
  position; it is not an append-only handle. A second writer's lines sat where the first's next went.
- **Fix:** each line seeks to the file's end before it is written, under a mutex named for the file (`Local\Daoris.MachineLog.`
  and a hash of its full path) that every writer of it takes, so the seek and the write are one step across processes; a
  wait of a second at most, a mutex left by a dead writer taken on, and a writer that cannot open it still writing at the end.
  And the desktop's `app.Run()` runs through `MachineLog.RunWatched`, which writes the exception leaving it while the log is
  open (the `using` closes it as the exception leaves `Main`) and rethrows it; the unhandled handler skips that one.
- **Verification:** `MachineLogTests` (driver), 22, with two logs on one file in turn and from many threads at once keeping
  all their lines, the watched body's exception written once, and the desktop's `Program` running it so; the desktop app built.
  The service's twin keeps the old write (MACHINELOGAPPEND2).

## 2026-10-21 — A facts judgement cut at its bound was logged late, then as an error (FACTSLATE1)

- **Symptom:** under load the help room's facts (`help.trees`, `help.lines`, `help.work`, `help.sweep`) each wrote `facts.late`
  and then an `error` line, seventeen errors in a day on the install with nothing broken.
- **Root cause:** `MachineFacts.JudgeAsync` passes the judge a token cancelled at the bound. A judge that honours it throws
  `OperationCanceledException`, which only the stopping filter caught, so the bound's own cancellation fell to the catch-all
  and `Log.Failed` after the warning already said.
- **Fix:** a cancellation whose bounded token was cancelled ends as late: `facts.late` once (said there only where the judge
  ended before the bound's wait did), nothing landed, the fact kept as last judged; any other failure is still an error.
- **Verification:** `MachineFactsTests` (13), its new bound case failing on the old code with `facts.late`, `error`.

## 2026-10-21 — Landed session trees holding a test's scratch repository sat in *What needs you* as blocked cleanups (OVERVIEWNOISE1a)

  scratch git repository under the ignored `_fixtures/`; one checkout held 33 orphaned seed run folders.
- **Root cause:** the look's last guard kept any tree with a `.git` below its top (`TreeSetAside.NestedRepository`), though a tree
  holding only ignored paths is otherwise moved aside for 14 days, so a scratch repository under an ignored path kept the tree
  like one the tree's status cannot see. Two tests made such scratch and left it: GATESLIM1's "by default" case in
  `merge-branch.test.ts` never called `repo.cleanup()`, and `GitSeed` removed `_fixtures/seeds/<run>` only at the test host's
  exit, which a host killed at a session's timeout never reaches.
- **Fix:** the guard lists every nested repository, none read into, and asks `git check-ignore` of each: an ignored one goes
  aside with the tree, any other keeps it as before. The merge-branch case cleans up and asserts its folder is gone; `GitSeed`
  sweeps, at a run's start, every run folder whose host's process id no longer runs.
- **Verification:** `BranchTidyingProcessTests.A_repository_under_an_ignored_path_goes_aside_with_its_tree` and the existing
  nested case (2 passed), `BranchTidyingTests` and the ignored-paths case (71 passed), `GitSeedTests` (9 passed), the
  merge-branch GATESLIM1 case; the home-path, one-word and partials censuses.

## 2026-10-20 — A session whose quest closed while it waited on its background work worked on until the timeout (DONEEND1)

- **Symptom:** on the install two driven sessions went on working, showing *Stop…* and holding a slot of the cap, after their
  quests closed done, until the 90-minute timeout killed them (one 14 minutes after its close); the kill left a test's scratch in
  its tree.
- **Root cause:** `AcpSession.AfterBackgroundAsync` read the quest once, at the turn's end (`waits(ct)`, BGWAIT1), then blocked in
  `AcpBackground.EndedAsync` until every piece of background work ended. A quest closed during that wait, by the agent in a turn
  its harness woke for one piece while a long test run went on, was never read, so only the timeout's kill ended it. Behind it, a
  run that did end with its work still running closed the agent's stdin and waited on its exit bounded only by the timeout
  (`Driver.WaitAsync`), so an agent the work held alive would hold the run the same way.
- **Fix:** the background wait races a look (`QuestMovedAsync`): the same judgement read every `BackgroundLook` (every fourth
  driver tick), which once the quest no longer parks waits for no turn to run (`AcpWake.IdleAsync`) and ends the session, saying
  `background.wait-over`. An unread look keeps waiting. The capture gives an agent that leaves work running 10 s to exit, then ends
  its tree (`Driver.EndedLingeringAsync`), told to `AcpEnding` so the conclusion reads the session's clean end, not the kill's exit.
- **Verification:** `AcpBackgroundTests`, `BackgroundWaitJudgementTests`, `NoteCodesTests`, `AcpTests` (150 passed), the page's
  `note.test.ts` and `noteLines.test.ts`; `DoneEndTickTests` (Process) failed at its 90 s bound before the driver's half and
  passed in 28 s after it, the stand-in's test run ended with its tree.

## 2026-10-20 — Two fast tests timed by the wall clock failed under a loaded machine (FLAKE1)

- **Symptom:** the full set on 9717f8d failed `StagedBuildTests.A_file_held_in_app_for_a_moment_does_not_roll_the_swap_back`
  (the swap rolled back) and the rehearsal kit's "a command its timeout ends is ended with what it started" (the command never
  said its id within its timeout), with six of the install's sessions, three builders and the CI's own gates on the machine.
- **Root cause:** each gave the machine's clock a job the load could outlast. The swap test let go of its hold from a thread-pool
  task's 300 ms delay while the swap waited up to ten seconds on the test's own thread, and the pool was starved past the wait;
  the kit's test gave a fresh node five seconds to start and write its id, and a node start took longer.
