  already did, so it no longer reads the wall clock; the kit's test runs the command again with thirty seconds where the first
  five saw no id, and only then says nothing was asked.

## 2026-10-20 — The window's counts disagreed: the title kept an older count, the status bar counted the person's conversations (SESSBADGE1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, two captures ten minutes apart: the title read (5) while Overview's badge, from the same value, read
  4; the status bar read one more than the rail's working group, an Ask Daoris conversation idle between turns among its count.
- **Root cause:** the page tells the frame each *What needs you* count over `SET_BADGE` and waits for no answer
  (`useTaskbarCount`), and the window posts each to its own thread as the module hands it on (`MainForm.ShowWaiting`). Nothing held
  two counts told close together in the order they were told, so a 5 then a 4 could be worn as 4 then 5, the title keeping the
  older. Not proven on the window to be the case seen; no other path from one value to two readings was found. The status bar
  counted every active record of the sessions list (`liveSessions`, `SESSION_ACTIVE`), a rule of its own beside the cap's
  (CAPCOUNT1), and ASKRAIL1 took Ask Daoris out of the rail but not out of that count.
- **Fix:** each `SET_BADGE` carries an `order` later than the one before (`nextBadgeOrder` in `bridge/windows.ts`, the clock's
  milliseconds so a reloaded page tells later), and `WindowsModule` wears a count only under a lock and only where its order is
  later than the one worn. The status bar reads the attention slice's `working` partition, the sessions the driver runs by
  `ActiveSessions.HoldsSlot` judged in .NET, the count Sessions' badge shows (D76's SESSBADGE1 note).
- **Verification:** `WindowsModuleTests` (a count told before the one worn is not worn; forty told at once from as many threads
  end on the latest, each worn in order) and `windows.test.tsx` (each order later than the one before, within one millisecond),
  both seen failing first; `sessionsBadge.test.tsx`'s status bar case.

## 2026-10-20 — The full set's driver Process half failed a race's control and a start's git ceiling (TREELOCK1, FLAKE1)

- **Symptom:** the full set on 50634f5 failed two `Process` tests, each again when re-run alone: `ProbeRaceTests`' control (two
  status questions at once on an expired account sign it out) found the account still signed in, and `StartGitCountTests` counted
  14 git starts before a session spawned, over its ceiling of 12.
- **Root cause:** the control's stand-in agent waited a fixed 1.5 s after reading the credentials before spending the refresh
  token, so it raced only when both questions had read within that window; on the loaded machine the second node start came
  after the first had already rotated the tokens, and the second read fresh ones. The loser also signed out after a fixed 100 ms,
  which could land before the winner's write. The ceiling was not raised when TREELOCK1, built by a session of the owner's install,
  added a session's own lock at a start: it reads the tree's lock (`git worktree list --porcelain`) and takes it
  (`git worktree lock`), two starts; the session's run had been told to run filtered classes, and this one was not among them.
- **Fix:** the control's two questions meet (a `meet` file beside the script): each records its read and waits for the other's
  before spending, and the loser signs out once the winner's tokens have landed. The other cases leave the file out and keep the
  fixed wait. The ceiling is 14, its comment naming TREELOCK1's two starts.
- **Verification:** `ProbeRaceTests` and `StartGitCountTests`, 8 passed, alone and with the CI's load beside.

## 2026-10-20 — Idle conversations held the driver's cap, so quests started two at a time (CAPCOUNT1)

  driven quests started two at a time.
- **Root cause:** every site that spent a slot took the cap less `snapshot.Active.Count`, and `Active` is every active session the
  service lists, a person's conversations among them (`SessionLedger.HelpRepository`'s records and any chat). The list is right for
  a busy tree and a repository's holder; it was never the count of what the driver starts. The kind alone could not separate them

  marks, and `Snapshot.SlotsHeld` is the one count the planner's starts and a look's intakes, helpers, brainstorms and meetings read
  (D130's note). `Active` is unchanged. The help room's machine line says what the cap counts.
- **Verification:** `CapCountTests` (two idle Ask Daoris records at a cap of four start four quests; the table of record kinds;
  `/api/sessions` read for the marks), `CapCountTickTests` over the stand-in service, and one test per site in `HelperLookTests`,
  `BrainstormBoundsTests` and `MeetingTests`. Each site's test failed with the count made over every record and passed with it.

## 2026-10-20 — A start carried the quest and the record of the session its driver ran in (ENVLEAK1)

- **Symptom:** run from a session Daoris drives, three `AdapterTests` (a chat carries no quest, no target, no record unless

  brainstorm's, the repository and the service) before a start sets its own; `DAORIS_HOME`, the PATH and the rest still pass.

  with `HeavyRunProcessTests`, 64 passed; `A_start_drops_the_roles_it_inherits_and_keeps_the_rest` holds the list.

## 2026-10-20 — A resumed session whose tree was gone ran with its shell in the repository's checkout (TREEGONE1)

- **Symptom:** the session the merge tool's prune took a tree from (DOGFOOD1, the entry below) was resumed with the person's
  words, and its harness started with its shell in the repository's main checkout, the folder its tree had been made from.
  Its agent noticed and remade its tree itself before editing; nothing stopped it editing the checkout.
- **Root cause:** a start asked whether the session's tree stood by `Directory.Exists` alone (`ConversationTrees.Stands`,
  `Driver.RunAsync`'s `resumedIn` and `joinedIn`). A removal that leaves its folder (anything it could not delete) answers
  yes for a folder that is no tree, where git walks up to whatever holds it; and a tree truly gone made a resume grow a
  fresh tree from the line, its agent starting without the session's commits. Where exactly the harness's shell landed in
  the checkout was not reproduced here: the window's run was not instrumented.
- **Fix:** `TreeReturns.EnsureAsync` (D51's TREEGONE1 note), asked by `Driver.RunAsync` with the repository's trees held,
  before any resume, carry-on or further part goes on in a session's tree: listed by git, it goes on; its folder gone and its
  branch standing, the tree is made again in its place on that branch, a leftover folder moved aside first, and said
  (`tree.remade`); its branch gone too, or not makeable, the start is held and said once on the record (`tree.gone`,
  `tree.unmade`), and `DriverContinuations.ContinueAsync` is told the tree does not stand, so no conversation resumes
  anywhere else.
- **Verification:** `TreeReturnsTests` (Process, git) 5 passed; `SessionMessagesTickTests` 12 passed, three new: a removed
  tree made again with its commit and the resumed prompt's working folder the tree, a leftover folder moved aside and the
  tree made again, and a branch gone too held with no harness started over two looks; `NoteCodesTests`, `NoteSitesTests`
  and the web's `locales/note.test.ts` with the three codes in both languages.

  left and opened again, or its other place opened) on *Waiting for the tool to open the page…* for ever, so the code the tool
  waits on is never shown there. Codex's sign-in was reported not finishing on the install; whether this is why is not measured.
- **Root cause:** a harness action's relay (`AgentActions.Relay`) sent each line as `SESSION_OUTPUT` and kept none, and a panel
  catches up by `TAIL_SESSION`, which read only the sessions' buffers (`SessionOutput`), where `<harness>:<action>` has none: a
  late panel's tail was empty, and a tool that prints once has nothing later to show. Claude Code's flow hid it, since its
  browser opens by itself and the person needs no line from the panel. The stand-ins hid it too: Codex's printed only
  *Successfully logged in* and exited at once.
- **Fix:** `AgentActions` keeps each action's latest run's lines, bounded as a session's are, its numbers going on across runs,
  and `ConsoleRoutes`' `TAIL_SESSION` answers them for a key no session holds. Codex's stand-ins now print as 0.160.0 did and
  wait, reading no input, until the code is entered.
- **Verification:** `SignInPhasesTests` (modules, `Process`): with the faithful stand-in waiting, `TAIL_SESSION` for
  `codex-acp:login-new` answers the code line and the phases so far, and the sign-in keeps its account once the code is entered;
  `CodexAccountProcessTests` (driver) the same through `HarnessActions.LoginAsync`.
## 2026-10-20 — The merge tool's prune took a running Daoris session's tree (DOGFOOD1)

- **Symptom:** the first session the owner's install drove on this repository (HEAVYRUN1a3, DOGFOOD1) stopped mid-work and
  asked for a tree: its worktree under the install's home and its branch `daoris/s-…` were gone. Its only commands had been
  reads and `npm pack` in its own `_fixtures/`. The merge of ACCESSSWAP1b printed `removed daoris/s-… its worktree … and the
  branch` at the same minute.
- **Root cause:** a merge's prune removes every local branch merged into main with its unlocked, clean worktree. A Daoris
  session opens its tree on a branch at main's tip and has no commit until it has work, so its branch reads as merged; its
  tree is not locked. The prune's rules knew the agent harness's trees and its lock, not Daoris's, since no install drove this
  repository before.
- **Fix:** `pruneCandidates` holds a branch Daoris names (`daoris/` for a session, `quest/` for this repository's landings),
  with its worktree, as Daoris's own housekeeping's to remove. That Daoris locks a session's tree while the session holds it,
  so no tool takes it, is TREELOCK1.
- **Verification:** `merge-branch.test.ts`' new case and the two end-to-end prune cases, 4 passed; `--prune --plan` keeps
  `daoris/s-…` with that reason. The session was told and went on.

## 2026-10-20 — A lost done's follow-up stood everywhere, and a step whose session ran across the go-on never got its source's work (CLOSEREOPEN1)

- **Symptom:** shown red, never seen on an install (nothing binds there). B took a chain's parent and closed it done offline, and its
  done published the follow-up, while A's take of the parent reached the remote first: raced (A's take landing between B's fetch and
  its push), or plain with B's own take of the follow-up, the follow-up stood on the remote and every machine, its take B's, on a done
  that lost (`QuestSyncTests`' CLOSE1e2 theory, three of four cases red). And a step whose session was running when the person reopened
  its source and went on with it ended as a park after the go-on, so its branch never got the source's new submission.
- **Root cause:** CLOSE1c21's remote rule held back only a step naming the submission it grew from; a done's follow-up names none, so
  the remote numbered it while the parent was behind. The rebase's `ForgetFollowUpsAsync` forgot a follow-up only while its history was
  its one unpushed publication, so a take of it kept it and synced it on its own. The session's end judged the reopen only by the step
  held as it ended (`HeldByReopen`), and once gone on the step reads unheld, so the end was ordinary, its record later than the go-on,
  and neither CLOSE1c2's carry-on nor CLOSE1c13's telling read it.
- **Fix:** D173's CLOSEREOPEN1 note. The remote answers behind for a pushed step naming no source while it holds the parent not done
  (`AwaitsItsSourceAsync`); the rebase forgets a lost close's follow-up with this machine's unpushed work, a take rewritten as a conflict
  (`ForgetFollowUpsAsync` through `ForgetStepsAsync`). The end reads the step's source moved since the run started
  (`Planner.ReopenedFrom`) and ends as the reopen stopped it, so CLOSE1c2's carry-on brings the branch up to date once.
- **Verification:** `QuestSyncTests` (the theory, and the raced lost-step guard probed red with CLOSE1c21's rule off), `PlannerTests`
  (`ReopenedFrom` red by compile, the carry-on once), filtered, green.

## 2026-10-20 — A start's fresh tree was left at the driver's close (QUEUEDTREE1)

- **Symptom:** PARALLEL1f's hand-back: a continuation that returns as the driver closes leaves the tree its start opened, and its
  `daoris/` branch, for the sweep, though the record is already right.
- **Root cause:** two ways. Each return after the open that starts nothing (GOONTREE1's) removed the tree on the loop's token, which
  the close cancels, so the removal threw at its first git (the gate's wait checks the token first). And every await between the
  open and the record's open (the go-on's record read, a carry-on's walk, the tree's head) is on the loop's token, so a close there
  threw past every removal. The first alone is rare: a record whose own tree stands opens no fresh tree, so the second is the close's
  usual way out.
- **Fix:** `Loop/FreshTree.cs` holds the opened tree. Each return lets it go once on no token, as the put-back's move is; the start
  runs through it from `ClaimedAsync`, which lets the tree go on the close until the record's open is asked (after that the ledger may
  hold it, so a close is the sweep's), then closes on. Other failures, the untrusted hold and a replay's hold keep their tree as before.
- **Verify:** `FreshTreeTests` (six rows) red first as a missing type, then green; `QueuedStartCloseTests` green. The start's own
  path opens its tree with git, so its end-to-end proof is the Process half's (GOONTREE1's row in `SessionMessagesTickTests`), not run
  on the branch.

## 2026-10-19 — A rehearsal's timed-out drive ran on, and one starved phase failed 22 checks (FAMILYFAIL1)

- **Symptom:** the full set on 0a5c608 failed `rehearse-family` after 46 minutes (it passed on b7043d982 in 26 and on f617bc1
  in 31). From "a met done whose note was left uncommitted is held for the person" on, 22 checks failed: that one read the
  quest held `evidence-unread` with no evidence, the `quest check` calls named no commit, two loops were refused as "already
  driven by a headless `daoris-driver`", and later quests sat on an uncommitted `notes/late.md`.
- **Root cause:** no merge on the path. The drive of that phase ran 155 s against the rehearsal's 90-second bound (9 s on an
  earlier passing run). Every process on the machine was starved from about 06:52 UTC: the stub sessions ran 5 to 17 times
  their earlier length, the host's requests took 5 to 11 s and its Kestrel heartbeat ran 9 s late, and two paths no merge in
  the range touched outran their bounds too (a host refusing a workspace identity at its start, 30 s; the set-up stub's six
  CLI calls, 71 s). The full set runs below normal beside the work (CIPRIO1), and that afternoon it ran beside five workers
  and the owner's own sessions running whole builds and suites (HEAVYRUN1). The product did what the check asks, late: the
  driver's log has the session-end read at 06:57:13, `uncommitted: 1`, and the quest's record then reads Done, held
  `evidence-missing`, the item `uncommitted`, as the check expects. What turned one late phase into 22 failures was the
  rehearsal's runner: `capture` ran each command through `execSync`, whose timeout on Windows kills the shell alone, so the
  timed-out driver (a `dotnet` under `cmd.exe`) ran on holding the home's lease. The rehearsal then read the quest before the
  read, ran its `git add` before the stub had written the note (so its commit was none, and the note stayed in the tree), was
  refused by the lease, and the orphan started the next phase's ask's intake, which stood down when that phase closed the
  ask. A second timeout (the set-up pilot's phase, 07:28 UTC) left a second orphan the same way.
- **Fix:** `capture` runs its command through `spawnSync` with the same shell, which answers the shell's id, and on a timeout
  ends whatever that shell left running, each with its own tree (`tools/processes.mjs` `endOrphans`: the processes whose parent
  was the shell and that started after it, `taskkill /T /F`). The answer is otherwise as before: standard output alone on
  success, both streams on a failure, -1 and the kill's line on a timeout. The bounds and the starvation are left as they
  are: a starved full set still fails the phase that outran its bound, now alone.
- **Verify:** `tools/rehearsal-kit.test.mjs`: a command whose `node` child waits a minute, run with a five-second timeout,
  is red against the kit before the fix (the child still ran ten seconds after `capture` answered) and green after it; the
  runner's answers (exit code, streams, input, variables) held by a second case, green before and after. The file's 34 tests
  pass. The family rehearsal itself is not run on a branch: the next full set runs it, and it passes only on a machine that
  is not starved.

## 2026-10-19 — A woken turn that ended as the stream did could fail its session (BGWAIT2c)

- **Symptom:** `AcpBackgroundTests.A_woken_turn_that_ends_as_the_stream_does_ends_the_run_as_that_turn` failed alone now and then
  (at the fifteenth run of a loop here; the row measured one in five) and in the CI beside on 0a5c608: `AfterBackgroundAsync`
  threw *"the ACP agent's stream ended while the session waited for its own background work"* (`Acp.cs`, the `EndedAsync` line),
  though the wire had said the work's ending, the woken turn and its end before the stream's end. On the install it would record
  a finished session `failed`, BGWAIT2's own defect.
- **Root cause:** the order of two reads on the waiter's side, not the reader's. The reader takes every update before the stream's
  end completes (`Ended` is the reader's own task). `AcpBackground.EndedAsync`, parked while the work ran, woke on the ending's
  signal on the thread pool and then asked whether the stream was over: where the reader had read on to the stream's end first,
  it said null without reading the work again. `AcpWake.AfterAsync` read the turn's end under its lock and the stream's end after
  it, the same order with a narrower window.
- **Fix:** both read whether the stream is over first and what the wire said after it, so what they read once the stream is over
  is its last word: work it said ended has ended, and a woken turn's end it said is the turn's end, however the two completions
  reached the wait. A stream that truly ends while work runs, or before any woken turn's end, is the door's failure as before.
- **Verify:** `Work_whose_ending_was_said_before_the_stream_ended_has_ended_however_the_wait_is_woken` parks the wait, then takes
  the ending and the stream's end on the test's own thread, 200 times: red on its first iteration in six runs of six before the
  fix. After it, `AcpBackgroundTests` (27) run twenty times alone, green every time, and the stream's-end case thirty times
  alone, green every time.

## 2026-10-19 — A resumed protocol conversation skipped a required posture (HELPMODE1a4)

- **Symptom:** none observed. HELPMODE1a1's own note says it: an Ask Daoris conversation in full access, resumed on an ACP agent
  whose `session/load` or `session/resume` answers with no object, would go on without `session/set_mode`, in the agent's own
  narrower mode under the full label.

## 2026-10-19 — A person's agent waited behind a git fan-out for a start place, and git calls ran unbounded (PARALLEL1de)

- **Symptom:** an agent a person asked for (Ask Daoris's among them) queued for a process-start place behind Daoris's own git
  fan-outs; a git that never answered held its caller for ever; a review's read or a file's preview whose caller stopped
  waiting left its git running; a task's stop from its tab waited for ever on a session that did not answer.
- **Root cause:** four. `ProcessStarts` gave every start, git's and a person's alike, one shared queue of four places (UIFREEZE1
  bounded starts, not whose). `WorkingTree.RunGitAsync` ran git with `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` unless its caller passed a
  bound, and only a fetch and a replay did. `ReadGitAsync` and `GitBytesAsync` (REVIEW2, REVIEW3) read the streams with the
  caller's token and, on its cancellation, threw out of the read and disposed the `Process` without ending it; a read of a
  pipe on Windows does not always hear its token either, so nothing ended git but git. `ConsoleRoutes`' `STOP_TASK` asked the
  session's agent on `CancellationToken.None`.
- **Fix:** a start says whose it is (`StartClass`); the background holds at most three places, and a freed place goes to a
  person waiting first (`ProcessStarts`). Git runs under `GitBounds` by its kind unless its caller passes a longer bound. The
  streamed reads are bounded alike, and their token, the bound's or the caller's, ends git's tree (`WorkingTree.Ending`), the
  kill closing the pipe under the read. `STOP_TASK` passes its route's token. D181's PARALLEL1de note has the rest.
- **Verify:** `ProcessStartsTests` (four background starts held, a person's starts; the background bound; a freed place goes to
  the person), `GitBoundsTests` (bounds by kind; the runner handed the bound and the caller's token; a run past its bound read
  as unknown by `LandedProofs`; a cancelled caller ends its git) and `DriverModuleConsoleTests` red first, then green;
  `ProcessStartsCensusTests` names each start's class. `GitStreamEndsTests` (Process, git) holds the streamed reads' end on a
  real git, run in the git half.

## 2026-10-19 — A second launch of the installed Daoris opened no window and the desktop wrote nothing of why (ONEINSTANCE2)

- **Symptom:** a second `Daoris.exe`, and a direct `app\Daoris.Desktop.exe`, each exited while Daoris ran; no second main window
  opened, and the machine log held no `window.launched`, which the hand-over writes on every path it reaches. Nor did it hold
  any `log` line, the kit's warnings, ever.
- **Root cause:** two silences, and the path behind them not yet known (D171's ONEINSTANCE2 note reads each). (1) The desktop's
  container made no loggers. LOG1a (`b2a6dc4f0`) registered `MachineLogProvider` as an `ILoggerProvider` and nothing else; a
  provider is only what a logger factory makes loggers of, the kit calls no `AddLogging`, and it asks the container for an
  `ILogger<T>`, which nothing answered, so every warning it wrote went to a null logger: the single-instance guard's (a channel
  that would not open, a running instance not reached, a mutex not taken, a callback that threw), the engine's (Chromium handing
  over a launch the guard let through) and the window registry's (a window that failed to create). `MachineLogProviderTests` held
  the provider alone, never a container. (2) ONEINSTANCE1 (`5aea0e835`) wired the hand-over as `_ = …OpenAsync(…)` inside
  `OnActivated`: a resolution that threw went into the kit's callback, reported to the null logger, and a faulted hand-over was
  an unobserved task. Its only proof was a test that those words were in `Program.cs`.
- **Fix:** `MachineLogging.AddMachineLog` (modules) answers `ILoggerFactory` and `ILogger<>` with the provider, which now also
  writes information from the categories the application names (the guard's and the engine's hand-over lines).
  `LaterLaunch.Options` (modules) is the options `Program.cs` hands the kit: `window.launch` is written before anything is
  resolved or awaited, and the hand-over is observed, so a failure is an `error` with `where` `a later launch`.
- **Verify:** `LaterLaunchTests` run the options through the kit's own `SingleInstanceGuard` (one holding the scope on a thread
  of its own, a later one handing over its channel) into a composed container with the window stubbed, and the throwing paths;
  `MachineLoggingTests` run the kit's guard with the container's logger. Both were red against the old wiring (no arrival
  line, the exception thrown into the callback, no `ILogger<SingleInstanceGuard>` in the container), then green. The installed
  proof (a second click opens `main:2`; the log says `window.launch` then `window.launched`) is the parent's, after the next
  install.
- **Rule:** the desktop README's 🔴 "The kit's loggers are the container's": register loggers through `AddMachineLog`, never a
  provider alone. A later desktop process writes no line of Daoris's own until the driver's `MachineLog` writes at the file's
  end (two writers of one day's file overwrite each other, measured).
- **Commit:** `21a3b6501`

## 2026-10-19 — The dev knowledge server ran the build it started on for nine days, a fixed host's watch with it (KNOWHOLD1)

- **Symptom:** twice (the full set of 2026-10-18 on bbc1a24, and again on 10-19) the deployment rehearsal's swap under
  `local/gate-tree/` rolled back `busy`: `app` held for 636.8 s, then 590.4 s, with `app/cli/node_modules` held by
  `16075bf6 (pid 36544)` (its swap journal's `heldBy`), while the dev knowledge server served this checkout's sessions.
- **Which handle:** pid 36544 is `dotnet local/knowledge-server/builds/20261009T121055Z-cac379e1/daoris-knowledge.dll`,
  started on 10-10 by `node tools/knowledge-server.mjs` for the parent's session and still running on 10-19: the process
  KNOWWALK1 named. Its build predates KNOWWALK1's fix of 10-17, so its host still watches the checkout's root with every
  folder below it, `local/gate-tree/` too, and walks each folder renamed there (KNOWWALK1's reading of the framework's
  IL). Asked on 10-19 it held the checkout's root and nothing else, and six renames of a 300-package tree under an ignored
  folder of a worktree caught it in none: the walk comes with the rehearsal's load and goes, as KNOWWALK1 saw.

  started on until the session ended: `serve` handed the build the session's own streams, and nothing moved it, so a
  merge's build reached new sessions only, and the parent's session kept a fixed host's watch for nine days.
- **Fix:** `relayServer` in `tools/knowledge-server.mjs` stands between the session and its server, a message a line.
  When `current.json` names a build other than the one serving, it moves the session at a request that arrives with
  nothing owed either way, or at its own look each minute while the session is idle. The new server is handed the
  session's own `initialize` under an id of the relay's, then its `initialized`; once it answers it serves, the session is
  sent `notifications/tools/list_changed` (the server advertises it), and the old server's input is ended, as a session's
  end ends it, with a kill after ten seconds. A build that does not answer in 30 s is left, and not tried again. A driven
  session's machine host is not followed: it is the install's. Nothing is stopped to pass a gate. The server running now
  runs the old relay too, so it moves only once its session reconnects it (`/mcp`), which is the owner's call.
- **Verification:** `knowledge-server.test.ts`, 13 tests to 18: the five relay tests failed first on a stub (the session
  was never answered), then passed: a move at the next request with the handshake replayed and nothing answered twice, a
  request still owed holding the move, an idle session moved by the look with the old server's input ended, a build that
  will not answer left and not retried, and a server that cannot start answering in the protocol. A smoke with the real
  connector in a worktree: two builds, `current.json` repointed mid-session, the search after it answered by the second
  build's process, the first ended, the relay's exit 0. `CheckoutFreshnessTests.A_checkouts_ignored_folders_at_its_top_are_neither_read_nor_watched`
  guards the read and the watch of `local/`, `node_modules/` and `_fixtures/`, files held unshared and the install's `app/`
  moved aside and back: green on arrival, red with the root watched whole as the old host watched it. Service tests
  2325 to 2326. The deployment rehearsal with the dev server running is the merge's, once pid 36544 has been replaced.

## 2026-10-19 — A session that went on after its landing had its later done's opinion closed before the loop asked it (FABRIC-CLOSE1h18)

- **Symptom:** under *Accept automatically* and an opinion rule, a session that landed, went on with the person's words (D137) and
  concluded again with more work had the opinion owed on that work closed as `landed` at the loop's next look, never asked. Its landing
  was then kept as `opinion` and waited on the person's ask, though the gate said *it is asked at the driver's next look*.
- **Root cause:** `OpinionLook.ClosesAsync` closed a due as landed wherever `LandedBranches.Landing` named its session, whatever the
  landing's time. A session's landing record outlives its done, so the record of the first landing stood for every later done's work.
  The automatic landing already compared a landing's acceptance with its entry's done (`AutoLander.JudgeAsync`); the opinion look did not.
- **Fix:** the record closes the due only where it was made since the due was owed (`OpinionLook.MadeSince`: `AcceptedAt` of the due's
  session, its landing or its newest advance, at or after the due's `At`). An older landing falls to git's reading of the tree, as a
  session with no landing does, with its squash as one proof more, so a due owed after a squashed landing whose push was held back still
  closes once the push lands. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h18 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `OpinionGateTests` (the new theory's 2 older-landing rows), `AutoLandingTriesTests` (the row's proof, 2
  rows, and the git reading's 2 rows where the tree went on past the landing); the git reading's other 2 rows green before and after, as
  guards. Then the driver's fast half 9687 of 9687 (9682 before), and the `AutoLanding` Git classes, run once by filter with
  `git.process.runsettings`, 85 of 85, this row's 6 among them.

## 2026-10-19 — A step's take that went with its source take still closed the step the winner's chain published anew (FABRIC-CLOSE1c24)

- **Symptom:** B took a source, bound, submitted and took the step its submission published, all before syncing, while C's take of
  the source reached the remote first. B's take of the step went with its submission, and C's chain then published the same step
  anew under the same id. B's session, still running until its driver's next look, could close, decline or set up that open step:
  B's store kept the move, a remote kept it from an older build, and B's rebase pushed one an older build left pending.
- **Root cause:** `QuestLog.OnALostTake` judged an open step lost only where the machine's take lost to the person's reopen
  (FABRIC-CLOSE1c18, CLOSE1c22), since an open quest is otherwise nobody's work (D95). A take that went with its source's take to
  another machine's take left nothing that reading could see, so the move counted as one on nobody's work.
- **Fix:** `QuestLog.LostOnTheOpenStep` reads where the machine's latest take conflict landed: on the step open, the take was made on
  work the step no longer stands on (withdrawn by a reopen, grown from another submission, or published anew after its submission
  went). `OnALostTake`'s open branch reads it beside `LostToTheReopen`, so the store, the remote and the rebase refuse alike. The
  refusal reads the reopen from the history (`QuestMove.LostToTheReopen`), and otherwise says the step was published anew on other work.
- **Verification:** `QuestSyncTests`, done, decline and set-up, the step published anew after B's pass and before it: the store's
  refusal red, the remote's red with it set aside, the rebase's red with both, then green; a done after a take lost to a delete still
  lands (D95). Service tests 2325 before, 2332 after, all passed; HTTP tests 292, all passed.

## 2026-10-19 — A next step's take that went with a take lost to the reopen was stopped in another machine's words (FABRIC-CLOSE1c22)

- **Symptom:** B took a step before A's reopen of its source reached it, submitted, and took the next step its submission published,
  all before syncing. Its sync lost the step's take to the person's reopen, and with it the next step. B's take of the next step was
  kept as a conflict saying "another machine's take reached the remote first", its claim answered no `why`, and B's driver stopped
  that session as taken on another machine. Once the step's chain published the next step anew under the same id, a done from B's
  stopped session would have closed it, since the open step's lost-take check reads only a loss to the reopen.
- **Root cause:** `StepWentWith` had two sentences, both written for another machine's move, and `QuestLog.LostToTheReopen` reads
  the reopen from the quest's own history. The next step's publication went with the submission, so its history on B holds only the
  conflict, and nothing there shows the reopen.
- **Fix:** `RebaseAsync` reads the source take's loss on its replay so far and hands it to `ForgetStepsAsync`, which words the
  conflict by the reopen and marks it (`QuestOperation.LostToTheReopen`, `lostToTheReopen` in the log and on the wire, only when set).
  `QuestLog.LostToTheReopen` reads a marked take conflict as lost to the reopen, so the claim's answer, the driver's stop and
  `OnALostTake` all follow it.
- **Verification:** `QuestReopenSyncTests`, plain and raced: the words red, then the claim's reason red against a probe that ignored the
  mark, then green, with the restart and the step published anew; the census's conflict sample red in the log and on the wire, then
  green. Service tests 2271 before, 2274 after, all passed.
## 2026-10-19 — A second opinion holding an ordinary automatic landing was never asked where no due was open (FABRIC-CLOSE1h17)

- **Symptom:** under *Accept automatically*, a done's landing held at the look by a second opinion nobody had asked was kept as
  `opinion` and waited on the person's ask alone, though the gate said *it is asked at the driver's next look*. It happened where the
  opinion rule started reading after the done, or where the done's due had closed `off` and the rule came back.
- **Root cause:** only a conclusion (`OpinionLook.Concluded`) or the person's ask owes a due, and the loop's opinion look asks only what
  is owed. FABRIC-CLOSE1h15 made the gate's reader owe one in a push held back's recovery, but the look's own judgement
  (`AutoLander.JudgeAsync`) kept the hold and owed nothing.
- **Fix:** `JudgeAsync`'s opinion hold calls `AutoLander.Owe` for the entry's session at the landing's occasion, at every look that
  reaches the gate. A due open is left as it is; one the loop closed as landed since the entry's done is not opened again, so the look
  never churns it. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h17 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `AutoLandingTriesTests` (the new theory's 2 rows: no due owed); its guard theory's 2 rows green before
  and after. Then the driver's fast half 9631 of 9631 (9631 before), and the `AutoLanding` classes with `OpinionLandingTests`, run once by
  filter with `git.process.runsettings`, 84 of 84, this row's 4 among them.

## 2026-10-19 — A remote kept a step published on a take that then lost, when the take's own push was behind (FABRIC-CLOSE1c21)

- **Symptom:** B took a step before A's reopen of its source and A's rebind reached B, bound it, submitted, and its submission
  published the chain's next step. Where A's reopen, submission and rebind reached the remote between B's fetch and B's push, the
  next step stood open at the remote and then on A and B, grown from B's submission, which no machine held any more. B's lost take's
  conflict also said "the quest's close is the winner's", where nobody won: the person reopened the work.
- **Root cause:** the remote judges a push quest by quest. B's step's group was behind (the reopen and rebind reached it after B's
  base), but the next step's group was a new quest nothing had moved, so it was kept and numbered. B's next round rebased the step,
  lost the take and the submission, and `ForgetStepsAsync` left the next step, since no machine forgets a numbered operation
  (FABRIC-CLOSE1e's *Left*). The words: `SubmissionWentWith` had one sentence, written for a take lost to another machine's.
- **Fix:** `QuestStore.ReceiveAsync` answers behind for a pushed step whose source it holds without the submission the step grew from
  (`AwaitsItsSourceAsync`), so the machine goes round and its rebase forgets the step with the submission, or pushes it again beside
  it. A source the remote never held waits on nothing. `RebaseAsync` words a take lost to the person's reopen
  (`QuestLog.LostToTheReopen`) by the reopen.
- **Verification:** `QuestReopenSyncTests`: the raced order was seen red as a probe (the next step found at the remote), then green;
  the words red in both orders, then green; a step whose source never leaves its machine still goes up in the first push (a guard).
  `QuestReopenSyncTests` and `QuestSyncTests`, 84 passed.

## 2026-10-19 — A second opinion holding a push held back was never asked, and the person's ask was dropped (FABRIC-CLOSE1h15)

- **Symptom:** under *Accept automatically*, a made branch whose push was held back by a second opinion nobody had asked waited on the
  person alone, though the gate said *it is asked at the driver's next look*. The person's `opinion ask` on it opened a due that the
  next look closed as landed before it read the request, so even that ask did not move it.
- **Root cause:** `OpinionLook.ClosesAsync` closed a due as landed once a landing was recorded for its session, and its last exit closed
  it too, since a made branch leaves nothing unlanded in the tree. A push held back is recorded as made, not pushed, and `push-held`
  lives only on the automatic landing's entry, which the opinion look did not read. And only a conclusion or the person's ask owes a
  due, so an opinion rule that started reading after the done owed none.
- **Fix:** the opinion look reads the sessions whose automatic landing is open as `push-held`, and a landing whose push one of them holds,
  not pushed at its tip, keeps the due owed. `PushHeldAsync`, held by the opinion's part of the gate, owes one at the landing's occasion
  for the session whose work the hand-on pushes. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h15 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `OpinionGateTests` (3 `ClosesAsync` rows and the push-held sessions; 4 guard rows green),
  `OpinionLookTests` (2 cases: no pass asked), `AutoLandingPushHeldTests` (the new case and CLOSE1h12's recovery case for an opinion;
  its review case green as a guard). Then the driver's fast half is 9607 with main merged (9598 before; this row's 8 are
  `OpinionGateTests`'), `OpinionLookTests` 6 of 6 (4 before), and the `AutoLanding` classes, run once by filter with
  `git.process.runsettings`, 72 of 75 (74 before): the 3 timed out in the fixture's 60 s waits for a push or a landing to reach its
  hold, a load timeout before any opinion is read, and pass alone.

## 2026-10-19 — The instance door's tests gave a stand-in two seconds to connect and answer (TESTWAIT7)

- **Symptom:** beside loaded merges, four `InstanceDoorTests` failed (exit 2 for 0; "trees: Daoris is running on this home … did not

  settings: 72 of 74 passed, the two failures (`AutoLandingPressTests`' push-waiting theory, 30 s waits in a test body another
  branch owns) pass alone. Also found in the fast half's one run: `DriverWatchTopicsTests.A_thousand_wakes_run_no_remote_sync` asserted

## 2026-10-19 — The driver's signal waits were 5-10 seconds, and load elapsed them (TESTPATIENCE1)

- **Symptom:** nearly every merge on 2026-10-18/19 re-ran a gate for a fast test that failed on time alone (TESTCLOCK1's sweep found
  about 100 such bounds).
- **Root cause:** `WaitAsync(10 s)`, `Poll.Until(..., 10 s)` and `SpinUntil(..., 10 s)` wait on a signal that arrives in milliseconds

  the elapsed-time bounds that state the claim, the staging delays, `ChildProcess.RunAsync`'s own 5 s argument, and the 15-30 s bounds
  (see the hand-back's rows). No assertion changed.

## 2026-10-18 — A step's next submission after the person's go-on was never sealed (FABRIC-CLOSE1c14)

- **Symptom:** after the person's go-on on a held step that had submitted, the successor that old submission published stood unheld,
  could be taken and worked on, and the step's next submission was never sealed by it: the step's close was refused `unsealed`.
- **Root cause:** CLOSE1c10's go-on cleared the step's own submission and wrote nothing on the successor, which still named the cleared
  submission as its `grewFrom`; `PublishNextAsync` rebinds only a withdrawn open step, so it left that successor standing.
- **Fix:** `QuestStore.ContinueAsync` writes, in the same transaction, a `reopened` naming the cleared submission on the step's successor,
  judged by the replay's rule: withdrawn while open, held while taken. The continue answer names it. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1c14 note has the
  behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestReopenTests` (2) and `QuestReopenSyncTests` (1 theory, 2 cases) failing, then green.
  `Daoris.Service.Tests` is 2258 (2254 before), and `Daoris.Service.Http.Tests` 287, all passing.

## 2026-10-18 — A source's next submission let go a step another machine had taken (FABRIC-CLOSE1c15)

- **Symptom:** a machine that reopened a source and submitted again before another machine's take of the step reached it rebound the step
  it read withdrawn. At the remote, and on every machine after, the step read taken and unheld, grown from the new submission: a started
  step went on without the person's word.
- **Root cause:** `QuestLog.Applies` admitted a `rebound` on a taken held step as on an open one, so the publication's rebind, made on a step
  its machine read open, applied at the remote and survived the pushing machine's rebase.
- **Fix:** a publication's rebind carries `whileOpen` (as a decline made while open does), in the log and on the wire, and `Applies`
  refuses a marked one on a step no longer open; the person's go-on writes none. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1c15 note and D68's note have the
  behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestReopenSyncTests` (1), `QuestReopenTests` (1) and the census's wire and log theories for `Rebound`
  failing, then green. `Daoris.Service.Tests` is 2254 (2252 before), all passing.
## 2026-10-18 — An automatic landing pushed past an opinion or a review that started holding after the look chose it (FABRIC-CLOSE1h12)

- **Symptom:** under *Accept automatically*, an opinion rule or a set-up step shown for review that started holding while a landing's
  push waited behind another push of its branch did not stop the push; nor did one that started before a `push-held` entry's recovery
  (a restart's first look included), which handed the made branch on. An ordinary done was open to it as well as a submission.
- **Root cause:** `AutoLander` read the landing gate once, in the judgement just before the landing. `BeforePushAsync` read only the
  quest, and `PushHeldAsync` chose the hand-on before the look's gate part ran.
- **Fix:** one helper (`AutoLander.GateAsync`) reads the gate and its first refusal for the look, the push and the recovery alike. The push
  reads it where it reads the quest again, for the same session; the recovery reads it before a hand-on is chosen and waits silently
  while it holds; the `push-held` wake hears every ledger family and the gate's files. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h12 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `LandingWakesTests` (2 rows) and the new Git cases (6 failing on their assertions, 2 passing as guards).
  Then the driver's fast half is 9598 with main merged (9581 before; this row's two are wake rows), and the `AutoLanding` classes,
  run once by filter with `git.process.runsettings`, pass 73 of 74 (66 before); the 74th timed out in the fixture's 60 s wait for its
  push to reach the branch, a load timeout, and passes alone.

## 2026-10-18 — The merge tool's `--beside` test held its fake gate a minute, and load outlasted it (TESTWAIT4)

- **Symptom:** under load (three builders and a merge's gates) the `--full --beside` test failed `kept local/gate-tree` not matched; green on rerun.
  Two other failures that day, in `generated` (`local/scratch/` "not ignored", exit 2) and `--passed` (expected 0, got 2), were not seen again.
- **Root cause:** the fake gate waited on `GATE_HOLD` for 60 s at most, and the test's own steps (a refused second run, a merge, a prune, each a
  process) took longer under load, so the hold expired, the gate ended and the prune removed the gate tree. The first two failures are the
  GATEIGNORE1 class (a `git check-ignore` that failed under load was read as "not ignored", a tool error, exit 2); the logs kept hold only green reruns,
  so the third is that class by its exit code only, not proven.

  No tool bound was the cause; `tools/merge-branch.mjs` is unchanged.

  fixtures shared from `test/workFrameBridge.ts` and `test/workFrameKit.tsx`. Test bodies are unchanged: every line of the old blocks stands in a part.

## 2026-10-18 — A hand-off pushed a later session's work on an earlier session's quest (FABRIC-CLOSE1h10)

- **Symptom:** where a chain's later session moved a landed branch on after a hand-off's door read it (or after the look chose a
  `push-held` entry), the hand-off pushed that later work while the later session's quest was taken back: the person's hand-off judged
  the session its door read, and the look's hand-on its entry's own quest, which still stood.
- **Root cause:** the advance is recorded before its push takes the branch's hold (`TreeLands`), and `TreeHandOffs.HandAsync` read the
  record again under that hold without telling its `beforePush` which session the record now named.
- **Fix:** `beforePush` is told the record's `LastSession()` under the hold. A session other than the one judged is judged on its own
  quest, read there: the person's doors by their rule (`HandedResult`, from `PressQuests.HandedAsync`), the look by its own, which also
  waits on that quest before choosing the hand-on (`AutoLander.PushHeldAsync`). D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h10 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `PressedResultTests` (5 failing), and the new Git cases (3 failing, 2 passing as before). Then the
  driver's fast half is 9568 (9561 before), and `AutoLandingTests`, run once by class, passes 65 (60 before).
## 2026-10-18 — A step gone on with after its session ended normally sat taken with nothing submitted (FABRIC-CLOSE1c13)

- **Symptom:** after the person's go-on cleared a held step's own result (CLOSE1c10), a step whose session had said `ready` and parked,
  or completed, before its source was reopened sat taken with no submission: nothing went on with it, and its branch never got the
  source's new work.
- **Root cause:** the planner's go-on after a reopen read only a session the reopen stopped (`StoppedByReopen`, CLOSE1c2), and the
  start's rebase onto the new submission (CLOSE1c5) was gated on the same; a park also holds its quest's slot and tree, so a new session
  beside it could never start.
- **Fix:** the look tells that session Daoris's words of the go-on, once (`Planner.GoneOnSince`, `ReopenTelling`), the planner's go-on
  resumes it with them, and the start's gate (`ReopenTelling.BringsToSource`) brings its branch up to date first. D173's
  FABRIC-CLOSE1c13 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `PlannerTests` (2), `ReopenGoOnTests` (1), `ReopenTellingTests` (6), then green; the driver's fast half
  is 9591 (9578 before).
## 2026-10-18 — The person's go-on kept a held step's result made on the reopened work (FABRIC-CLOSE1c10)

- **Symptom:** a step that had said `ready` before the person reopened its source went on, at the person's word (`continue`), with that
  submission still current, its answers, yes and verdict with it: its close could take work made on the reopened source as finished, with
  nothing submitted again.
- **Root cause:** CLOSE1c's `rebound` step in `QuestLog.Step` moved `grewFrom` and let the hold go, and touched nothing else, while the
  reopen and the `submitted` steps both clear a quest's result.
- **Fix:** the `rebound` step clears the step's submission, answers, yes and verdict too; the continue answer says so, and that the step
  must submit again. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1c10 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestReopenTests` (2) and `QuestReopenSyncTests` (1) failing, then green. `Daoris.Service.Tests` is 2252
  (2249 before) and `Daoris.Service.Http.Tests` 287 (286 before), all passing.

## 2026-10-18 — A hand-off that waited behind another push told its plugin of a result taken back meanwhile (FABRIC-CLOSE1h8)

- **Symptom:** handing a landed branch on (`HANDOFF`, Ask Daoris's card, `trees hand`), or the look's hand-on of a push held back, waiting
  up to minutes behind another push of the branch (LANDRACE1), told its plugin of the branch whatever its quest had come to meanwhile: a
  submission reopened, readied again or a done turned down was pushed all the same, and the look's hand-on pushed through a fresh hold.
- **Root cause:** `TreeHandOffs.HandAsync` took no judgement at the push, so no hand-off read a quest past its door; CLOSE1h3 fenced only
  the press and Accept.
- **Fix:** `HandAsync` takes a `beforePush`, asked under the branch's hold just before the plugin; a refusal tells no plugin and records
  nothing (`TreeHand.Withheld`). The person's doors pass the result of the session that last moved the branch (`PressQuests.HandedAsync`,
  CLOSE1h3's rule), the look its own rule, keeping the entry `push-held`. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h8 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `PressedResultTests` and `DriverCommandTests` (fast, 6 failing), and the new Git cases (5 failing, 2
  passing as before). Then the driver's fast half is 9545 (9538 before), its one failure a load flake that passes alone, and
  `AutoLandingTests`, run once by class, passes 60 (53 before).
## 2026-10-18 — A git that could not answer `check-ignore` refused a merge as "not ignored" (GATEIGNORE1)

- **Symptom:** CLOSE1q5's merge failed its cli gate: the scratch tool exited 2 saying `local/scratch/` is not ignored, in a scratch
  repository that ignores it; green on rerun. The false reason hid git's real error.
- **Root cause:** the five `git check-ignore -q` probes in `tools/merge-branch.mjs` read any non-zero status as "not ignored", but git
  answers 1 for that; 128, or a git that could not answer under load, is an error.
- **Fix:** one `ignoredVerdict` (through `isIgnored`) for all five: 0 ignored, 1 not ignored, anything else a `Refusal` saying the probe
  failed with its status and git's stderr.
- **Verification:** red first: the new unit over the three statuses failed (`ignoredVerdict` absent), then `merge-branch.test.ts` passes
  116 (115 before).

## 2026-10-18 — A press that waited behind another landing landed a result taken back meanwhile (FABRIC-CLOSE1h3)

- **Symptom:** the person's Accept (`LAND_SESSION_TREE`, `trees land <session>`) or an entry's or an ask's, waiting up to minutes behind
  another landing of the same tree (LANDRACE1), landed whatever stood when it got the tree: a submission reopened, readied again or a done
  turned down meanwhile was branched and pushed all the same. An entry's later part was never judged after its earlier parts landed.
- **Root cause:** `TreeLands.LandAsync`'s `judged` and `beforePush` (CLOSE1h, CLOSE1h2) were passed only by `AutoLander`; every press door
  passed neither, so nothing read the quest again past the door's own reads.
- **Fix:** `PressQuests` keeps one press's quest reads, so the press is made on the read that named its landing, and `PressedResult`
  judges that result again under the tree's hold and before the push: moved, the press makes nothing, or at the push keeps its branch
  and tells no plugin. A quest's hold does not stop a press. The route, the terminal and `EntryAccepts` (each part on its own quest)
  build it alike. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h3 note has the behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `PressedResultTests`, `EntryLandingsTests`, `TreesWordsTests` and `DriverCommandTests` (fast), and the
  new Git cases (8 failing, 4 passing as before). Then the driver's fast half passes 9524 (9486 before), and `AutoLandingTests` with
  `EntryLandingTests`, run once by class, 67 (55 before).

## 2026-10-18 — A push held back after its branch was made waited for the whole look (FABRIC-CLOSE1h7)

- **Symptom:** a `push-held` entry (CLOSE1h2) was looked at only by the whole look at `pollSeconds`, never by the `quests` wake its
  release (the hold let go, a reopen, the next submission) raises.
- **Root cause:** `LandingWaits.Of` had no case for `push-held`; its kept tip did not make it `tree` (`AutoLandingCode.OnChange` excludes
  it), so it fell to `look`, which no wake concerns.
- **Fix:** `LandingWaits.Of` reads `push-held` as `quests`, beside `held` and `unreviewed`.
- **Verification:** red first: `LandingWakesTests`' `push-held` rows (the two quests-family rows failed); then 52 pass there.

## 2026-10-18 — A session due again after a try that closed its entry was never tried (FABRIC-CLOSE1h6)

- **Symptom:** under a rule with *Accept automatically* on, a session that landed, was carried on with more words (D137) and concluded
  done again stayed open on the due list and was never tried: its later commits waited for the person's Accept, where the look should
  have moved its branch on (LAND2c). In a closure graph, a submission reopened (entry closed `undone`) and readied again never landed.
- **Root cause:** `AutoLandings.Due` reopens an entry with its tries kept, and `AutoLandingRules.ShouldTry` judged the reopened entry by
  its last try, which was the earlier due's: for any code that closes (`landed`, `undone`, `nothing`, …) it answered no for good.
  `LandingWaits.Of` likewise left it to the whole look alone.
- **Fix:** `AutoLanding.Reopened` (open, with a last try whose code closes; only `Due` makes one) is judged afresh: `ShouldTry` answers
  yes, and `LandingWaits.Of` reads it as a first try. An entry still due on its own last try keeps its rule. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1h6 note
  has the owner-facing behaviour.
- **Verification:** red first: `AutoLandingRulesTests`' eleven closing codes, `LandingWakesTests`' two rows, and `AutoLandingTests`' two
  Git proofs (no branch after the next `ready`; no second frame after the done that went on). Then the driver's fast half passes 9482
  (9463 before) and `AutoLandingTests` 42 (40 before), the proof's second conclusion with nothing new closing `already` with no push.

## 2026-10-18 — The person's stop on a close for a reopened submission stopped the next submission's work (FABRIC-CLOSE1q2)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no quest is bound to a closure graph there. A close for S1 left unanswered when the person reopened S1,
  then S2 made ready at S1's commit: the person's `stop` on S1's close, applied by a loop started again, stopped S2's deploy where it was
  already sent, or else the close node, so S2's close never ran. On a wake, `record` on a held close for S1 reached the close node with
  S1's key while the quest stood on S2.
- **Root cause:** `QuestCloser.Recover` stopped every live node of the unit, and a stop holds across revisions (`NodeStates.Bound`);
  `QuestCloser.Resolve` never read the quests, and a pass that was no whole look kept the read from before (`NodeRuntime.PassAsync`).
- **Fix:** `Resolve` takes the pass's quests, and where a close's submission is the quest's no more (`QuestClosing.Moved`), `record`
  and `stop` are taken back with `submission-moved`, said; `resend` asks after S1's key alone, as before. A pass with a close's word
  waiting reads the quests afresh. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1q2 note has the choices.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestCloseTests`' theory's two `stop` rows (S2's deploy stopped; S2's close node stopped) and the wake
  fact without the fresh read (S1's key on the node). Then the driver's fast half passes 9449 (9442 before), and the page's
  `WorkMilestone.test.tsx`, the locales, `i18n:check` and `names:check --strict` pass.

## 2026-10-18 — A stream-of-wakes test counted looks over four wall-clock seconds, and a held-words line fell back with no cause shown (TESTWAIT6, TESTWAIT5)

- **Symptom:** under load, `DriverWatchTopicsTests.The_whole_look_still_runs_at_its_deadline_under_a_stream_of_wakes` failed twice
  ("6 look(s) for 7 wakes"), and `SessionsSayCommandTests.Held_words_name_what_holds_them` once, reading "held: the same session goes
  on…" for the planner's hold sentence; each passed alone.
- **Root cause** (read, not reproduced): the first sent wakes for 4 s of the machine's clock, so a starved test thread sent 7 wakes
  and the `> 10` looks bar judged the load. The second's `HeldAsync` falls back to its "next look" sentence when the planner's look
  throws or gives no verdict, and said nothing of which; the in-process stand-in has no client timeout, so the cause stays unproven.
- **Fix:** the wakes test sends wakes, each awaiting the look it woke, until two deadlines and eleven looks have passed (the loop's
  own counts, 40 s cap), then asserts the deadlines at most one per elapsed second plus one and more looks than deadlines. The
  words' line is unchanged; `SessionsWorld.Fell` reports the fallback's cause, and the test asks again up to three times over a
  fresh room when it fell, the last try failing with the causes named.
- **Verify:** both classes (70 tests) passed 3 of 3, then the driver fast half. If the held test fails again its message names the cause.

## 2026-10-18 — A redirect test's status call timed out under load before its listener was asked (TESTWAIT3)

- **Defect:** `RunningServiceTests.A_redirect_is_no_answer` failed twice in the driver gate beside two other gates and passed alone.
- **Root cause** (read from the code, not reproduced red): `RunningService.Status` has a fixed 2 s bound (`Within`); under load it
  ends before the loopback listener accepts, `Status` returns null, the listener's answer fails on the closed socket, and
  `Assert.True(await redirect, "the address was not asked")` fails.
- **Fix:** the test reruns, up to three times, with fresh listeners when the redirect listener was not asked; an asked try keeps both

## 2026-10-18 — Two fast service tests asserted what a real observer or a process pipe had not yet delivered (TESTWAIT2)

- **Symptom:** beside other gates (GATELANES2), `ChangeStreamTests.A_write_outside_every_family_wakes_nobody` failed at
  `Assert.True(_stream.Seen > seen)` and `NewerIndexTests.The_connector_over_a_newer_index_starts_and_says_so_once` on its stderr

  600 ms wait, and the stderr line (read through `ErrorDataReceived`) lagged the `app.started` log line the test waited on.

## 2026-10-18 — A take queued past its bind's expiry bound it, and an older build's naming could replace an owned bind's graph (FABRIC-CLOSE1w)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no install names a graph for a take. Found by the read-only review of the close path. A take asked
  before the bind's expiry and kept waiting for the store's write past it still bound the graph. A build before FABRIC-CLOSE1o, naming a
  graph for the same quest, replaced the graph of an owned bind and kept its owner, so the owner's take bound the older build's graph;
  and an older build's take bound an owned bind by the quest's id alone, whoever took and however late.
- **Root cause:** `QuestStore.MoveAsync` judged the expiry on the `now` its caller took before the write's gate and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
  (`Quests/Quests.cs`). The owned binds shared `quest_take_binds` with the builds before them, whose upsert names only `graph` and `at`
  and whose take deletes and binds whatever row the id names.
- **Fix:** the take measures its wait for the write on the store's monotonic clock and judges the bind at its caller's moment plus that
  wait. Binds are now named in `quest_owned_take_binds`, a table no older build knows; a row in `quest_take_binds` is an older
  build's, consumed at a take as owning nothing and discarded at the open. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1w note has the choice.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestTakeBindTests`' take queued past the expiry bound, the owner's take after an older build's naming
  bound the older graph, and an older build's take read the owned bind; the unarmed store's take and an older build's own statements,
  green before and after. Then the service suite passes 2223 (2219 before), and its HTTP suite 283 (283).

## 2026-10-18 — The close door closed a bound quest of no chain the close was at (FABRIC-CLOSE1v)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no quest is bound to a closure graph there, and the driver names only its own chain's quests. Found by
  the read-only review of the close path. A close at one quest naming another bound, submitted and unheld quest, of another chain,
  another repository or another graph, closed both. A plain bind in a workspace syncing through a remote bound the quest.
- **Root cause:** `QuestStore.CloseAsync` judged each named quest's own state alone (`Quests/Quests.cs`), so the driver's filter
  (`QuestClosing.Judge`) was the close's only scope. The plain bind in `QuestExchange.BindAsync` never read the remote map that the bind
  at the take reads.
- **Fix:** the store takes the quest the close is at and refuses, before any quest's state, a quest of another repository, of no chain
  it grew from (`LineageAsync`, the driver's `Lineage` twin), or bound to another graph, by its own code, whole, kept under its key. The
  plain bind reads `remotes` as the take's does. The driver knows the three codes. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1v note has the choices.
- **Verification:** red first: three `QuestClosureTests` closed what they named, `QuestTakeBindTests` bound through a remote, and the
  client's theory left each code unknown. Then the service suite passes 2219 (2215 on main), its HTTP suite 283 (283), and the driver's
  fast half 9396 (9393 on main).

## 2026-10-18 — A close never delivered was sent after a restart on the evidence it was recorded on (FABRIC-CLOSE1u)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no quest is bound to a closure graph there. Found by the read-only review of the close path. A
  loop that ended after writing a close attempt and before the close left, then a session branch that moved, then a restart: the
  restarted loop sent that close, and the door closed the quest on the old revision, since its submissions had not moved.
- **Root cause:** `QuestCloser.ReconcileAsync` sent every recorded or unknown close again with its key, before any fence
  (`Trees/Nodes/QuestCloser.cs`). The key's idempotency protects an outcome the door already keeps; a key it never took runs as new.
- **Fix:** step 4 asks instead (`POST /api/quests/{id}/close/outcome`), answered from `quest_closes` and running nothing. A key taken
  settles from its first outcome. A key never taken is withdrawn there in the same transaction, its attempt settled `not-started` and
  its node invalidated, so a close is made again only through the fresh fence, under a new key. An unanswered close stays unknown and
  takes the person's `resend` and `stop`. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1u note has the choices.
- **Verification:** red first: the crash, move and restart test sent the old close; the lost-answer theory, the unknown close's stop,
  the client's question and the service's withdrawal failed. Then the driver's fast half passes 9338 (9334 before), the service's
  2215 (2214) and its HTTP suite 283 (283), and `CloseFenceGitTests` (Git, run once) passes.

## 2026-10-18 — A chain's close closed an earlier quest whose own deploy was still held (FABRIC-CLOSE1t)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no quest is bound to a closure graph there. Found by a read-only review of the whole close path. In a
  two-quest chain, the first quest published the second while its deployment stayed held, and the second's close closed both.
- **Root cause:** the terminal quest's own prerequisites were fenced by the evaluation that proposed its close. `QuestClosing.Judge`
  then named each earlier quest on its submission and hold alone (`Trees/Nodes/QuestCloser.cs`), and `NodeRuntime.CloseAsync` read no
  other quest's node record.
- **Fix:** `NodeRuntime.Unreached` judges each other quest a close names on its own node record, under its bound graph and at its
  current revision, with the evaluation its own pass makes. The close waits, said once a pass naming the quest and the node, until that
  quest's close is eligible there. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1t note has the detail and the counts.
- **Verification:** red first: three `QuestCloseTests` (the held deploy, the same chain reached, an unreadable record) sent the close.
  The unarmed look's test was green before and after. Then the driver's fast half passes 9280 (9276 before), and `CloseFenceGitTests`
  (Git, run once) passes with its counts unchanged.
## 2026-10-18 — The rehearsals waited for the whole Process lane, and the web gate's vitests for service (REHLANE1, WEBSPLIT1)

- **Symptom:** after GATELANES2 (a merge's light lane about 4 m 15 s, against 9 m 35 s one at a time) a full set's wall was
  the Process lane in turn: the git half about 45 to 50 m, alone in the lane; the serial half about 15 to 19 m;
  `rehearse-family` 10 to 26 m; `deployment` about 13 to 15 m. Before it, the light lane's floor: `web`, 4 to 6 m, behind
  `service`, about 10 m under load together.
- **Root cause:** a rehearsal waited for every Process half, though the family rehearsal and the git half share nothing
  but the desktop's build output, which only the rehearsal's build of the driver host touched. The web gate's first step,
  the page's vitests, builds nothing, and waited for service only because the rest of its gate builds the HTTP host.
- **Fix:** `tools/merge-branch.mjs` runs a rehearsal of `BESIDE_GIT_HALF` (the family rehearsal) beside a git half, and
  every other Process-lane gate alone, the deployment rehearsal last; a git half's re-run alone waits for it. The family
  rehearsal builds the driver host into its own output (`ownBuild` in `tools/rehearsal-kit.mjs`, `--artifacts-path` under
  `_fixtures/rehearsal-builds/family`). The web gate's vitests are their own light gate, `web-unit`
  (`npm run test:web:unit`); `web` runs `npm run test:web:e2e`. D115's note "REHLANE1, WEBSPLIT1" has the choices.
- **Verification:** seven new tests in `merge-branch.test.ts` (the schedule's pair and order, the run beside and the
  re-run alone, the family's own output read from its tool, the web gate's two halves) and one in `rehearsal-kit.test.mjs`,
  all seen red but one: the unit run beside service passed on GATELANES2's light lane as it stood. Then `merge-branch.test.ts` 104 (97 before), `rehearsal-kit.test.mjs` 29 (28), `dogfood.test.ts`
  32, and `verify`. **The walls** (the rows' proof, recorded by the parent at its next full sets, against the figures
  above): set 1 —; set 2 —; set 3 —; the Process lane's wall, the light lane's, and the flakes of each, with the family
  rehearsal's transcript showing its driver host built under `_fixtures/rehearsal-builds/family`.

## 2026-10-18 — The light lane ran its gates one at a time, and each Process half built again (GATELANES2, GATEBUILD1)

- **Symptom:** a merge's light lane (universal, code-map, orient-index, cli, service, driver, modules) took 10 to 12 minutes
  under load and about 5 on a quiet machine: 394 to 434 s in the 2026-10-18 merges' logs, cli 144 to 231 s and service 142
  to 206 s of it. In a full set the light lane took about 14 minutes (2026-10-17, 1 h 38 m in all), and every Process
  gate waited for its heavy gates (GATEORDER1). Each Process half then built the test project its fast half had just built.
- **Root cause:** GATELANES1 ran the light lane beside the Process lane but one gate at a time within it, though only gates
  that build one .NET component share `obj/` and `bin/`. And a `dotnet test` gate always builds, whatever ran before it.
- **Fix:** `tools/merge-branch.mjs` runs up to three light gates at once (`LIGHT_WIDTH`), never two that build one
  component (`gateComponents`, read through the root scripts: the CLI's `verify` shares the devkit's, the web gate the
  service's). A Process half runs `--no-build` when its test project's fast half passed in the same run on the tree it
  starts on (`testBuild`, `reuses`, `reuseBuild`); its line says whose build it ran.
- **Verification:** seven new tests in `merge-branch.test.ts`, six seen red first. Then 97 of 97 green (90 before), with the
  end-to-end tests that read the gates' order reading which ran instead, and `verify`. **The walls** (the row's proof,
  recorded by the parent at its next full sets, against the one-at-a-time light lane above): set 1 —; set 2 —; set 3 —;
  the flakes of each, and a Process half's log showing `--no-build` with its verdict as before.
## 2026-10-18 — A close spoke for a later submission, and a held close took a plugin's words (FABRIC-CLOSE1q)

- **Symptom:** found before any install armed a closure graph (the owner's holds none), by the row's pre-mortem checked against the
  code. A close kept for one submission was read as the close of any later one. S2, the same commit made ready again and closed by the
  person, reached its close node through S1's receipt (`ReachByChain`) and was never read as overridden. A close its door made, whose
  answer its node could not take, was held and offered PERFORM1g's three words. *It did not* failed it as the person's and made it ready,
  minting a second close under a new key; *it happened* stood in for the door. While it was held, the door's Done read as the person's.
- **Root cause:** `QuestClosing.Naming` matched a close to a quest by its id alone. The held list and its two doors took Daoris's own
  close for a plugin's attempt. `NodeRuntime.Settle` counted a closed or waiting close as the door's, and not a held one.
- **Fix:** `QuestClosing.NamesCurrent` matches the quest, its submission's machine and its sequence, for `ReachByChain` and the
  override alike; a held close with no refusal kept is the door's. A held close takes `record`, `resend` and `stop`
  (`HeldResolutions.Of`, `QuestCloser.Resolve`); a plugin's word is refused at the door (`not-close-word`), and one recorded before is
  taken back. D173's note "FABRIC-CLOSE1q" has the choices.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestCloseTests` (part 1's one; part 2's theory of three and one more), `NodeRuntimeTests` (a close's
  word on a plugin's attempt, at the door and at the pass), `DriverModuleLinesTests` (the wire's `words`) and `WorkMilestone.test.tsx`
  (two). Then green with the driver's fast half (9224 before, 9230 after), the modules' (1392, 1393) and the web's touched files with
  its page-wide checks.
## 2026-10-18 — A graph named for a take bound whichever take came, however late, and the store never upgraded its table (FABRIC-CLOSE1o)

- **Symptom:** found by a pre-mortem of FABRIC-CLOSE1l before any install armed a closure graph (the owner's holds none). A pending
  take-bind bound the next take of its quest id. That could be another session's take, a take of the same ask deleted and published
  again, a take hours later, or one after the circle gained a remote. A store from before the row had an owner kept its rows as they
  were.
- **Root cause:** `quest_take_binds` held the quest id, the graph and a moment, and the take read it with `DELETE … RETURNING graph`
  alone. The connector's session never reached the take. The remote was judged once, at the naming. The table was made by
  `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, which upgrades nothing.
- **Fix:** D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1o note. The row keeps its session, the publication's operation and an expiry. The take consumes it in its
  own write and binds only where `PendingTakeBind.Judge` reads all of them, with the remotes map read there. The columns are added at
  open, and a row without an owner is discarded. An expired, replaced or remote-since bind is said once, in the take's answer and on the
  loop's end line.
- **Verification:** red first: `QuestTakeBindTests` (five of six theory rows, an older build's row, a bind naming no session),

## 2026-10-18 — The close's fresh fence read no branch tip, so a commit after a prerequisite's acceptance was closed on it (FABRIC-CLOSE1p)

- **Symptom:** none on an install: no quest is bound to a closure graph there. Under one, a session branch that moved after the close's
  prerequisite was accepted was closed on that acceptance. This held whether the branch moved between passes or between the pass's read
  and the fence's.
- **Root cause:** CLOSE1l's fence read the units again right before the close, but the loop's read (`DriverWatch`'s units callback)
  passed no roots to the inventory, so it asked git nothing. A branch unit's `Subject.Revision` is its kept end fact's, which a commit
  does not move. `QuestClosing.Revision` therefore digested records alone. `QuestCloseTests` handed in branch units with tips already
  set, so it never saw this.
- **Fix:** the read carries `NodeUnitsRead.Tips`, the tip of each branch a bound chain worked. `QuestClosing.TipsAsync` reads them
  with one `RefSnapshot` per repository, per read. `Revision` digests those tips, and an unread tip leaves the close waiting
  (`QuestClosing.Unread`). A fence that finds the unit moved ends its judgement for that pass. D173's FABRIC-CLOSE1p note has the
  detail and the counts.
- **Verification:** red first. `CloseFenceGitTests` (Git, real git through the production read) sent the close after the move; it
  now sends none until the deploy is accepted again on the new tip. The same test counted three `for-each-ref` in the fenced pass
  before the early end, and counts two now. `CloseTipsTests`' four tests were red on the members. The driver's fast half passes
  9229 (9224 before).

## 2026-10-18 — The merge tool's prune left merged agent worktrees and a half-removed folder standing (CLEANUP2)

- **Symptom:** 24 worktrees stood with 3 agents running. 9 merged ones were kept as "locked, so in use", 5 for worker logs
  under `local/`, and a 320 MB folder under `.claude/worktrees/` that git no longer listed, held by two `node land.mjs` a
  test had leaked on 10-16, was never looked at.
- **Root cause:** GATE2 took the agent harness's lock (`claude agent <id> (pid N)`) to mean an agent was running. The harness
  holds it for its session's whole life. Any file under `local/` counted as work, logs included. A folder git did not list
  was outside the prune's rules by design, so a `git worktree remove` that could not finish left one for ever.
- **Fix:** `tools/merge-branch.mjs` lifts the harness's lock from a merged worktree (`harnessLock`, `pruneVerdict`'s
  `unlock`). Its branch must not be at main's tip, the tree must be clean, and no process may name its folder: one CIM
  query per prune (`listProcesses`, `processesInside`). `local/scratch/` and `*.log` are disposable (`disposableLocal`). A
  folder under `.claude/worktrees/` with no `.git` that git does not list is removed (`strayFolders`, `folderVerdict`,
  `removeFolders`). Links are never followed, and a process found inside is named, never stopped. The leaked `land.mjs` had
  already been fixed by 1f780e43e, which ends the plugin in a `finally`.
- **Verification:** red first: five unit tests, and both `--prune` end-to-end tests in `merge-branch.test.ts`. Then 90 of
  90 green (84 before), and `verify`. The end-to-end test holds a real process in a worktree and in a folder, links a
  junction out of a half-removed folder, and keeps a folder that is a process's working folder on Windows.

## 2026-10-18 — The prune removed a live worker's tree under it (CLEANUP2b)

- **Symptom:** a fresh worker fast-forwarded its branch to main's tip. Before its empty start commit, a merge moved main and the
  next `--continue` pruned: the tree was removed under the working agent.
- **Root cause:** CLEANUP2's rules read a harness-locked tree as finished when its branch was merged but not at main's tip, it
  was clean, and no process named its folder. Main had moved past the fresh branch, so the tip guard no longer held. A command
  line does not show a shell's working directory, and the harness lock is held for the agent's whole run, so nothing showed it.

  the folder's top-level entries, those folders' children but build output, and the git folder's HEAD, index and HEAD log (no full
  walk). `HARNESS_IDLE_MINUTES` (two hours) is the span. `--prune --plan` says "written N minutes ago, a worker may be in it". The
  unlocked-tree and half-removed-folder rules are unchanged. `docs/development.md` and the GATE2 header say so; the brief tells a
  worker to make its start commit before merging main.
- **Verification:** red first (the new `pruneVerdict` cases and the prune end-to-end test, which added a young harness-locked tree
  beside the aged ones); then `merge-branch.test.ts` 98 of 98 (97 before), and `verify`.

## 2026-10-18 — A closure graph's close was not safe to arm: eight fences missing, and its own node's record stopped reading after its Done (FABRIC-CLOSE1l)

- **Symptom:** found by a second maker's review of FABRIC-CLOSE1b before any install armed a closure graph (the owner's holds none, so

  take's write (`quest_take_binds`); `SessionTarget.Ready`; `RemoteTarget.Effective`; `QuestClosing.Revision` and a fresh read before the
  send; `ClosureGraphs` kept by digest, arming a home that keeps one; only the door's coded answers settle; and a settled, never-sent
  `QuestClosing.Chained` attempt for a node reached again on its chain.

  (5 rows), `RemoteTargetTests` (1). The ninth showed red as CLOSE1b's own first and chain tests once a closing quest's revision moved.
  Then green with the driver's fast half (9083), `Daoris.Service.Tests` and `Daoris.Service.Http.Tests`.

## 2026-10-17 — The evaluation runtime could restart failed work for ever, judge under removed graphs and outrun its bounds (FABRIC-RUN1e)

- **Symptom:** found by a second maker's review of FABRIC-RUN1 before any install armed a graph (the owner's names no performed node,
  so nothing ran there). Six faults: a config wake judged a unit under a graph since removed; a disarm left a pending retry's timer and
  the cached units, and the plan's supervision could start a plugin the last graph awaited after its removal; graph edits back and
  forth restarted a permanent failure past `retry`; units past the first 32 never judged; a pass's four sends not counting
  reconciliation; the awaited set told after a lease lost mid-pass.
- **Root cause:** RUN1 cached governance per look and checked nothing at a wake; it cleaned a disarm up only when a non-empty set had
  been told, and link 8 runs after link 5's supervision; a run's identity follows the graph, and both WIRE1f (another run's failure
  lapses) and WIRE1e (a binding of another graph lapses, its tries counted afresh) took a graph edit as a new start; the pass took the
  same id-ordered prefix and counted only its own starts; `Tell` asked no lease.

  held and is called at link 5 before the look; `WireEvaluation` keeps a failure or rejection of another graph or run for the person,
  lapsed by a new revision alone; `Turn` takes the units past 32 in turn; `WorkSends` is one count shared by reconciliation and starts;
  `Tell` asks the lease before `Watch`. D173's RUN1 note, "After review", has the detail.
