  lapse tests rewritten to the new rule); then green with the driver's fast half, `NodeRuntimeLoopProcessTests` and
  `WorkPerformProcessTests` by class.

## 2026-10-17 — A landing squash-merged on the platform, then deleted, read dropped with a recovery ref kept for ever (CLEANUP1c)

- **Symptom:** found reading CLEANUP1 against the owner's install, before it ran there: a landing whose pull request the platform
  squash-merged, its branch deleted by the person after the pull, would read *over without its result* in `work state`, and its
  commits would be kept on a recovery ref held by nothing, so kept for ever and listed for the person to delete. Most of the
  install's 18 deleted landings were squash-merged.
- **Root cause:** CLEANUP1b judged a landing git says is missing by the line's ancestry of its recorded commit alone, and a squash
  leaves no ancestry: the squash is a commit of its own. The content proof, which ends a standing landing after a squash
  (`LandedProofs.ProveAsync`), was never read for a gone one, so CLEANUP1's `WentAsync` took it as dropped and kept its commit.
- **Fix:** `EndJudgement.GatherAsync` reads a gone landing's content proof at its recorded commit where no ancestry holds it, and
  `JudgeGone` ends it `on-line` only where that proof holds on a form of the line; content only a branch of the person's holds, and an
  unread proof, end nothing. `EndKeeping.KeepGoneAsync` then keeps the fact as it retires, so no recovery ref is made. D173's CLEANUP1c
  note has the detail.
- **Verification:** red on CLEANUP1b's branch first, one in `EndJudgementTests` and one in `CleanupGitTests` (squash on the platform,
  pull, delete: ended, clean-up completed, no recovery ref); two guards green before and after (a file still differing reads dropped and
  kept; a commit git collected reads missing with nothing to keep). Then green with the driver's fast half and `CleanupGitTests`,
  `EndJudgementGitTests` and `HeldFactsGitTests` by class under `git.process.runsettings`.

## 2026-10-17 — A landing merged into the line, then deleted, read moved to the line for ever (CLEANUP1b)

- **Symptom:** a landing branch whose pull request was merged with a merge commit and pulled, then deleted by the person before a look
  judged it, read *moved to `main`* in `work state`: not ended, its clean-up pending for ever.
- **Root cause:** CLEANUP1's `WentAsync` asks git which local branch holds the recorded tip once the branch is missing, and the line is
  a local branch, so the line holding the work by ancestry read as a rename. The end judgement never saw it: `EndKeeping` judges only
  a landing whose branch stands, and the judgement called a landing whose branch is not standing unknown.
- **Fix:** a landing git says is missing is judged first through `EndJudgement` at the tip its landing recorded, by the line's ancestry
  alone (`EndSubject.Gone`), and `EndKeeping.KeepGoneAsync` keeps the fact as it retires (`LandedBranches.HoldGone`), so the inventory
  reads it ended with its clean-up completed. Only where no end is kept does `WentAsync` read where the work went. D173's CLEANUP1b
  note has the detail.
- **Verification:** red on CLEANUP1's branch first, one in `EndJudgementTests`, one in `HeldFactsTests` and three in
  `CleanupGitTests`; then green with the driver's fast half and `CleanupGitTests`, `EndJudgementGitTests`, `HeldFactsGitTests` and
  `TidyEffectGitTests` by class under `git.process.runsettings`.

## 2026-10-17 — Work state listed leftovers that could never clear (CLEANUP1)

  end it: the record kept no word of why it went, so git's own "missing" (the person's removal) read the same as a read that failed.
  Recovery refs had no rule but "never deleted", and a recovery no record named was drafted as a unit with an unknown owner.

  `stands`), written by the clean-up and once by the look; the inventory reads a unit whose landings all went as missing, nothing of
  it standing, as dropped and retired, and keeps every doubt, saying which. A recovery ref whose commit a branch or a tag holds goes
  after 30 days in a verified transaction; one nothing else holds is kept and says how to delete it. Recoveries no record names are
  listed apart, not as units. D173's CLEANUP1 note and D102's have the detail.

  milestone's web test in both languages.

  then remove that branch on a squash's record with no recovery, leaving the commit held by nothing: only a tag or a local branch of
  the person's (outside `daoris/`, not a landing's) holds now. (2) A renamed landing branch read as dropped: where another local branch
  holds the recorded tip it reads `moved`, kept and followed; and where no tag or recovery ref holds it, its commit is kept on a
  recovery ref before the record retires. (3) The look's write applied by name, so an observation read before a new landing of the
  same name retired the new one: each write now names the landing read, by identity and tip. (4) A folder moved aside whose purge a
  later write, a link or a failed read blocks was listed as a recovery for ever: past its date it is a unit blocked on the person.
  Red on round 1's branch first, five in `CleanupLeftoversTests` and four in `CleanupGitTests`; D173's and D102's CLEANUP1 notes,
  *After review*, have the detail. The coordinator's re-check closed four more, each red first: a symbolic branch held a recovery ref
  (now no symbolic ref holds, by git's `%(symref)`, in every proof by ancestry too); a moved-to name made again elsewhere was still
  taken for the work, and a rename to `feature/HEAD` read dropped (the branch's commit is kept and compared, and only a remote's `HEAD`

## 2026-10-17 — The HTTP host watched its content root as the connector had (HTTPWATCH1)

- **Symptom:** none seen yet; KNOWWALK1's cause, found in the connector, stood in the other host Daoris builds.
- **Root cause:** `WebApplication.CreateBuilder` in the HTTP host kept the default `appsettings.json` reload watch over its
  content root, which is the project folder in development (`bin/` and `obj/` under it) and the install's `app/` when the
  desktop hosts the service: exactly what an update swaps. The search of the source found no other generic or web host: the
  desktop shell and the driver host build none (the driver's console is a plain process).
- **Fix:** `HostRoot.Builder` takes the content root from `HostRoot.ContentRoot` (the binary's folder when it carries
  `wwwroot`, else the working folder when it does, else the binary's) and passes `--hostBuilder:reloadConfigOnChange=false`
  first among the arguments, so no file is watched and the environment and command line are read as before. The note
  `.claude/knowledge/host-content-root.md` (HOSTROOT1) says it once for the next host. In development the content root is
  still the project folder, which the SDK serves `wwwroot` from; only its watch is gone.
- **Verification:** `HostRootTests` failed first on the unbuilt member; the host's file sources are not reloading and the
  root is the binaries' folder, and the bundle choice is pinned in the three cases. Http service tests 280 to 282.

## 2026-10-17 — Every knowledge connector watched its whole checkout, and walked each folder renamed in it (KNOWWALK1)

- **Symptom:** the deployment rehearsal's swap of `_fixtures/deployment-rehearsal/install/app` was refused `busy`, and
  DEPLOYBUSY1's diagnosis named `bin` held by `16075bf6 (pid 36544)`: a `dotnet` whose image an installer had replaced as it
  ran (the `.rbf` name), running the workspace's knowledge connector build of 10-09, started by `tools/knowledge-server.mjs` on
  10-10 for a session in this checkout. Asked again later, it held the checkout's root and nothing under `_fixtures/`: the hold
  came and went.
- **Root cause:** not the knowledge read. Neither the 10-09 build nor main reads outside the `.claude/` tiers, `docs/` and the
  declared folders, and the 10-09 build had no watcher of its own. The connector's host did: `Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(args)`
  takes the working folder, the session's checkout, for its content root, and its default configuration watches
  `appsettings.json` there for a reload. The framework's `PhysicalFilesWatcher` watches that root with `IncludeSubdirectories`
  set, and its `OnRenamed` lists everything in a renamed folder with `SearchOption.AllDirectories` (read from the IL of the
  running build's own `Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Physical.dll`). So every session's connector (23 processes held the
  checkout's root when asked) heard every write in the checkout, ignored trees too, and walked each folder renamed in it. The
  swap's rename of `app` set each one walking the renamed tree, holding `bin` as the swap's next move came. Two smaller causes
  besides. On main only, EVENT6's recursive watch of `.claude/` reached `.claude/worktrees/`, so each agent's build and install
  marked the reading stale. And, latent, the documents folder's walk (`RepositoryScanner.Records`) entered every folder, so a
  docs site's `docs/node_modules/` would have been walked and its READMEs indexed.
- **Fix:** `KnowledgeServer.HostBuilder` takes the build's own folder for the content root and sets
  `hostBuilder:reloadConfigOnChange` false: no file is watched, and a repository's own `appsettings.json` no longer configures
  the connector. `IgnoredPaths` asks git once (`ls-files -z --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory`, ceilinged at the
  root's parent), which names each ignored folder and not what is in it. `Records` skips what it names, asked at the first
  record of a read. `CheckoutFreshness.OpenTree` watches a folder with an ignored one inside in parts. Where git cannot answer,
  both are as they were. The cost is one git process, 0.1-0.34 s measured in a worktree on this machine under load: once per
  read for the walk and once per process for the watch.
- **Verification:** the members came first and each new test failed before the fix. `ConnectorHostTests`: all four file
  sources were watched. `IgnoredPathsTests.A_read_of_a_checkouts_documents_opens_nothing_under_a_folder_git_ignores`: forty
  ignored package folders under `docs/` and two files held with no sharing; the read threw the sharing violation before the
  fix, and opens neither after it. `CheckoutFreshnessTests.A_write_in_a_folder_git_ignores_inside_a_watched_one_is_not_heard`:
  writes in `.claude/worktrees/` marked stale before the fix. Service tests went from 2197 to 2203. A running connector keeps
  the old host until its session restarts it on a build made after this fix.
- **Followed, 2026-10-19 (KNOWHOLD1):** the same pid 36544, still on the build of 10-09, held `app/cli/node_modules` in two
  later rehearsals; a running session now follows the current build. See that entry.

## 2026-10-17 — The update's swap said `busy` of a two-minute hold and nothing of what held it (DEPLOYBUSY1)

- **Symptom:** twice in a row on main (3a0d0af, 6bd7e0e) the deployment rehearsal's 9e rolled `fails-to-start` back `busy`,
  not `exited`: the move of `app` was refused for its whole 120 s after `app.stopped`, while nothing ran from `app/` (the
  launcher's own check had passed). The 9d swap before it met a 41 s hold that gave way. The journal said which move was held and
  for how long, and nothing of which file or which process.
- **Root cause:** not yet attributed; this entry is the diagnosis half. The launcher counts as *running from `app/`* only a
  process whose image is under it, and any other process holding a handle there (a file open, a folder as its working folder, an
  enumeration under way) refuses the folder's move unseen. Two rehearsals in a worktree with the diagnosis below passed 115/115.
  The first met a 45 s hold in 9d, on `app`'s `bin`, held at the first refusal by a process outside Daoris (a long-running
  `dotnet` of another tool on the machine, named by its image's installer rollback file, `<hex>.rbf`, since an update had
  replaced that image as it ran); the second met no hold at all. No Daoris process was found holding `app/`, and the holds
  come and go with what else runs on the machine, as SWAP2 measured.
- **Fix:** the swap now names what it found held. `HeldFiles` asks Windows which processes hold the folder moved or an entry
  within it (`FileProcessIdsUsingFileInformation`, the Restart Manager's own question, which also answers a folder that is some
  process's working folder: `RmGetList` takes files alone). It is asked at the first refusal, every five seconds after and at the
  give-up, keeping the last answer, since one moment's holder can be a passer-by. Each hold journals `held` (the entry),
  `by` (`name (pid n)`) and `holders` (each with its start and command line, the journal's alone); `busy`'s detail and
  `daoris-driver update` say them, and `update.installed`/`update.rolled-back` carry `held` (its name) and `heldBy`.
- **Verification:** each new test failed first at run time (members added without behaviour), then passed: a file this process
  holds is named with its pid, a held move's journal and detail name both, a hold that gave way keeps its holder, a hold asked
  again names the last holder and not the first (red with the ask made rare), the journal's new fields round-trip and an old
  one reads as before, the terminal's words and the log line's fields. `HeldFilesProcessTests` (Process): a `node` whose working
  folder is `app/` is named as holding `app` itself, and the folder's move is refused. Two deployment rehearsals, 115/115 each.
- **Attributed, 2026-10-17 (KNOWWALK1):** the `dotnet` a rehearsal's hold named by its `.rbf` (`16075bf6`, pid 36544) was
  this checkout's knowledge connector, walking the folder the swap had renamed; see that entry.
## 2026-10-17 — An unread ref forgot its record, and a detached tree's removal verified nothing (RECORDUNREAD1, DETACHTX1)

- **Symptom:** a fifth review of FABRIC-END4a: a session branch whose ref git could not read was forgotten by LAND3's door as
  "gone already", and by each look's and press's clean-up of the record; a landing's branch that did not read was retired as gone;
  and a detached tree whose holder was rewound after its proof was removed, leaving the commit it had out on no ref.
- **Root cause:** each path read a failed read as absence. `rev-parse --verify --quiet` exits 1 on any failure to resolve, a broken
  ref's too, and `for-each-ref` leaves a broken ref out of its list and exits 0, so the door, `ForgetGoneAsync` and
  `JudgeLandedAsync` saw "missing" where git had said nothing of the kind; `merge-base --is-ancestor`'s 128 was read as "not the
  landing's". A detached tree's removal deletes no branch, so no ref transaction verified what its proof rested on.
- **Fix:** absence asked of `show-ref --exists`, exit 2 alone (`ContentHolds.MissingAsync`, the knowledge note `git-ref-absence`);
  anything else keeps the record and says unread, a landing as kind `unknown`. A detached tree's commit kept on a recovery ref
  before the tree goes, dropped only in one transaction verifying what its proof rested on (`DropKeptVerifiedAsync`). D173's
  RECORDUNREAD1 and DETACHTX1 note has the detail.
- **Verification:** red first on END4a's branch, six tests: `UnreadRecordGitTests`' five broken reads and `JudgedDeleteGitTests`'
  detached holder rewound as the tree went; then green, with the driver's fast half and the Git classes that reach the door, the
  clean-up, the tidy and the delete.

## 2026-10-17 — A tidy could rest on a landing's branch alone, a replaced holder or a live name (FABRIC-END4a, fourth review)

  line rewound past that landing; LAND3's squash path cleared a chain's earlier branch on a landing branch made again elsewhere; the

  for a branch nobody judged.

  (`madeAt`), else nothing judged and each standing branch said as not judged (`TidiedBranch.Unjudged`); the carrier asked about the

  seal its step. (2) A step a lost submission had published survived the rebase once this machine had taken it: it synced on its
  own, and its session ran with a held claim. (3) A close sent with a key already used, naming another quest list, answered
  success without closing the rest. (4) A refused close sent again with its key after the hold was released closed.

  same ones; clearing `Evidence` on the replacement cannot fence a verdict arriving after it. (2) The submission's rebase reused
  `ForgetFollowUpsAsync`, written for a lost done, which forgets a step only while its history is its single publication. (3) The
  replay matched the key on any named quest's Done and compared nothing else. (4) Only a success left its key anywhere, on the Done.

  for that one only (`QuestEvidenceVerdict.AskedFor`); `QuestStore.ForgetStepsAsync` forgets a lost submission's unpushed steps
  with what this machine did on them, rewriting a take as a conflict on a quest no push carries; the store keeps every close
  outcome, refusal or success, under its key in `quest_closes` with its token and submissions, answering only the same call with
  it (`KeyReused` otherwise).

  members added without behaviour, then passed. `Daoris.Service.Tests` (2197) and `Daoris.Service.Http.Tests` (280) pass, the

## 2026-10-17 — The due moments could fetch twice, overwrite a completed answer and drop the start's focus (FABRIC-END6c)

  repository that `RepositoryHolds` holds (the replay's lock, a landing) and asks once it is let go; `PullRequestMinute` is the one
  minute of every occasion; an answer is kept only where asked no earlier than the kept one, and a completed one never replaced;
  `StateAnswer.AskedAt` is each request's own time; `RemoteFetches.InGit` reads `FETCH_HEAD` and origin's line's log; `PendingFocus`

  test and three new rows over real git. All then passed, with the driver's and the modules' fast halves and

## 2026-10-17 — A node declaration moved with its caller's collections, and a reach's ports could name another acceptance (FABRIC-NODE1d)

  port was accepted), then passed; the node suites pass, and the driver's fast half.

## 2026-10-17 — An automatic landing could land on stale facts, from a loop that did not hold the home, and wakes were lost (FABRIC-END7's review)

- **Symptom:** a second maker's review, from source, would not stage END7 with auto-landing on. A look chose two due entries. While
  the first one's plugin ran, the second's quest could be held again, or its tree could gain commits that needed another review;
  the second then landed anyway. A `drive --share` loop beside the desktop could land the same due entry. And a quest's release
  heard while a landing ran waited for the whole look.
- **Root cause:**
  - The landing at done is two halves, a look that chooses and a pass beside it that lands. The pass handed `TreeLands` the gate
    the look had read, and `TreeLands` checks a supplied gate's refusal; it does not read it again. Nothing between the two halves
    read the quest, the holds or the tree again.
  - Auto-landing was guarded per process (`RunningSessions`), but the home's lease, which the end keeper checks, was never asked.
  - END7 took each topic's wakes before the tick and emptied their store whatever followed. A failed tick lost them, and so did a
    selection skipped because a landing ran.
- **Fix:**
  - Each choice is judged again just before its own landing, from a fresh world, and its gate is pinned to the tip read there
    (`LandingGate.Tip`). The branch is made or advanced to that commit, or refused where the tree moved past it.
  - Only `HomeLease.HeldHere` selects or launches an automatic landing.
  - A wake is spent only where a selection judged with it: otherwise it goes back, and a running landing's end offers it again.

  D173's FABRIC-END7 note, *After review*, has the detail.
- **Verification:** eight new tests, each red against END7 first, then green:
  - Fast: `AutoLandingLookTests` (2), `LandingWakesTests` (2), `RunningSessionsTests` (1).
  - Git: `AutoLandingTests` (2), `ReviewLandingTests` (1).

  The landing's Git classes (`AutoLandingTests`, `AutoLandingWakesTests`, `ReviewLandingTests`, `OpinionLandingTests`, 37 tests)
  pass once, by class.

  (57); the deployment gate re-run on the fix. The gap that let it through is a row: a light gate builds the launcher.

## 2026-10-16 — A content proof git could not read said the work was held nowhere (PROOF-UNREAD1)

- **Symptom:** none seen on an install; found reading the fabric events design §B7 against the code. `ContentHolds.HeldByContentAsync`
  returned null both for "no branch holds this work" and for "git could not answer", so a missing git, a timeout or a ref git
  could not read looked like the work was held nowhere, a finding the callers worded as one ("holds commits no branch of yours
  holds"), not as a read that was not made.
- **Root cause:** every read in the proof's chain (the line's forms, the tip's tree, each merge base, the changed files, the
  branch list, each holder's comparison) turned a git failure into "continue" or `null`, and `LineFormsAsync` read any failure of
  `rev-parse --verify --quiet` as "no such ref", so a git that never ran left a line with no forms and the proof returned
  before a single comparison. "Absent is never zero" (D57) was not kept.
- **Fix:** the proof returns a `ContentProof`: held (`Hold`), not held (both null) or unread (`Unread`, git's words). Exit 1 of
  `rev-parse --verify --quiet` and of `merge-base` is git's answer (no such ref, no common commit); any other failure marks the
  proof unread unless another read found the work held. `LandedProofs.ReadLineFormsAsync` says what it could not read. Callers:
  the sweep keeps the row unread (as its own git failures already do), the branch tidy's and the tree's unforced removal refuse
  saying git could not tell (and `--force` stays the door), the head's discard offer offers none. `LandedProofs.ProveAsync` had no
  such gap: a failed read ends as `Unknown`, never `OnLine` or `Merged`. A test seam, `WorkingTree.Answered`, scripts git's answer.
- **Verification:** `ContentHoldsUnreadTests` (the driver's fast half): git missing, each git ask failing in turn (tree, commit,
  merge base, diff, log, branch list), a timeout, each reading as unread; no common ancestor and a clean find-nothing reading as
  not held; `ProveAsync` reading unknown. Written with the code, so the red was a build that failed for want of the type.

## 2026-10-16 — Accept named a conversation's branch from the person's opening words (ACCEPTFOOT2)

- **Symptom:** on the installed Daoris, a conversation's *Accept* put its one commit on a branch made from a slug of the
  person's first sentence and the session's id, under a repository whose landing pattern is `feature/<KEY>-<words>`. Nothing in
  the name said what the work was.

  searched it for a ticket and `{slug}` was made of it, as PROCESS1d-ii's note said (*made at Accept from its opening*). The
  opening is the person's chat, worn by the page as the conversation's name only because it has no title (RAIL1).

  sets its name to the oldest commit's subject beyond the line, the subject PROCESS1b-ii already names a squash by where there is
  no title; the opening stays its title and is searched for a ticket after that subject. The plan and the press read it alike
  (`TreeLands.ForWorkAsync`), only under a pattern that reads words, each commit kept by its boundary (`%x1f%s`) so an empty
  oldest message names `work`; an entry is named for its first part's work when its subject is made (`EntryForWorkAsync`), so its
  parts join one branch. A second maker's review found the entry's split, the empty message and the needless read in the first
  build. D164's ACCEPTFOOT2 note.

  none found, no commit read, the oldest subject's boundary, the patterns that read words); `LandingTests`' real-git cases (plan
  and press naming one branch, seen red with the opening's slug; an empty oldest message, seen red naming the next commit) and
  `EntryLandingTests`' (two parts' different oldest commits land on the first's branch, seen red naming the second's).

## 2026-10-16 — A conversation whose turn ended with work offered Accept only in the review's side bar (ACCEPTFOOT1)

  nothing is beyond the line (REVIEWBASE4); the same *Accept…* and press (D56). A second maker's review found the first build
  counting by ancestry alone (work held by content offered), reusing a review read before the turn's last commit, and naming a
  detached tree's branch. D164's ACCEPTFOOT1 note.

  once the turn ends, none while it runs, none with nothing beyond the line or held by content, the review read again for the
  turn that ended and no offer from the turn before's answer) and `DriverModuleTreesTests` (the answer's `offer`), each seen red

## 2026-10-16 — A terminal's discovery would take another install's service (HOMEID1)
## 2026-10-16 — *Send now* could cut the words' own turn, stop a turn with a word on its way, or close a finished call as cut (STEER2a)

- **Symptom:** a second maker reviewed the unmerged branch and found three defects; the coordinator checked each against the
  code. None ran on the install.
  - A stop arriving late could cancel the turn of the very words it was kept for, and that answer was lost.
  - A press on Claude Code's door could send `session/cancel` while an earlier word was on its way.
  - A call that had finished could be closed as `cut`.
- **Root cause:**
  - **The late stop.** `ChatTurns.TakeNowAsync`/`StopKeepingAsync` and `DrivenInbox` decided the stop under their lock but
    sent it after releasing the lock. In that gap the turn could end and the pump or the run could send the kept words as the
    next turn. The inbox also stopped once per press, not once per turn.
  - **The cancel with a word on its way.** The steer's guard `open` failed whenever anything waited, for instance a helper's
    answer. The press then queued the words and stopped the turn even on the next-step door, which D136 point 4 forbids
    while a word is on its way.
  - **The finished call closed as cut.** `AcpSession.Track` treated an update with no status as open.
- **Fix:**
  - **A stop is tied to its turn.** Each turn is counted. A stop is decided for one turn and dropped if that turn has ended.
    The next turn waits until the stop is on the wire or dropped: `PumpAsync` awaits it, and `NextOrClose` hands back a
    `Waits`. The inbox asks a turn to stop once.
  - **The next-step door is never stopped.** That holds while a word is on its way, or wherever the door takes words at
    its next step. Where the agent steers, the press steers past what is ahead: a steer is no stop (D136's STEER2a note).
    Where it cannot steer, the words go behind, answered `now: false` with `why: "behind"`.
  - **A finished call stays finished.** It is kept finished through any update without a status. Only `pending` or
    `in_progress` opens a call, or an announcement with no status, which the protocol reads as `pending`.
- **Verification:**
  - `ChatTurnsTests`: a slow stop holding the kept words' turn until it landed on the turn before; on a door that cannot
    steer, the helper-waiting case and the word-on-its-way case; on one that steers, past both with nothing stopped.
  - `DrivenInboxTests`: one stop per turn; no held word taken while a stop is on its way; past a word on its way, or
    behind it where the agent cannot steer.
  - `AcpSteerTests`: completed, then a statusless update, then a steer, with no cut.
  - Each was seen failing behaviourally once its surface compiled.


- **Symptom:** found by a second agent's review of the terminal RPC plan, checked against the code, not met on the install:
  `daoris-driver` and `daoris` with no `DAORIS_SERVICE_URL` would act on whatever Daoris host answered at the address in
  `<home>/running.json`, whichever home that host served.
- **Root cause:** FINDDAORIS1 took the address where its process lived and `/api/status` named a `tier`, the test the supervisor
  adopts a host by. Every Daoris host answers that: another install's service on the port this home's desktop once held passed,
  as did one a process id reused by the system led to, since the CLI checks the id alone; and the status was asked with
  redirects followed, so an address could send the asker to another host.
- **Fix:** a home has an id, `<home>/home.json` (`HomeIdentity`, three twins); a local host answers it at `/api/status` as
  `home`, `running.json` keeps it, and both discoveries take an address only where the status, asked with redirects off,
  answers this home's id. D171's HOMEID1 note.
- **Verification:** `RunningServiceTests` (red as they could not compile: another home's id, no id, a home with none, a reused
  process id, a redirect between two real loopback listeners), `RunningAddressTests`, the driver's and the service's
  `HomeIdentityTests`, the HTTP tests' `HomeStatusTests` and `PersonDoorHostTests`' status shape; the CLI's `running.test.ts`
  (red on the missing export: another id, none, a reused pid, a redirect between two real `node:http` servers) and
  `home.test.ts`.

## 2026-10-16 — *Bring up to date* counted and replayed commits the line already held (LANDSYNC3)

- **Symptom:** on the install, WSR6's plan said *replays 3 commit(s)* of a session branch whose first commit a pull request had
  squash-merged, and *replays 1* of one whose only commit was; the press replayed those commits again, where they became empty or, with
  the line's changelog changed beside them, conflicted.
- **Root cause:** `BranchJudging.JudgeReplayAsync` cut a branch only by its record (where it grew from) or, with no record, by the walk
  by content, then counted `cut..tip`. A session grown from the line is cut where it leaves the line, so nothing asked whether the line
  held any of its commits since: a one-commit squash matches no content walk once the line changed its file, and a recorded branch never
  walked at all. LANDSYNC1 built the per-commit judgement for the landing alone.
- **Fix:** `LineHolds.JudgeBeyondAsync` reads the commits beyond the cut in one `git log --cherry-mark --right-only` (patch ids and
  files); the walk by content is asked for a recorded branch where the line changed every file its first unheld commit touched. The cut
  moves past held commits it begins with, held ones between are skipped run by run (`BranchReplays.Stretches`), the count is what the
  replay carries. D87's LANDSYNC3 note.
- **Verification:** `LineHeldBeyondTests` (fast: red as they could not compile, green after). `TreeSyncHeldTests` (Process: the
  install's two branches, a squash of several, a skipped cherry-pick) and `TreeSyncStartsTests`' bound are written and owed to the
  serial run.
## 2026-10-16 — A chain's step that merged the line showed its parent's work as its own (REVIEWBASE3)

- **Symptom:** a session grown from its parent's tip (a chain's step) that then merged the line: Review listed the parent's commits'
  files beside the step's own, as the step's work.
- **Root cause:** REVIEWBASE1 chooses the review's base among the line's merge-base and the record's base. Where neither reaches the
  other, `ReviewBase.Newest` takes the line's, so the line's changes are not shown, and the parent's, which the line does not hold, are.
  No single commit in the tree's history excludes both.
- **Fix:** where `merge-base --independent` names both, the diff reads from `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two
  (`ReviewRange.Against`, `Reads`), one git start more in that case only; the answer's `base` is still the line's commit. A conflict
  between them reads from the line's, as before. D164's REVIEWBASE3 note.
- **Verification:** `ReviewBaseChoiceTests`' three `Incomparable` cases (red first, the member missing, then green).
  `ReviewBaseTests.A_chain_step_that_merged_the_line_shows_only_its_own_changes` and
  `A_chain_step_whose_parent_conflicts_with_the_line_reads_from_the_line_as_before` are `Process` rows, owed to the parent's serial run.

## 2026-10-16 — Under a squash rule a part joining its entry's branch was refused as grown apart (ACCEPTALL1d)

- **Symptom:** under a branch rule that squashes (PROCESS1b-ii), an entry's Accept landed its first part as one squashed commit and
  refused every later part that ran alongside: the advance's refusal (`exists`) said its work does not grow from the tip. ACCEPTALL1b's own
  Accept for a part would have refused the same part's later work too, since it now joins the entry's branch.
- **Root cause:** `TreeLands.AdvanceAsync` judged growth from the record's `Squashed` tip whenever the rule squashes. That tip is the
  first part's own session tip, the tree the squash was made from; a later part's work replayed onto the branch (ACCEPTALL1's join, or
  LANDSYNC1's replay past what the line holds) grows from the branch's squash commit, the record's `Tip`, never from it. Whether a
  part joins at all was judged from the branch's tip, which under a squash no session tip descends from, so the same part's own later
  work was replayed too, and refused the same way.
- **Fix:** `LandingAdvance.GrewFrom` answers the recorded tip where a replay was made, and the squashed tip only where the session's own
  tip moves the branch; `BranchAsync` judges joining from the squashed tip under a squash and leaves the commits up to it out of a
  replay, since the branch holds them by content. D87's ACCEPTALL1d note.
- **Verification:** `LandingChainTests.A_replayed_advance_grows_from_the_branchs_tip_under_a_squash_too` (the table: red before the
  function, green after). `EntryLandingTests`' two squash cases (Process) are written and owed to the serial run.
## 2026-10-16 — A word taken back from a driven session could still go to its resumed run (SAIDBACK1e)

- **Symptom:** none met; read by SAIDBACK1d. The person takes back a word waiting on a quest's parked or ended session, the door
  says it was taken back, and the resumed run is still handed it.
- **Root cause:** `DriverContinuations.ContinueAsync` read the record's words and built the resumed prompt (on the native door,
  into the spawn's command line) before `Driver.HoldAsync` spawned the run, and the ledger's move to working came only after the
  spawn. The take-back door refuses a record that runs, so until that move it took words back that the prompt already held.
- **Fix:** the move to working comes first, then the words are read as it left them and the run is spawned (`HoldAsync`'s
  `movedFirst`). A run that never starts puts the record back with its words (`Continuations.PutBack`): an ended record as it
  ended, a park ended as a fallback ends it, its words carried on, never `failed` with them. D137's SAIDBACK1e note.
- **Verification:** `ContinuationTests.A_record_moved_to_working_goes_back_as_it_was_where_no_run_of_it_started` (red first,
  the member missing). `SessionMessagesTickTests.A_word_taken_back_between_the_look_and_the_move_never_goes` and
  `Words_whose_run_could_not_be_spawned_wait_on_the_record_as_it_ended` are `Process` rows, owed to the parent's serial run.

## 2026-10-16 — A withdrawn session request could also be taken, the door saying withdrawn (REQTAKE2)

- **Symptom:** none met; REQTAKE1's mechanics read against `SessionRequests.WithdrawAt`. A terminal verb withdraws a request
  nothing took within its wait and tells the person so ("it was withdrawn"), and a loop could still act on it: a stop, words or a
  take-back the person was told did not reach the session would reach it.
- **Root cause:** the mirror of REQTAKE1. A take's `File.Move` opens the file for `DELETE`, sharing read, write and delete, then
  renames through that handle. A withdrawal's rename landing between the two moved the file to its withdrawn name, the take's
  handle then moved it on from there to the take's name, and the withdrawal's `File.Delete` of its withdrawn name found nothing,
  which `File.Delete` does not report. `WithdrawAt` returned true and the take read and honoured the request.
- **Fix:** after its rename, `WithdrawAt` opens the withdrawn name alone (`FileShare.None`, `DeleteOnClose`): that waits out
  every handle opened before the rename (none can open it after, the name being gone), and removes the file as it closes. Gone
  by then, the take that moved it on has it, and the withdrawal says false, so the verb says the loop took it. Held past a
  second of tries, it is put back for a loop and is not withdrawn. On Linux a rename is by name and whole, so nothing moves it
  on, and the open only waits out a reader. D126's REQTAKE2 note.
- **Verification:** `SessionRequestsTests.A_withdrawal_and_a_take_begun_before_it_never_both_win` holds the file as a rename in
  progress does, withdraws, and lets the rename land from wherever the file then is: it failed first (the withdrawal said
  withdrawn and had already removed the file the rename was moving), then passed. On Linux the rename lands by name, finds
  nothing, and the withdrawal has it, which the test allows.

## 2026-10-16 — A session request taken by two loops at once could be lost unread (REQTAKE1)

- **Symptom:** STATEHUB1e's worker, taking `.told` notes as `SessionRequests.TakeAt` takes a request (rename aside, read,
  remove), lost one note in twenty in `PressesToldTests` when two loops took at once; its read came back empty after its rename
  had succeeded. Requests (stop, say, take-back) used the same take, so a person's stop or words could be dropped silently.
- **Root cause:** on Windows `File.Move` (`MoveFileEx`) opens the file for `DELETE`, sharing read, write and delete, and then
  renames through that handle. When loop B has opened it so and loop A's rename lands first, A's rename succeeds (B shares delete)
  and B's handle follows the file to A's name. While B's handle is open, A's read (`File.ReadAllText`, sharing read only) is
  refused with a sharing violation; `Read` swallowed it as null and `TakeAt` removed what it had moved, unread. B's rename then
  met a file pending deletion, or gone, and returned null too: neither loop honoured the request. The rename itself was never
  the fault; the take's assumption that a rename that succeeded left the file at its name, readable, was.
- **Fix:** `TakeAt` reads what it moved aside until it is not refused (twenty tries, ten milliseconds apart), returns null where
  the file is gone, since the loop whose rename moved it on has it, and removes only what it read. A read still refused after the
  tries puts the file back for the next look (`PutBack`); a newer request for the session in its place replaces it, as `Write`
  does. `Read` and the new `Parse` are split so the take tells a refusal from a file that does not read. D126's REQTAKE1 note.
- **Verification:** `SessionRequestsTests.A_take_whose_read_is_refused_leaves_the_request_for_the_next_look` holds the file as
  a rename in progress does (open for read and write, sharing read, write and delete) and takes it: it failed first, both takes
  null and the folder empty, then passed. `Two_loops_taking_twenty_at_once_honour_each_exactly_once` (two watches on threads of
  their own) passed in three plain runs before the fix, and passes after it: the race did not reproduce on its own here. On Linux, where a
  rename is whole and nothing refuses a read, the first test's take succeeds while held, which the test allows.

## 2026-10-16 — A start cut off inside `git worktree add` left a half tree and its branch for good (OPENCUT1)

- **Symptom:** on the install, 2026-10-15: `trees/<workspace>/<repository>/s-0031408d`, half checked out (staged deletions),
  locked, on a `daoris/s-*` branch no record named, from a start cut off as the old window closed (GOONTREE1's entry); listed
  *(unreadable)* by `trees list`, kept by the look, and removed by hand.
- **Root cause:** `SessionTrees.OpenAsync` deleted the branch only when `worktree add` answered with a failure. A cancel stops
  git's process tree and throws, so nothing after the add ran: the branch git makes first, the folder, and git's own
  `initializing` lock, which git removes only at the add's end, all stayed. A kill leaves the same, and the look kept such a tree:
  locked (AUTOTIDY1's guard), dirty, and a branch that never moved.
- **Fix:** D88's AUTOTIDY2c and OPENCUT1 note. The open holds its tree locked under a reason naming its process until where its
  branch started is recorded, and anything that cuts it off undoes it (`TreeOpenings.UndoAsync`: the tree removed with
  `--force --force`, what is left of the folder it made deleted, its branch deleted). A kill's leftover, locked by git's own reason
  or by an ended process's, is moved aside by the look with its branch (`TreeStrays`).
- **Verification:** `SessionTreesTests`' two OPENCUT1 tests (real git: a cancel once the tree is added, through the git-start
  seam, and one while git still runs, held in a `post-checkout` hook) failed first on the branch left behind and no lock, then
  passed; `BranchTidyingProcessTests.A_tree_whose_opening_a_kill_cut_off_is_moved_aside_with_its_branch` failed first (it did not
  build), then passed. The rest of the `Process` half did not run in the branch.

  keeps them, saying the machine has not answered yet, with nothing put back; the session's queue or record settles them
  (`work/sending.ts`, `SentSettler`), and a chat that ended without them gives them back, said so.

## 2026-10-15 — An accepted session's plan read stale after a tab switch, and never in another window (STATEHUB1b)

- **Symptom:** the owner's, on the install: *"the 采纳 status does not read properly when switching tab"*. After *Accept…*
  (采纳…) the head and the review went on showing the plan from before the press when the view was shown again; a second
  window showed it until the driver's next change.
- **Root cause:** a press refreshed only what its own hook invalidated, in the window that pressed. `useLandSessionTree`
  invalidated the sessions, the review, the hand-off and the clean-up's list after a done landing, never the plan

  read the cached plan. `DRIVER_TICK`, which asks the driver's key again, comes only when the loop saw a change of its own,

  after a successful answer, and `bridge/stateHub.ts`, mounted by `ShellSignals` in both roots, asks every plan again (a
  landing moves the line each plan is judged against) with the rest the route declares, in every window.
- **Verify:** `ShellSignals.test.tsx` (*a landing done in another window reads anew here, shown or mounted again, from the
  event alone*, with the application's fifteen-second freshness) failed with no hub mounted, then passed; `stateHub.test.tsx`;
  `StatePublisherTests` (the declared table, and the event raised only after the route answered). Not seen on the installed
  window from this branch; the terminal's presses and a press in flight are STATEHUB1e and STATEHUB1c.

  `2b751dcf` for them (`message.sent` 06:42:19, `help.room.look` 24.9 s at 06:42:38, `session.started` 06:42:39).

  (24.9 s under load), then the agent spawned: past the bridge's 30 s bound, so the page's opening ahead stopped waiting. The
  send's own `START_HELP` then timed out too; read from the code, not the log, it met a record open whose process was not yet
  held, so it read the whole room again. And the page gave words that did not arrive back to the box they were written in (the new conversation's): once the list
  showed the conversation the driver had opened, the panel drew that one's box instead, so the words sat in a box nobody saw.

  off the request (`RunHelpAsync`, `HelpRoutes.RunPlacedAsync`); a second press is handed the one starting, and words said to it
  meanwhile wait in `HelpStarting` as its queue. The room reads a whole Sessions look under 30 s old (`SessionsLooked`). The page
  keeps words whose send or start timed out, saying the machine has not answered yet, never back in the box to send twice, and
  gives words that never arrived back to the box drawn now (`AskConversation.tsx`'s `box`).

  reading the room itself), `HelpChatTests`' placed tests (Process half, alone), and `AskDaoris.test.tsx`'s three SENDLOST1 tests,

## 2026-10-15 — The window froze for minutes behind a sweep's git starts (UIFREEZE1)

- **Symptom:** the owner's, on the install: *"I think the local daoris is stuck"*. The window did not answer for minutes; the
  machine log's `ui.stalled` was ongoing, 406 s at worst, with no route in `during`, and every route's synchronous part was
  under 20 ms. The Sessions page asks for the clean-up's list routinely, so it came back in daily use.
- **Root cause:** a stack report of the frozen install (`dotnet-stack`) held the window's thread in `Monitor.Enter` inside
  `Process.StartWithCreateProcess`, .NET's one process-start lock, reached from `LinesRoutes.SweepAsync` →
  `LandedCleanups.CleanPlanAsync` → `PullRequestAsks.DueAsksAsync` → `CanonicalLine.ResolveAsync` →
  `WorkingTree.DefaultBranchAsync` → `ChildProcess.RunAsync` → `Process.Start`, resumed there through
  `Control.InvokeMarshaledCallbacks`. Three things met: the bridge dispatches on the window's thread and the kit's pipeline
  keeps the caller's context, so every await in a route came back to the window (the stall watch's own remark, "a route runs
  there until its first wait", was untrue after the wait); `ChildProcess.RunAsync` started each process synchronously on its
  caller's thread; and the clean-up's list asked git for each checkout's line three times (the pull requests' asks, the
  session branches' list, the landed branches' judgement), up to three git processes each. 51 of 76 threads waited on the
  lock behind one slow `CreateProcess` (an antivirus hooks process creation on that machine), and the window waited with them.
  The stall named no route because the route's part on the thread was its continuation, which the middleware never sees.
- **Fix:** `OffTheWindow`, a middleware after `UiStallWatch`, runs a `DAORIS.*` route's call with no synchronization context
  and puts it back before returning, so its awaits go on on the thread pool while its synchronous part is still timed and
  named; the kit's own window modules keep the window's thread. `ProcessStarts` gates every start through `ChildProcess` (and
  `WorkingTree`'s two streaming git readers): four at once, waiting asynchronously, each on the thread pool, so a fan-out
  queues as tasks rather than as parked threads. `TreeContext.OneLook` asks git each checkout's line once per look (the
  list, the press and the sweeps' one path), still reading the person's set line at every call.
- **Verify:** `OffTheWindowTests` (a Daoris route's continuation timed out waiting for the window's pump before the fix, and
  goes on off it after; the kit's own route still resumes on it), `ProcessStartsTests` (forty starts against a held start:
  never more than four inside, none on the calling thread; red with the gate unbounded), `TreeLineLookTests` and
  `SweepLineProcessTests` (the list asked the line 3 times a repository before, once after; the press once; the next look
  asks again). Reasoned from the stack, not reproduced on the owner's machine; the install's `ui.stalled` lines after the
  republish are the field proof.
- **What it left, done (SWEEPFLIGHT1, PROCSTART2, 2026-10-16):** the stack's 22 `SweepPlanAsync` threads were as many lists
  asked at once, so identical `LINES` and `SWEEP_PLAN` asks now join the one under way (`[OneFlight]`, `RouteFlights`; a
  press forgets them as it answers). The starts still made directly (a session's, its going on, a conversation's, a harness
  action's, a usage read's, a plugin's and its trial, the host, Edge, the file manager) now pass `ProcessStarts`. Verify:
  `DriverModuleOneFlightTests` (two asks read the registry twice before, once after; the next ask reads again),
  `RouteFlightsTests`, `ProcessStartsCensusTests` (red with nine files starting directly and three bare folder doors),
  `GatedStartsTests` and `OpenFolderGateTests` (each start seen nowhere, or on the caller's thread, before; off it after).
- **And the terminal's shell (TERMSTART1, 2026-10-16):** `DAORIS.TERMINAL`'s `OPEN` started the shell with the pseudo-console's
  `CreateProcessW`, which no census of .NET's starts saw, in its synchronous part; it now runs that start through the gate's
  `RunAsync`, and a shell whose terminal was ended while it waited there is ended as it starts. The census counts
  `CreateProcessW` too. Verify: `TerminalOpenGateTests` (the start on the caller's thread before, off it after).
- **And the update's relaunch (UPDATERELAUNCH1, 2026-10-16):** *Update now*'s `SET` looked, applied and started the launcher
  synchronously; the look is awaited now and the launcher started through the gate (`UpdateLauncher`), and `App/Program.cs`
  is off the census's list. Verify: `UpdateRelaunchGateTests` (the launcher started on the caller's thread before, off it
  after), the census (red with `Program.cs` off its list before the move).

## 2026-10-15 — The person-door host missed its 15-second stop once under load: not reproduced, its one long wait bounded (FLAKE2)

- **Symptom:** `PersonDoorProcessTests.The_real_host_reads_its_key_from_its_input_gates_by_it_and_still_stops_when_the_input_ends`
  failed once in a merge's service gate under load (2026-10-14, QUEUEEDIT1a's merge): *the host did not stop when its input
  closed* within 15 s. It passed on the rerun, whose log replaced the first, so nothing else of it was kept.
- **What the stop waits on, read from the code:** the input's end, read on a background thread the host starts once it is up
  (`InputEndStop.Watch`), which then asks its lifetime to stop; the lifetime's stop, where Kestrel stops listening and waits
  for the requests in flight up to `HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout`, never set, so the framework's 30 s; the composed service's
  disposal (the index closes once its gate's work in flight ends); the exit. `Process.WaitForExit(int)` waits on the process
  alone, not on its redirected output (.NET 10.0.13, read decompiled), and the test is the only writer of the host's input
  (`Process.Start` duplicates the parent's end uninheritable, under its lock), so the close always reaches the host. In this
  test every request is answered before the input closes, so nothing is in flight and no step waits long. The drain is the one
  wait in the stop that runs past 15 s by design, and past the 5 s the shell waits before it kills the host
  (`HostSupervisor.StopWithin`).
- **Not reproduced:** the test's steps timed in a scratch harness, the host from the tests' own build: input closed to exit in
  42–126 ms over 20 runs beside a CPU load, and 60–647 ms (median 148) over 30 beside that load, two looping builds and the
  service gate. A host whose port another took between `FreePort` and its bind exits by itself within 3 s (E0434352), which
  fails the test at its exit code, not its stop. The class 20 of 20 beside the CPU load before, 20 of 20 with no load after.
- **Fix:** the one long wait bounded, and a missed stop made to say where it sat. A host the shell started
  (`DAORIS_STOP_ON_INPUT_END=1`) waits 3 s for its requests in flight (`InputEndStop.Drain`, `BoundDrain`), under the shell's
  5 s, so the shell's stop ends as a stop rather than a kill; a host started from a terminal keeps the framework's.
  `RealHost.StopByInput` closes the input and, on a miss, says whether the log has `app.stopped` (the stop was asked, or never)
  and the host's last 40 printed lines with their times, its lifetime's `Hosting stopping` and `Hosting stopped` among them
  (the real hosts the tests start log `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` at Debug); both real stop tests read it.
- **Verify:** `InputEndStopTests.A_host_the_shell_started_waits_for_requests_in_flight_less_than_the_shell_waits_for_it` was red
  before `BoundDrain` (it did not compile) and green after; `The_real_host_not_asked_keeps_serving_when_its_input_closes` holds a
  miss's sentence (*never asked*, the input's close, *Application started*). Merged with main, the HTTP host's suite 266 of 266
  and the service suite 2043 of 2043.
- **The trap:** the load beside the runs (a scratch spinner on every core) froze the owner's installed window, and the parent
  stopped it. Reproduce a flake with plain repeated runs of its one class, never with a load generator.
- **Commit:** `e8498d33`.
- **Followed (REALHOSTPORT1, 2026-10-21):** `RealHost.StartAsync` took its host as up once anything answered at its port, so a
  port taken between `FreePort` and the bind could pass another host off as this one. `RealHost.Launch` now mints the host's
  home id under its scratch before it starts, and a start takes the host as up only when `/api/status` names that home; an
  answer naming another is said in the exit's or the timeout's message.
  `StartFailureTests.A_host_whose_port_another_host_answers_is_not_taken_for_up` holds it (a stand-in answering a status over
  another home holds the port).

## 2026-10-15 — A service test's SQLite connection was disposed just after it opened, by another class's pool clearing (FLAKE3)

- **Symptom:** `SearchTests` threw `ObjectDisposedException` once in a merge's service gate under load (2026-10-14, WAITSHOWN1's
  merge), and passed on the rerun.
- **Root cause:** fourteen of the service tests' classes let go of their database files with `SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools()`,
  which clears every pool in the process, and xUnit runs the project's classes in parallel. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite (10.0.12, read
  decompiled) hands a pooled connection out and only then activates it, outside the pool's lock, setting it active before it
  records its owner (`SqliteConnectionInternal.Activate`); in between it reads as leaked (active, owner gone), and every pool's
  `Clear` reclaims leaked connections, disposing their handle. So one class's clear could dispose the connection another class
  had just opened on its own file, and that class's next command met the disposed handle
  (`SafeHandle.DangerousAddRef` under `SqliteCommand.PrepareAndEnumerateStatements`). A probe in scratch, 22 threads each
  opening, writing and closing its own file and then clearing: clearing every pool, 40 and 48 `ObjectDisposedException`s in two
  10-second runs (about one round in 120), each that stack; clearing only its own pool, none in two.
- **Fix:** a test releases its own database alone: `SqlitePools.Release(file)` (the service tests' `Platform`) clears the pool of
  the connection string a store at that path opens with, which `SqliteKnowledgeStore.ConnectionString` now gives both, and the
  tests' raw connections to such files open with `Pooling=False`, as the suite's other raw connections already did, so they
  need no clearing. No other class opens a test's file, so no release reaches a connection being opened. Per database rather
  than a collection serializing the classes that clear: the victim is any class opening a pooled file connection while a clear
  runs, not only a clearing class, so a collection would have had to hold every such class too, and would have run them one at
  a time. `SqlitePoolsTests.No_test_here_clears_every_pool_in_the_process` holds the class by a source scan. The HTTP host's
  tests keep `ClearAllPools`: that assembly runs one test at a time (`DisableTestParallelization`).
- **Verify:** `SqlitePoolsTests`' two release cases were red before `SqlitePools` existed (they did not compile) and green after;
  its source scan failed naming the fourteen files and passed once each released its own database. The service suite: 20 of
  20 before with no load and 20 of 20 before beside a CPU load, 20 of 20 after beside the same load (2037, then 2040 tests):
  the window is too narrow for the suite to show in 40 runs, which is why the probe is the proof. Merged with main, 2043 of
  2043, and the HTTP host's suite 266 of 266.
- **Commit:** `ef852e2c`.
